title: Accession
text: Accession { top} Overview Purpose. Accession is where a specimen becomes a case. You enter (or import) the patient and order details, describe each specimen, and submit. PathScribe then gives the case its accession number, creates a grossing worksheet for each specimen, proposes a grossing template for each one, sets up the first block and stain orders, and offers labels to print. Intended users. Accessioners and laboratory managers. Saving a case needs a permission of its own: if Submit Accession is greyed out when everything is filled in, your role does not allow it; ask your manager. Where it fits. Before Accession, a specimen arrives at the bench or in the lockbox (Lockbox Drop Off), and an order may already be waiting. After Accession, the case goes to Grossing and appears on the Worklist. note "What is demonstration data today" The waiting orders, patient index, facilities, physicians and specimen dictionary you see come from demonstration data. The grossing template suggestion is made by PathScribe's AI assistant when it is configured; if it is not, every specimen keeps the default template and the screen says so. Sending the new order to your laboratory information system depends on that connection being set up. If it is not delivered you are told with a message after the case is saved. Screen Tour The screen is titled Accession ("Log a new Orchestration case and assign Grossing Templates per specimen"). It has two tabs, Case & Patient and Specimens . A third tab, Outside Patient Data , appears only for an outside or contract case. Field definitions Import from Order (top of Case & Patient) Field What it means Import from Order (n pending) Optional A search box over orders already waiting. Search by order number, MRN, patient name, date of birth or facility code. Type at least two characters. "No matching order? Skip this and enter the case details directly below." Advanced Search Opens Order Lookup & Patient Verification , which searches waiting orders and this laboratory's known patients side by side. Patient Origin / Intake Type Choice What it means Standard / EMR Order The usual case. Temporary / Downtime For an unidentified patient or a registration outage. Shows a warning that the identity must be reconciled later, and a Downtime Reason list. Outside / Contract Case External billing and report distribution. Adds the Outside Patient Data tab. Patient Field What it means Given Name(s), Family Name(s) Required. Preferred Name (optional) Shown in brackets in the summary if it differs. Prefix (optional), Suffix (optional) Title and suffix lists. Date of Birth Required. Sex at birth Female, Male, Indeterminate or Not known. Starts blank (a dash) and must be chosen before the case can be accessioned. Patient ID The medical record number. Whether it is required is set by your laboratory. The placeholder text shows the expected format for the chosen facility. If you leave it blank and it is optional, PathScribe makes one. A small coloured dot beside the label shows whether the ID format is recognised (after a facility is chosen). National identifier and registry choices Appear for facilities in some countries. They record a national number and any opt out from screening or cancer registry. Priority The case priority list set by your laboratory. Starts as Routine. Encounter Item What it means Checking for active encounters... PathScribe is looking for a current visit for the patient ID you typed. Auto filled from Encounter n One active visit was found and applied. Select Change / Unlink Encounter to undo. Select Encounter (n active) Several were found. Choose the correct one, or "Create without encounter link (Manual Entry)". Order details Field What it means Submitting Facility Required. The ordering facility. Technical component performed by Shown only for outside material or consultations. Choose a lab only when another lab did the processing, cutting and staining and this lab reads the case. "None (same lab)" otherwise. Location (Ward / Room / Bed) Optional unless your laboratory requires it. Choose a facility first. Origin Hospital / Organisation, Site / Facility Show where the case belongs. The site list appears when your organisation has more than one site. Requesting Provider Required. Search staff or type a name. Unverified physicians are marked "unverified". Assign to Pathologist (optional) Leave as "Unassigned leave for triage" to let triage decide. Clinical Indication The reason for the specimen. Your laboratory may require it. It also helps PathScribe propose grossing templates. Check for Existing Patient (optional) Search for a patient already known under another name (for example a name change). This is the same patient links the new case to that person without merging the two records. ICD 10 Diagnosis Code(s) Search by code or description and add as many as you need. Case Comment (optional) A general note about the whole case. Case Level Deficiencies (optional) Flag a problem with the whole case, such as missing requisition paperwork. Cytology (shown when a specimen is gynaecological or non gynaecological cytology) Field What it means Patient Detail tab Last Menstrual Period, Hormonal Status, Reason for Study, Prior HPV Result, IUD / Contraception Use, "Persistent contact bleeding observed during specimen collection" and Prior cervical procedure. Each has "not specified" or "Not recorded" as a choice. Clinical History tab Structured history entries by category, for the whole case or for one specimen. Autopsy (shown when a specimen is an autopsy specimen) Field What it means Jurisdiction, Case Authority Required. Medicolegal / Forensic or Hospital Consented. Authority Type, Verbal Order Received At, Verbal Order Received From For a medicolegal case. Consenting Relative Name, Relationship Optional, for a hospital consented case. Specimens tab (one block per specimen, labelled A, B, C...) Field What it means Specimen A Dictionary Entry Opens the specimen picker. Choose

title: Add-On Orders
text: Add On Orders { top} Overview Purpose. Add On Orders is where a pathologist orders more work on a case that already exists: deeper levels or recuts of a block, special stains, immunostains (single stains or a panel of them), and molecular or send out tests. You open the case, tick the blocks, build a cart of order lines, choose the priority and the type of slide, and submit. The screen then follows each order through the laboratory and is where you answer the bench if a block has run out of tissue. Intended users. Pathologists, fellows and residents. These roles have the screen and the permission to place orders by default. A person without the permission to place orders can open the screen and read the tracking list, but Submit Add On Order is greyed out for them. Where it fits. There is no Home tile. The usual way in is the Add on order button in the block row of the report screen's header, which opens this screen with that case already loaded. Each slide you order appears as a Pending slide on its block at the Microtomy Workstation, where the technologist cuts, labels and prints it. Finished slides are routed at the Slide Distribution Station. A molecular test run in the laboratory goes to the molecular order queue (see Order Queue); a test that is sent out goes to the reference laboratory you choose. Screen Tour The page is titled Add On Order Builder . If you arrive without a case, it shows only a search box: "Search or scan an accession number…" and an Open Case button. Back at that point returns to Home. Once a case is open, Back closes the case and returns to the search box. A bar across the top shows the accession, the patient name, "Case status: …" and "Primary pathologist: …" (the pathologist's name; if the case holds something that is not a known user, it is shown as stored). If PathScribe cannot work out which laboratory performs the work, the bar adds "No performing lab could be resolved for this case — routing will show all matching stations, not scoped to one lab." Below are three panels side by side, and the Order Tracking list underneath. Field definitions Left panel: Block & Tissue Context Field What it means Specimen heading The specimen letter and description. Block row A tick box, the block label (for example A1), and a note such as "3 level(s) already cut", with Tiny Tissue and Fragile if those flags are set. The count includes every slide already on the block. Exhausted, Lost, Damaged, Cancelled A badge on a block that cannot be ordered from. Its tick box is greyed out. Center panel: Add On Order Builder Field What it means Order kind Four buttons: Recut / Deep Level , Special Stain , IHC , Molecular / Send Out . IHC Panel With IHC chosen: Breast Panel (ER/PR/HER2/Ki 67), Lynch/MMR Panel (MLH1/MSH2/MSH6/PMS2) and Renal IF Panel (IgG/IgA/IgM/C3/C1q/Kappa/Lambda). Choosing a panel adds one line for each stain of the panel. Search stains… Narrows the stain buttons by name. Stain buttons The stains offered for the kind chosen (the first 24 that match). A recut can use any stain; the others show only stains of their kind. "No matching stains." if none. Level Depth (µm) Recut only. Starts at 4. Required only if your organisation requires it. Control Pairing Appears for a stain that needs a control, or when a panel is chosen: No Control , On Slide Control , Separate Control Slide . Right panel: Order Summary & Routing Field What it means Blocks selected How many blocks are ticked. The cart is ordered on every ticked block. Cart lines The stain name, a panel tag, the depth ("4 µm levels"), the control choice, and where it goes ("Routes to:" the benches that can do it, or "No matching station configured for this lab yet — order still routes to the queue."). Remove takes a line out. Molecular line Where a laboratory can run the test itself, a choice between in house and sent out; if not, "Sent out (this lab doesn’t run this test in house)." In house: "Goes to the Molecular Workcenter’s Order Queue." Sent out: Reference / Send Out Lab with a list of labs; "Only the labs approved for this test are listed." or "No labs are linked to this test yet, so every reference lab is listed." Priority STAT / Urgent , Routine Sign Out (the start), Research / Protocol . Slide Media & Charge Standard Charged (the start), Uncharged , Plus Glass . Microtome Bench Instructions Free text for the technologist. Optional unless your organisation requires it. Submit Add On Order Places the order. Some fields can be required by your organisation (a red star). A line beginning "Still required" names what is missing, and the button stays grey. By default the blocks, at least one order line, and the reference laboratory of a sent out test are required. Order Tracking (below the panels; one row for each order placed on this case through this screen, plus any slide on the case that has an open exception, even if it was not ordered here, such as an original H&E that a technologist flagged as exhausted) Field What it means Block and stain For example "A1 — ER", with the panel tag. Stage badge Requested, Block Retrieved, Cut / Pending Stain, Stained / QC, Checked Out / Scanned, Exception or Cancelled. Details "Ordered by …", the priority, the queue it was routed to, and "Send out: …". Prompts and messages Text Where and what it means This case has no specimens. Shown in the block list when the case has no specimens, so there is nothing to order on. No blocks on this specimen. Shown under a specimen that has no blocks yet. {{count}} block(s) selected In the order summary, how many blocks are ticked. The number replaces the braces. No order lines added yet. Shown in the cart until you add a line. Submit stays grey. Select a reference lab… The first choice in the list for a sent out line. Choose the laboratory that will run the test. Toolbar Button What it does Open Case Opens the case for the accession typed or scanned in the search box. Add to Cart Adds the chosen stain (or panel) to the cart. Remove Takes

title: Audit Log
headings: Map Patient and Review Interface Exception windows
text: Audit Log { top} Overview Purpose. The Audit Log screen (the title on the screen is System Logs ) is the laboratory's record of what happened: what people, the system and the AI did, which errors occurred, what the interfaces sent and received, the permanent quality assurance record, billing and charge failures, critical result notifications, outside consult links, and the background jobs of the PathScribe server. You read it, search it, and download parts of it as spreadsheets for an inspection or a review. This article is written for the person who reads the record. Setting up who may see it is in the Administrator Guide. Intended users. Laboratory managers, quality staff and the laboratory director. By default the roles Admin, Lab Director and QA Reviewer can open the screen. A Pathologist cannot open it unless the laboratory has granted it. If the System Logs tile is missing from Home, or you see "You don't have access to this screen", ask your laboratory manager. Where it fits. The screen shows only what has already happened. Nothing is set up here. Work that creates the entries happens on the other screens: sign in, accessioning, grossing, reporting, quality work. You come here afterwards to answer "who did this and when", to clear errors and failed messages, and to prepare evidence for CAP or another inspector. note "Read only, with a few actions" Almost everything on this screen is for reading. The actions are: Resolve on an error, Review on an interface exception, resending a failed interface message or print job, Revoke on a consult link, Requeue on a failed server job, and the Export CSV buttons. Screen Tour At the top are the title, the line "Complete record of AI actions, user changes, system events, errors, and quality assurance activity", and the row of tabs. Below the tabs is a box for finding a support reference. The rest of the screen is the tab you chose, and a footer. Field definitions Tabs Tab What it records Audit Log Every audit entry you are allowed to see: AI actions, user actions and system actions. Error Log Errors, warnings and information messages raised by the system, each marked Open or Resolved. A number on the tab counts the open ones. Interface Log Messages between PathScribe and other systems. Five sub tabs (see below). A number on the tab counts interface exceptions waiting for review. Quality Assurance The permanent, searchable record of quality work, in eight groups. A number on the tab counts open deficiencies. Financial Billing logs and failed charge messages. Critical Alerts Every automated critical result notification and what became of it. Consult links Every link given to an outside consultant, with its status. Server jobs The background jobs of the PathScribe server. This tab appears only for people who hold the permission to see it. Audit Log tab Field What it means All, AI, User, System Filter buttons by type of entry, each with a count. AI is what the AI did, User is what a person did, System is what the system did by itself. Patient Management Only A tick box. Shows only patient merge, move, link, rebind and demographic update events. It combines with the other filters. All Users A list of users. It appears only in a Superadmin session (ForMedrixAI support). Everyone else finds a person by typing their name in the search box. Date range Today, Last 7 Days, Last 30 Days, Last 90 Days or Custom Range. Custom Range shows a from date and a to date; the to date includes the whole day. The screen opens on Last 7 Days . Search "Search event, detail, case ID". Matches the event name, the detail text, the user and the accession number, ignoring capital letters. Timestamp When the entry was written. Type AI, User or System. Event The name of the event, with a small "Support ref" chip you can click to copy the support reference. Detail A sentence describing what happened. It is written in English in every language, and contains no patient name, date of birth, MRN or clinical value. User The person or system actor. Automatic actions show a system actor. Case The accession number when the entry concerns a case. Click it to open the case report. Footer count "Showing N of M events": the entries your filters leave, out of all the entries you may see. Error Log tab Field What it means All, Error, Warning, Info Filter by severity, each with a count. All Status, Open Only, Resolved Only Filter by whether the error has been dealt with. Search "Search message, code, source". Columns Timestamp, Severity, Code, Message, Source, Case, Status. Status Open, or Resolved. Hover over Resolved to see "Resolved by (name), (time)". Interface Log tab, sub tabs Sub tab What it shows Interface Exceptions Inbound messages PathScribe could not safely match to a patient or case. Filter by All, Pending, Resolved or Dismissed; search by event type or reason. Columns: Timestamp, Event Type, Reason, Source Patient, Target Patient, Status. Outbound Interface DLQ Outbound messages that failed or are waiting, in eight queues (patient updates, results, accession events and others). Choose the queue; each failed row shows its error and retries, with Retry Dispatch and Capture as CAPA . Outbound Dispatches A history of the order creation messages PathScribe sent, with the outcome: Delivered, Failed or Outcome unknown. Click a row to see the exact message that was sent and Copy Payload . Print Queue Queued, held, failed and completed print jobs, with Hold, Release, Cancel, Retry and Redirect, singly or in bulk, and Run Batch Now for grouping jobs. A line above the list reads "Site agents — online: n, need attention: n, offline: n." with an Open site agents link to the place where an administrator manages them. It appears only when a site agent has been set up for a site you may see. Engines The health of each hospital's interface engine: status, last check in, free disk, certificate expiry, and each channel with what is waiting. Shown only to people who hold the permission to see engin

title: Autopsy Authorization and Body Release
text: Autopsy Authorization and Body Release { top} Overview Purpose. An autopsy case can be opened before its legal authority is complete. This article covers the two windows on the report screen that finish an autopsy case at either end: Complete Authorization , where the written order or the family's consent is entered so that gross examination can go ahead, and Release Body , where you record where the body went once the preliminary diagnosis is signed. Intended users. Pathologists, pathology assistants and the laboratory staff who handle autopsy paperwork. The release needs a specific permission, so the button is greyed out for roles without it. Where it fits. The case is started on Accession as a temporary accession. Both windows open from the case's report screen. The turnaround figures for the same cases are on the Autopsy Dashboards. Screen Tour Neither window has a menu entry of its own. A banner on the report screen opens each one, so this article has no address of its own and is reached from the links in related articles. Field definitions Complete Authorization window The window is titled Complete Authorization . Its introduction says to enter the written authorization once it arrives, and that gross examination stays blocked until it is on file. A Temporary Accession badge shows while the case is still blocked. What follows depends on how the autopsy was authorized. Field What it means Already on File A heading above what was recorded at intake: for a legal (medicolegal) case, who gave the verbal order and when; for a hospital consented case, the family point of contact and their relationship. Written Order Legal cases only. The heading above the two fields below. Order Reference The reference number of the written order, for example a coroner's order or form number. Order Date The date on the written order. Consent Grant Hospital consented cases only. The heading above the consent fields. Consent Given At The date and time the family gave consent. Consent Scope What the consent covers, typed as words, for example "full" or "no organ retention", separated by commas. Excluded Organs Organs the consent leaves out of examination or retention, the hint in the box reads "e.g. brain, heart (comma separated)". Terms the system does not recognise are ignored. Optional. Retention of tissue/organs is permitted A tick box, ticked at first. Clear it when the family did not agree to keep tissue or organs. A red star marks any field your organisation requires. A line beginning "Still required" lists what is missing, and Save Authorization stays grey until it is complete. A second badge below the fields previews the result: Temporary Accession with the note that gross examination cannot begin until full authorization is on file, or Fully Authorized with a note that saving will allow gross examination to proceed. Release Body window Field What it means Released To Who received the body. The hint reads "e.g. Smith Family Funeral Home". Released By The staff member who handed it over. The hint reads "e.g. Tech: M. Davis". The window is titled Release Body , with the line "Record where the body is being released to. This becomes part of the specimen's own permanent location history." If the case is not ready, the window lists the reasons instead of the fields: release needs a signed Preliminary Anatomical Diagnosis (the final report is not required), and it is blocked while an ancillary hold is active. Toolbar Button What it does Complete authorization On the amber report screen banner "Autopsy: temporary accession, written authorization pending". Opens the Complete Authorization window. Another button beside it lets a person with the override permission continue with a recorded reason. Save Authorization Saves the authorization on the case and closes the window. A message reads "Authorization recorded". Grey until the required fields are complete. Release Body On the banner "Autopsy — Ready for Body Release", which appears once the preliminary diagnosis is signed and no hold is active. Opens the Release Body window. Confirm Release Records the release and closes the window. A message reads "Body released". It shows "Releasing…" while it works, and is grey until both fields are filled or when you lack the release permission. Icons and status indicators Indicator Meaning Temporary Accession Authority is not complete. Gross examination is blocked. Fully Authorized The order or consent is on file. Autopsy — Ready for Body Release The preliminary diagnosis is signed and nothing is holding the case. Hotkeys Key Spoken phrase Action Ctrl+Alt+Shift+3 "record authorization" Saves the authorization while the window is open, with the same checks as the button. Ctrl+Alt+Shift+4 "release body" Confirms the release while the window is open, with the same checks. Step by Step Procedures Standard workflow 1. Open the autopsy case's report screen. If the banner reads "Autopsy: temporary accession, written authorization pending", select Complete authorization . 2. For a legal case, type the Order Reference and choose the Order Date . For a hospital consented case, enter Consent Given At and Consent Scope , list any Excluded Organs , and clear Retention of tissue/organs is permitted if retention was refused. 3. Check that the badge below reads Fully Authorized , then select Save Authorization . The window closes and gross examination can proceed. 4. After the preliminary diagnosis is signed, the banner "Autopsy — Ready for Body Release" appears. Select Release Body . 5. Type Released To , for example "Smith Family Funeral Home", and Released By , for example "Tech: M. Davis". Select Confirm Release . The banner disappears and the release joins the body's location history. Alternative workflow 1. Use the keys or spoken phrases in the Hotkeys table instead of the buttons. Exception handling 1. The authorization has not arrived. Leave the case as a temporary accession. Do not enter an order reference you do not have;

title: Autopsy Dashboards
headings: Case Timeline on an autopsy case
text: Autopsy Dashboards { top} Overview Purpose. The Autopsy Dashboards screen shows how the autopsy service is performing. It answers four questions at three levels: are the preliminary (PAD) and final (FAD) anatomic diagnosis reports being signed on time, what is the state of consent, how much tissue is being kept (organ retention), and what are the causes of death. The three levels are Case (one autopsy against its targets), Department (one facility, with the reports overdue right now) and Enterprise (every facility and jurisdiction side by side). Intended users. Laboratory directors, quality reviewers, administrators and anyone your laboratory has given the "Open Autopsy Dashboards" permission. The screen is for oversight. It does not change a case, sign a report or send a reminder. Where it fits. Open it from Home, then Quality & Compliance , then the Autopsy Dashboards tile. The cases themselves are worked in the Worklist and the report screen. The screen reads those cases and the turnaround targets your laboratory has set, and works out the figures every time you open it. note "Demonstration data today" Simulated cases are switched on by default. They give a demonstration site enough volume for a percentage to mean something. They carry ids beginning SIM A , their facility names end in "(Simulated)", and a banner says how many are included. They are not real patients, and nothing about them is written to the audit log. Tick off Include Simulated cases to see only real cases. Real autopsy cases have no recorded cause of death yet, so they are counted as "Not recorded" (see Field definitions). The figures come from the cases held in this browser session in the demonstration build; the reporting store for a live installation is not built yet. Screen Tour At the top are the title and a one line description, then three controls: the level tabs, the Period choice and the Include Simulated cases tick box. Under them, a level specific picker (for Case and Department), the four panels, and then, for Department and Enterprise, an extra table. Field definitions Controls Field What it means Case / Department / Enterprise (tabs) The level of the dashboard. It opens on Enterprise. Period Last 30 days , Last 90 days (the default), Last 12 months or All time . A case belongs to the period by the date the body arrived, not by the date a report was signed. Include Simulated cases On by default. Adds the demonstration cases to every figure. Case (picker, Case level) Lists the cases in the period, newest arrival first. It opens on the most recent. Simulated cases show "Simulated" after the id. Department (picker, Department level) Lists the facilities that have cases in the period, in alphabetical order. It opens on the first. Case detail (Case level only) Field What it means Facility The facility the case belongs to. Authority Hospital (consented) or Statutory / judicial (for example a coroner's or forensic case). Body arrived The date and time the clock started (see "How the turnaround clock works" below). Preliminary (PAD) / Final (FAD) A coloured badge, then "X h of Y h": hours used so far against the whole window. If the case spent time on ancillary hold (for example waiting for toxicology), "N h on hold not counted" is added. Turnaround panel (one block for Preliminary (PAD) and one for Final (FAD) ) Field What it means "N% within target" Of the reports that are decided, the share signed inside the target. A report is decided once it is signed (on time or late) or has gone overdue unsigned. It reads "No reports decided yet" when there are none. "X of Y decided" X reports were signed on time out of Y decided. "N open" Reports not yet signed and not yet overdue (badges On track and Due soon ). "N overdue" Reports not signed and past their deadline. Shown in red when above zero. "median N h" The middle value of the hours taken, for reports that were signed (on time or late). With an even number of reports it is the average of the two middle values, rounded. Hold time is removed. It is left out when no report is signed. Consent panel. A bar and a count for each of Consent in force , Narrowed , Consent revoked and Not applicable (statutory) . Statutory or judicial cases are always counted as not applicable. A hospital case with no consent record counts as in force. Organ retention panel. A bar and a count for No tier recorded , Tier 0: none kept , Tier 1: diagnostic tissue only , Tier 2: full organs and Tier 3: education, research, genomic . Cause of death panel. One bar per broad category (Cardiovascular, Respiratory, Infection, Neoplasm, Neurological, External causes, Undetermined, Not recorded), largest first. A note explains that a case without a recorded cause is counted as not recorded, and that a live case holds its cause in the signed report text. For the consent, retention and cause bars, the bar length is the count divided by the number of cases at that level, so the bars show shares of the whole. Reports overdue now (Department level only) Field What it means Case id and "PAD overdue by N h" The report the case is working towards that is past its deadline, longest overdue first. "Nothing is overdue." appears when the list is empty. By facility and By jurisdiction (Enterprise level only) Column What it means Cases Cases in the period for that facility or jurisdiction. PAD in target / FAD in target The "within target" percentage described above, or a dash when nothing is decided yet. Overdue now Cases whose PAD or FAD is overdue. Red when above zero. Consent revoked Cases whose hospital consent has been revoked. The tables list the largest group first. How the figures are worded The numbers replace the braces in these lines. Line What it means median {{hours}} h On the panels: the middle time in hours for signed reports. {{within}} of {{decided}} decided On the panels: how many of the decided reports met the target. {{tier}} overdue by {{hours}} h In the Department list of overdue reports: PAD

title: Waste Tracking Report
text: Waste Tracking Report { top} Overview Purpose. The Waste Tracking Report is a read only record of everything that has already been disposed of: specimens, blocks, slides, decants and matrix blocks and slides. You can narrow it by facility, material type and date, and export it as a spreadsheet file for an inspection or audit. It reports the past; it never disposes of anything. Intended users. Laboratory managers, quality staff and the bench roles that have Batch Management. Viewing needs only the Batch Management screen. Exporting needs a separate permission, checked for the facility you are reporting on. Where it fits. Every successful scan on the Disposal Queue adds a row here. The report is the mirror image of that queue: the queue lists what may be disposed of, and this report lists what was. Screen Tour The page title is Waste Tracking Report . The subtitle reads: "A real, computed report of every specimen, block, slide, decant, and matrix block/slide that has genuinely been disposed — filterable by facility, material type, and disposal date, and exportable for regulatory audit." Under the title are four count cards, the filter row and the table. Field definitions Count cards Card What it means Total Disposed The number of rows that match the filters. Tissue Block How many of those are blocks (cassettes included). Slide How many are slides. Wet Tissue How many are specimens or decanted portions. Filters Filter What it means Filter by facility All Facilities or one facility. If this computer has a scan station, the report opens already filtered to that station's facility. Filter by material type All Material Types , Tissue Block, Slide or Wet Tissue. From date, to, To date An inclusive date range on the day of disposal. Leave either end empty for no limit. The report recomputes whenever you change a filter. Table columns Column What it means Disposed The date and time of disposal, in your language's format. Type Tissue Block, Slide or Wet Tissue. Item ID The identifier on the item's label. Case The case accession number. Specimen The specimen letter. A matrix block shows each specimen it holds, separated by commas. Disposed By The name of the person who scanned it. If the account can no longer be found, the stored user identifier is shown; if none, a dash. Location The item's last known location, or "Unknown". This is the location event with the latest time, the same rule the Disposal Queue and the disposal scan use. Rows are listed newest first. Toolbar Button What it does Export Downloads the rows currently shown as a spreadsheet (CSV) file named waste tracking report (date). Greyed out when there are no rows. The exported columns are Disposed At, Material Type, Item ID, Case Accession, Specimen, Disposed By and Location. The export records itself in the audit log. Icons and status indicators Indicator Meaning Computing the real, current report... The report is being worked out. Nothing has been disposed yet matching these filters. No rows. Change or clear the filters. You don't have permission to export the disposal report. Shown if your role cannot export for the chosen facility. The Export button looks dimmed with a tooltip naming the permission. Hotkeys None. Step by Step Procedures Standard workflow 1. Open Batch Management and select the Waste Tracking Report tile. The report opens with the totals and the table. If your computer has a scan station, the facility filter is already set to its facility. 2. Choose the facility and material type you need, or leave them on All. 3. Enter the From date and To date for the period. 4. Read the count cards and the table. The cards update with the filters. 5. To keep a copy, select Export . A file downloads with the rows you see. Alternative workflow 1. For an audit of one facility, choose it in the facility filter and export, then repeat for the next facility. 2. For a monthly record, set From date to the first of the month and To date to the last. 3. To prove a single item was disposed of, filter by a narrow date and look up its identifier in the Item ID column. Exception handling 1. An item you disposed of is not listed. Check the facility filter. The facility is taken from the item's last known location, so an item with no location history appears only under All Facilities. 2. The facility filter hides everything. Choose All Facilities. 3. Export is dimmed. Your role cannot export for that facility. Ask your laboratory manager. Choosing a facility you work in may help. 4. A date range returns nothing. Check that From is not after To. Error recovery 1. "You don't have permission to export the disposal report." Choose a facility you are permitted for, or ask your laboratory manager to grant the permission. 2. The file opens with odd characters in a spreadsheet. Import it as UTF 8 text. 3. The numbers differ from yesterday's export. New disposals have been added, or the filter was different. Check the dates and facility. warning "Reports contain case identifiers" The table and the export contain case accession numbers. Store exported files where your laboratory keeps controlled records, and do not send them by ordinary email. Tips and Best Practices Common mistakes Reading the facility filter as the place of disposal. It is the item's last recorded location. Forgetting the report opens already filtered to your station's facility. Exporting before setting the dates, producing a very large file. Expecting the report to show items waiting for disposal. That is the Disposal Queue. Efficiency recommendations Set the dates first, then the facility, then export once. Use the count cards for a quick total before opening the file. Workflow recommendations Export at regular intervals and keep the files with your accreditation documents. Compare totals with the Disposal Queue after a large disposal run to confirm the work is recorded. Ask quality staff to review "Disposed By" for unusual patterns.
