title: Disposal Queue
text: Disposal Queue { top} Overview Purpose. The Disposal Queue lists the specimens, blocks and slides that may be thrown away today, and lets you record the disposal by scanning the physical item. Before it accepts a scan, PathScribe re checks that the item is really allowed to go. Anything that is not is refused at once with a full screen red warning, so the wrong block is not discarded. Intended users. Staff who handle retained material: histotechnologists, cytotechnologists, molecular technologists and laboratory managers. Scanning to dispose needs its own permission, which the bench roles have by default. Where it fits. Material enters this list when the case has been signed out and the retention period for that kind of material has ended, and no retention hold is active on the case. Placing a hold on the case removes its material from the list. What is disposed here appears in the Waste Tracking Report. warning "Disposal cannot be undone" A successful scan marks the item as disposed on the case, with your name and the time. There is no undo on this screen. Scan only the item you hold in your hand, and put it in the waste stream straight after the green confirmation. note "Retention periods" How long each kind of material is kept comes from your laboratory's retention policy and jurisdiction, set by your administrator. In this version some of the supplied retention figures are placeholders that your records or compliance lead must confirm before relying on them. Ask your laboratory manager which policy is active. Screen Tour The page title is Disposal Queue . The subtitle reads: "A real, computed list of blocks and slides that genuinely qualify for disposal right now — retention period elapsed, no active hold, not already disposed. Scan a physical item's own barcode to dispose it; anything that doesn't match gets rejected immediately, on screen." After it comes either "Scoped to (facility)." or "No scan station set — showing all locations. Set a station for a location scoped queue." Under that is the line "Scan a cassette or slide barcode to dispose it. Hands free — no need to click into a field first." You do not click anywhere before scanning. Field definitions Field What it means Qualifying for Disposal (n) The number of items that may be disposed of now. Item identifier The identifier on the item's label. Type Tissue Block , Slide or Wet Tissue (a specimen or a decanted portion). Cassettes are shown as Tissue Block. Specimen / Eligible since / location For example "A · Eligible since 12 Mar 2026 · Histology Store". The last part is the item's last known location and is left out if none was recorded. A block shared by several specimens (a matrix block) shows "A, B (shared)" so you can see that more than one specimen is affected. Which items appear: The case must be signed out. The retention clock starts at sign out. The retention period for that kind of material, and for the specimen type, must have ended. When specimens of different types share a block, the longest period applies. The case must have no active retention hold. The item must not be disposed of already. If a scan station is set, the item's last known location must belong to that station's facility. "Last known location" is one rule everywhere (the queue, the scan check and the Waste Tracking Report): the location event with the latest time. A location entered late with an earlier time does not count as the current one, and for two events at the same time the one recorded later wins. Toolbar None. The screen has no buttons. You act by scanning. Icons and status indicators Indicator Meaning Green flash "(identifier) disposed" The scan was accepted. The item has been recorded as disposed and removed from the list. A beep sounds. The flash stays for about two and a half seconds. Full red screen with a stop sign The scan was refused. The message names the reason. It clears itself after about four seconds, or when you click it ("Tap anywhere to dismiss"). An error tone sounds. Computing the real, current queue... The list is being worked out. Nothing qualifies for disposal right now at this location. The list is empty. The red screen messages: Message What to do (identifier) was already disposed on (date). Nothing; it has already been recorded. Check that you are not holding a second copy. "(text)" doesn't match any cassette, slide or container on any case. The label could not be matched to anything. Check the barcode. (identifier) couldn't be found in its case record. The label matches a case but not a record on it. Tell your laboratory manager. (identifier) can't be disposed until (date), when its retention period ends. Keep it. Put it back. If the date is not known the message reads "an unknown date" in its place; ask your laboratory manager when the retention ends. (identifier)'s case isn't signed out yet, so its retention period hasn't started. Keep it. (identifier) can't be disposed: its case has an active retention hold ((note)). Keep it. The hold's note is shown. See Retention Holds. (identifier) was last recorded at another location, not this facility. The item is recorded as belonging elsewhere. Do not discard it here. You don't have permission to dispose of retained material. Your role does not include this permission. Hotkeys None. Any barcode scan on this page is read as a disposal scan. Step by Step Procedures Standard workflow 1. Open Batch Management and select the Disposal tile. The Disposal Queue opens with the list of items that qualify. 2. Check the scope line. If the page says no scan station is set, ask your laboratory manager to set one for this computer so that you see only your own location. 3. Take the physical item to be discarded and scan its label. 4. If the screen shows a green "(identifier) disposed", place the item in the waste. The row disappears and the count falls by one. 5. If the screen turns red, read the message. Do not discard the item. Dismiss the message by clicking it and carry on wi

title: Engraver Monitor
text: Engraver Monitor { top} Overview Purpose. The Engraver Monitor is a read only status board for the cassette engravers in your laboratory. It shows, for every engraver that has reported in, whether it is online, engraving, warning, faulted or offline, any supply warnings (cassettes low or out, a cassette colour unavailable), and when it last reported. It is a quick answer to "can I print cassettes now, and will I run out?". Intended users. Histotechnologists, grossing staff who depend on cassettes, and laboratory managers. Where it fits. Engravers are driven by the cassette engine, which owns the machine's detailed diagnostics. PathScribe shows only a coarse summary here, and a link to the engine's own diagnostics for anything deeper. Cassettes engraved here are the ones Grossing prints and that later appear in Pending Batch Load. note "Demonstration data today" With no live engraver feed connected, the screen shows a set of example devices and a Simulated badge in the toolbar. When the badge is shown, nothing on the board is a real machine. Hopper level detail and hardware controls are not built into PathScribe; they stay in the cassette engine. Screen Tour The page title is Engraver Monitor . The subtitle reads: "A real, high level status summary for every engraver the Cassette Engine reports on — status, real warning summaries, and a direct link to the Engine's own diagnostics for anything deeper. PathScribe doesn't model hopper level detail or hardware telemetry here; that stays the Engine's own job." Field definitions Status tiles. Five tiles each show a count: Online, Engraving, Warning, Fault and Offline. They count the devices shown (so they follow the organisation filter). They are not buttons. Device cards Item What it means Name The device name, or its identifier if it has no name. Identifier and location The device ID, and its location label if one was reported. Status badge Online, Engraving, Warning, Fault or Offline. Warnings A list that appears when there is anything to report. Supply warnings read "(colour) Low", "(colour) Depleted" or "(colour) Unavailable", or just Low, Depleted or Unavailable when no colour applies. Other warnings are shown as the device sent them. Reported (time) When the device last reported. Launch Engine Diagnostics A link that opens the engine's own diagnostics for this machine in a new tab. Shown only when the engine supplied a link. Devices: "Devices (n)" counts the devices shown. "Loading real device status..." appears on the first load. "No engraver has reported status yet." appears when no device has reported. Toolbar Control What it does Refresh Reads the latest status now. Reads "Refreshing..." while it works. Filter by organisation Appears only when devices belong to more than one organisation. Choose All organisations or one. Simulated badge Shown when the board is running on example data. The board also refreshes itself: at once when a change is announced, and otherwise every 30 seconds, without showing "Refreshing...". Icons and status indicators Indicator Meaning Online (green) The engraver is ready and idle. Engraving (blue) It is working on a job. Warning (amber) It is running but has something you should look at, such as low supply. Fault (red) It has stopped because of a fault. Offline (grey) It is not reporting. Simulated badge The data is demonstration data. Hotkeys None. Step by Step Procedures Standard workflow 1. Open Batch Management and select the Engraver Monitor tile. The status tiles and device cards appear. 2. Read the five tiles to see how many engravers are in each state. 3. Find your engraver's card by name or location. Check the status badge. 4. Read any warnings. A "Low" or "Depleted" warning on a colour means restock that colour of cassette before printing. 5. Check "Reported (time)". If it is old, the engraver may be offline or the link down. 6. For a fault, select Launch Engine Diagnostics and follow the engine's own screens. Then return and select Refresh . Alternative workflow 1. Leave the screen open on a bench monitor. It updates itself. 2. In a multi organisation setup, use the organisation filter to see only your own devices. Exception handling 1. No devices. "No engraver has reported status yet." Nothing has reported. Check the engraver and the cassette engine connection, or whether this is a Simulated board. 2. A device shows Offline. Check power and network at the machine. The last report time tells you how long. 3. Fault. Use the diagnostics link, if shown. If there is none, contact your engine support. 4. A colour is unavailable. Choose another cassette colour at Grossing or restock. 5. The Simulated badge shows on a live system. The live feed is not connected; contact support. Error recovery 1. The board looks out of date. Select Refresh . 2. The diagnostics link does nothing. Your browser may be blocking the new tab; allow pop ups. 3. Counts seem wrong after filtering. The tiles follow the filter; choose All organisations. Tips and Best Practices Common mistakes Expecting to control the machine from here. The board is read only. Treating a Simulated board as real. Ignoring "Reported (time)". A green badge from an hour ago may be stale. Efficiency recommendations Check supply warnings before a large grossing session, not during it. Keep the screen open on a bench monitor. Workflow recommendations Report persistent faults to your laboratory manager with the device ID shown on the card. Use Equipment Log to record maintenance of the engraver after a fix. Related Features Upstream workflow Equipment Log: the engraver's service history. Downstream workflow Grossing: printing cassettes. Label Reprint: reprinting cassette labels in bulk. Troubleshooting Common user issues Problem Likely cause Every tile shows zero No device has reported. The organisation filter is missing Only one organisation is reporting. No diagnostics link on a card The engine did not send one for that device. Colour names show as code

title: Equipment Log
text: Equipment Log { top} Overview Purpose. The Equipment Log shows each active instrument in the laboratory with its maintenance and calibration state, and lets bench staff record what they did: maintenance, calibration, function checks, malfunctions and repairs. The history is a permanent record for inspections. Intended users. Histotechnologists, cytotechnologists and molecular technologists, who can record entries by default, and laboratory managers. Recording an entry needs the "record maintenance" permission. Adding, editing or scheduling equipment is not done here; that is in Configuration, System, Equipment. Where it fits. Instruments such as tissue processors, stainers, slide scanners and engravers appear in the batch workflows and on other screens. An overdue or faulted instrument is flagged but never blocked: the device is marked, and the decision to use it is yours. Screen Tour The page title is Equipment log . The subtitle reads: "Each active instrument's maintenance and calibration status. Record what you did with Log entry; adding or changing equipment is in Configuration → System → Equipment." Field definitions Table Column What it means Equipment The instrument's name. Code Its short code, as other records and labels carry it. Kind Analyser, Camera, Engraver, Label printer, Scale, Slide scanner, Stainer, Storage unit, Tissue processor or Other. Service The service state, and below it the next due date ("Next due (date)") or, if passed, "Was due (date)". Actions The Log entry button. If no active equipment exists the table says "No equipment matches the current filter." Rows in a red tint have an alert state: Malfunction or Overdue. Service states State Meaning Up to date Everything scheduled has been done within its interval. Due soon Something is due within 14 days. Overdue A scheduled maintenance or calibration is past due. Not yet done A schedule exists but nothing passing has ever been logged. Malfunction A malfunction was logged and no passing repair or function check has been logged on or after that day. Not scheduled The instrument has no maintenance or calibration interval. When several apply, the worst one is shown, in that order: Malfunction, Overdue, Not yet done, Due soon, Up to date. Due dates count from the last passing entry. A Maintenance entry with outcome Not applicable also counts toward maintenance, but not toward calibration. Log entry window (title: "Service Log — (name) ((code))") Field What it means Open malfunction notice "Open malfunction: no passing repair or function check has been recorded since." Shown when the state is Malfunction. Maintenance, Calibration lines For each: Up to date, Due soon, Overdue or Not yet done, "Last done (date)" and "Due (date)", or "Not scheduled". Type Maintenance, Calibration, Function check, Malfunction or Repair. Starts on Maintenance. Date Done The day it was done. Starts today. It cannot be in the future. Outcome Pass, Fail or Not applicable. Starts on Pass. Done By Who did it. Starts with your name. Change it for a service engineer's name. Required. Notes Free text. Required for a Fail outcome or a Malfunction type. History A table of earlier entries: Date, Type, Outcome, By and Notes, newest first. Toolbar Button What it does Log entry Opens the Service Log window for that instrument. Dimmed with a tooltip if you lack the permission. Add Entry In the window. Saves the entry. The window stays open, the notes box is cleared and the history and state update. Close (x) Closes the window. Icons and status indicators Indicator Meaning Red row Malfunction or Overdue. Outcome tag Pass, Fail or Not applicable in the history. "Entries can't be changed or deleted. Correct a mistake with a new entry." The log is permanent. Hotkeys None. Step by Step Procedures Standard workflow 1. Open Batch Management and select the Equipment log tile. The list of instruments appears with their service states. 2. Find the instrument. Check the state and due date in the Service column. 3. Select Log entry . The Service Log window opens. 4. Choose the Type of work, check the Date Done , leave Outcome on Pass or change it, and confirm Done By . 5. Add Notes if you wish, or if you chose Fail or Malfunction. 6. Select Add Entry . The entry appears at the top of the history and the instrument's state updates. 7. Select the close mark when you are finished. Alternative workflow 1. Record several entries for one instrument in one visit; the window stays open between entries. 2. To close a malfunction, log a Repair or a Function check with Outcome Pass dated on or after the malfunction. Exception handling 1. An instrument is broken. Log type Malfunction, outcome Fail (or Pass), and describe it in Notes. The instrument turns red with state Malfunction. Tell your laboratory manager; the device is not blocked from use. 2. A service engineer did the work. Type their name in Done By. 3. You forgot to log yesterday's work. Set Date Done to yesterday. Dates in the future are refused. 4. A check failed. Choose Fail and explain in Notes. A failed maintenance or calibration does not count toward being up to date. 5. The instrument is not listed. Only active equipment appears. Ask your administrator to add or reactivate it. Error recovery 1. "Choose a type." Select a type. 2. "Enter the date it was done." Fill in the date. 3. "The date can't be in the future." Use today or earlier. 4. "Enter who did it." Fill in Done By. 5. "Choose an outcome." Select Pass, Fail or Not applicable. 6. "Describe what happened: required for a failure or malfunction." Add Notes. 7. "The entry could not be saved." Try again; if it persists contact support. 8. A wrong entry was saved. Entries cannot be changed or deleted. Add a new entry that corrects it, with an explanation in Notes. Tips and Best Practices Common mistakes Logging maintenance as Not applicable and thinking calibration is covered. It is not. Forgetting that a Fail does not reset the due date. Leaving Done By as yo

title: Batch Management
text: Batch Management { top} Overview Purpose. Batch Management follows groups of cassettes and slides from one laboratory step to the next. A batch is a physical carrier (a processor basket, a decalcification vessel, a staining rack, an archive tray, or an ad hoc box) with a barcode on it. You scan each cassette or slide into the batch, and when the carrier reaches its destination you scan every item back out and PathScribe checks that nothing is missing and nothing extra arrived. The result is a record of who handled what, and when. The module is also the doorway to eight related screens, reached from the tiles at the top of the page: Pending Load, Disposal, the Waste Tracking Report, Retention Holds, Label reprint, Slide scanning, the Engraver Monitor and the Equipment log. Each has its own article, linked at the end of this one. Intended users. Histotechnologists, cytotechnologists and molecular technologists, who have the screen by default, and laboratory managers. Administrators can open the screen but their roles do not include the batch actions unless your laboratory adds them. If the Batch Management tile is missing from the Pathology Workspace, ask your laboratory manager. Where it fits. Batch Management sits between the workstations. Grossing creates the cassettes. The Embedding and Microtomy workstations turn them into blocks and slides. Slide Distribution hands slides to pathologists or to a scanner. Batch Management records the movement of groups of those items between the processing, staining and checkout steps, and out to a reference laboratory. note "Demonstration data today" In this version the batches, racks and readings are held in your browser session and the example batches are seeded for demonstration. Three examples are provided: a staining batch part way through reconciliation (one slide missing, one unexpected scan), a referral batch with an unacknowledged temperature excursion of 11.4 °C, and a running processing batch. Resetting the demonstration restores them. The cold chain readings come from a labelled Simulated control because no temperature sensor feed is connected yet. Terms used in this module Term What it means Batch (container session) One carrier and the list of items scanned into it. Also called a container. Master barcode The barcode of the carrier. A disposable container gets a new single use label that begins CONT . A reusable rack carries a permanent engraved ID that begins RACK . Cassette The plastic holder that carries a tissue block. In this module a cassette and its block are the same item and are shown as a Block . Block Tissue embedded in wax in a cassette. Its identifier is the accession, specimen letter and block number. Slide A section cut from a block, identified by the block identifier plus the slide level. Specimen, Decant, Matrix Block Other items a batch can hold: the wet specimen container, a portion decanted from it, and a block shared by several specimens. Each decant slide and matrix slide is also an item. Manifest The list of items scanned into a batch. Items can enter a batch only by being scanned; nothing is pre filled. Processing node The laboratory step a batch belongs to. There are ten: Decal / Special Processing, Processing, Embedding, Microtomy / Sectioning, Staining, Checkout, External Referral, Cytology Processing, Cytology Staining and Cytology Imaging. Reconciliation Scanning every item back out of the carrier and comparing the scans with the manifest. Missing, Matched, Unexpected After reconciliation starts, an item is Missing until scanned out, Matched once scanned out, and a scan of something not on the manifest is Unexpected . Screen Tour The page title is Batch Management with the line "Track groups of cassettes and slides through processing nodes (Decal / Special Processing, Processing, Embedding, Microtomy, Staining, Checkout) via container barcodes — chain of custody scanning, reconciliation, and QA discrepancy logging." From top to bottom: a row of tiles, the lookup box with the New Container button, then two lists of batches. Selecting a batch opens its detail page. New Container opens a dialog. Field definitions Stage tiles (the first ten tiles) Tile What it counts Decal / Special, Processing, Embedding, Microtomy, Staining, Checkout, Referral, Cyto Processing, Cyto Staining, Cyto Imaging The number of open batches (Active or Reconciling) at that step. Select a tile to show only those batches in the Active & Reconciling list. The tooltip reads "Filter by: ..." and, once chosen, "Showing: ... — click to reset". Select the tile again to clear the filter. The filter changes the Active & Reconciling list only. The Complete & Aborted list always shows every closed batch. Page tiles (the last eight tiles) open other screens. They do not filter anything. Tile Opens Disposal Disposal Queue Waste Tracking Report Waste Tracking Report Retention Holds Retention Holds. Hover text: "Open the Retention Holds queue". Pending Load Pending Batch Load Label reprint Label Reprint. Hover text: "Reprint labels for many cases at once". Slide scanning Slide Scanning Engraver Monitor Engraver Monitor Equipment log Equipment Log Lookup box Field What it means Scan or enter a master batch barcode... Scan or type the carrier's barcode and press Enter. If it is an existing batch, the batch opens. If it is a registered reusable rack that is free, New Container opens with that rack already filled in. Otherwise a red message appears. Batch lists Item What it means Active & Reconciling (n) Batches that are still open. Each row shows the status, master barcode, processing node, protocol, a STAT badge for urgent batches, the item count and the time the batch was created. Complete & Aborted (n) Closed batches, shown dimmed, with the time they were completed or aborted. The list appears only when there is at least one. No active batches. Create one to get started. There is nothing open (or nothing open at the chosen stage). Loading batches... T

title: Label Reprint
text: Label Reprint { top} Overview Purpose. Label Reprint reprints requisition, specimen container and cassette labels for many cases at once. You find the cases by accession date or accession number range, tick the label types you want, and PathScribe prints them one at a time. Each label is recorded in the audit log, and any that fail can be retried. Intended users. Histotechnologists and laboratory managers (and administrators). Printing needs its own permission, "Batch label reprint", which is not given to every role that can open the screen. Where it fits. Use it after a printer jam, a lost tray or a damaged batch of labels, when labels for a whole day's cases must be redone. For a single case, use the print buttons on the case itself. Once labels are reprinted, the items can be scanned into batches on Batch Management. Screen Tour The page title is Label reprint . The subtitle reads: "Find cases by accession date or number, choose the labels, and reprint them one at a time. Every label is audited; failed labels can be retried." Field definitions Filters. Enter at least one. An empty search finds nothing, on purpose, so that the whole laboratory is never reprinted by accident. Field What it means Accessioned from, Accessioned to A date range, inclusive, on the day each case was accessioned. Accession number from, Accession number to A range of accession numbers, inclusive. They are compared as text, so type them in the same format as the case numbers. You can combine a date range with a number range. A case must satisfy every filter you fill in. Case list (after Find cases) Item What it means "(n) cases found; (m) selected." How many cases matched and how many are ticked. Reprint (tick box) Tick or untick a case. All found cases start ticked. Unticked cases are left out. Accession The case accession number. Cases are listed in accession order, oldest first. Specimens How many specimens the case has. No cases match. Enter a date range or an accession number range. Nothing matched, or no filter was entered. Label options Option What it means Requisition One requisition label sheet per case. Ticked by default. Specimen containers One container label per specimen. Ticked by default. Cassettes One cassette label per block, and one per matrix block. Not ticked by default. Cassette printer Appears only when Cassettes is ticked. Choose the cassette printer from your printers. "(n) labels to print." The total for the cases and label types currently chosen. Toolbar Button What it does Find cases Searches with your filters. It also clears any earlier results and unticks nothing. Disabled while a print is running. Reprint labels Starts printing. Disabled when nothing is to print or a print is running; dimmed with a tooltip if you lack the permission. Retry (n) failed label(s) Appears after a run that had failures. Prints only the failed labels again. Icons and status indicators Indicator Meaning Printing (done) of (total)... The run is in progress. The tick boxes and buttons are disabled meanwhile. Printed (n); failed (n); blocked by the on demand guardrail (n). The summary at the end of a run. A list of problems One line per failed or blocked label: the accession, the label type and target (for example a specimen letter or block), the status and any message. Statuses are printed, failed, blocked and not printed. Choose the cassette printer first. You ticked Cassettes without choosing a printer. There is nothing to print. No labels in the selection. Sending label to the printer… A small line at the bottom of the screen while a label goes to a printer through the PathScribe site agent. It goes away when the job finishes; the screen that printed reports the outcome. Label queued: prints next The label is waiting and will print as soon as the one in front is done. When others are ahead it reads "Label queued: n jobs ahead", and "n more labels waiting" is added when several are queued. Printing on … The printer (for example a ZD421) is printing your label now. It appears only when the site agent reports that printing has started. Network print jobs Labels sent to printers set to "Direct via Interface Engine" are listed in a small area at the bottom of the screen, each with its state: sent and waiting ("Label … sent to …. Waiting for the printer…"), printed, or failed with the reason (for example the printer is out of labels or out of ribbon, the print head is open, or the printer could not be reached). A failed label, or one with no answer after two minutes, shows Retry and Dismiss ; retry is never automatic. Simulate: printed / Simulate: out of labels Two small demonstration buttons shown beside a waiting network print job only when no interface engine is connected (the demonstration). They stand in for the engine's answer; they do not print anything. You don't have permission to reprint labels in a batch. Your role lacks the permission. Hotkeys None. Step by Step Procedures Standard workflow 1. Open Batch Management and select the Label reprint tile. 2. Enter the date range and/or accession number range of the cases and select Find cases . The list appears with every case ticked. 3. Untick any case you do not want to reprint. 4. Under Labels , tick the types you need. If you tick Cassettes , choose the Cassette printer . 5. Check the line "(n) labels to print." 6. Select Reprint labels . The line "Printing (done) of (total)..." counts up. Labels are sent one at a time with a short pause between them. 7. When it finishes, read the summary. If everything printed, collect the labels. Alternative workflow 1. To reprint only cassettes for a run, untick Requisition and Specimen containers, tick Cassettes, and choose the printer. 2. To reprint one case, search by an accession number range with the same number in both boxes. Exception handling 1. Some labels failed. Read the problem list. Fix the cause (printer off, paper out, pop ups blocked) and select Retry (n) failed label(s) . Labels that already printe

title: Pending Batch Load
text: Pending Batch Load { top} Overview Purpose. Pending Batch Load answers one question: which cassettes and slides have been printed or engraved but have not been scanned into any open batch yet? It is a read only worklist for finding what still needs to be picked up and loaded. You do not load anything from this screen. Intended users. Histotechnologists, cytotechnologists, molecular technologists and laboratory managers, anyone who has the Batch Management screen. Where it fits. After Grossing prints cassettes, and after the Embedding and Microtomy workstations produce blocks and slides, the items wait here until someone scans them into a batch on the Batch Management page. As soon as an item is scanned into an open batch it leaves this list. note "Nothing is stored on this screen" The list is worked out fresh each time you open or refresh the page, by comparing every case's physical material with the manifests of all open batches. It cannot be edited, and it cannot go out of date except between refreshes. Screen Tour The page title is Pending Batch Load . The subtitle explains that it lists cassettes and slides that have been printed or engraved but not yet scanned into an active batch, and that to load one you open or create the batch it belongs in from Batch Management and scan it there. A second line tells you the scope: "Scoped to (facility), per the active scan station." when this computer has a scan station set. Only cases from that facility are shown. "No scan station set — showing every facility's own pending items. Set a station for a facility scoped queue." when no station is set. Field definitions Field What it means Scan or type to search — cassette/slide id, case, or specimen... A search box. It matches part of the item identifier (what a barcode holds), the case accession number or the specimen label, ignoring capitals. Scanning a label into it fills in the identifier. Awaiting Batch Load (n) The number of waiting items. While you search it reads "Awaiting Batch Load (n of total)". Case heading The case accession number and how many items it has waiting, for example "(accession) — 3 items". Items are grouped by case. Item identifier The cassette or slide identifier, as printed on the label. Type Cassette (a block) or Slide . Specimen (letter) The specimen the item belongs to. Toolbar Button What it does Search box Narrows the list as you type. Clear Appears once you have typed something. Empties the search box. Refresh Works the list out again. Reads "Refreshing..." while it works. Icons and status indicators Indicator Meaning Computing the real, current queue... The list is being worked out. Nothing printed is currently waiting to be loaded into a batch. Every printed item is already in an open batch. No pending item matches "(text)". Nothing matches your search. Clear it to see the full list. What counts as waiting: A cassette whose block has been grossed, embedded or marked exhausted. A block that is still a placeholder, with nothing printed yet, is not listed. A slide that has been cut. A slide still marked Pending Cut is not listed because nothing physical exists yet. Neither is in any Active or Reconciling batch. Items in Complete or Aborted batches that are not in an open batch count as waiting again. Hotkeys None. Step by Step Procedures Standard workflow 1. Open Batch Management from the Pathology Workspace and select the Pending Load tile. The page shows "Computing the real, current queue..." and then the list. 2. Read the second line under the title to check which facility the list covers. 3. Look through the groups, or type or scan into the search box to find a specific cassette, case or specimen. 4. Collect the physical items. 5. Return to Batch Management (use the breadcrumb or the browser back button), open or create the batch they belong in, and scan each one into it. 6. Return here and select Refresh . The scanned items are gone from the list. Alternative workflow 1. To check a single label, scan it into the search box. If its identifier appears, it is waiting. If it does not, it is already in an open batch, has been disposed of, or was never printed. 2. To check a whole case, type its accession number. Exception handling 1. An item you printed is not listed. Search by the case number. If the case is not there, check that the block was actually grossed and the label printed; a placeholder block is not shown. Check the facility scope too: a station set for another facility hides this case. 2. An item you expected to be in a batch is listed. It is not in any open batch. Perhaps it was in a batch that has since been aborted. Scan it into the right batch. 3. A slide is not listed. It is still Pending Cut, or it is in an open batch already. 4. No scan station is set. The list covers every facility. Set the station for this computer (see your laboratory manager) to scope it. Error recovery 1. The list looks stale after you load items. Select Refresh ; the page does not update itself. 2. The search shows "No pending item matches". Select Clear and try fewer letters. 3. The list stays on "Computing..." for a long time. Refresh the page and, if it persists, contact support. Tips and Best Practices Common mistakes Expecting to load items from this page. It is only a list. Loading is done by scanning on a batch's detail page. Forgetting that the page does not refresh itself. Select Refresh after you load. Reading the list as the whole laboratory when a scan station is set. It is scoped to that station's facility. Efficiency recommendations Scan a label into the search box instead of typing. Search by the case number to see all of a case's waiting cassettes and slides together. Workflow recommendations Look at the list at the start of a run and before the end of the shift to catch cassettes that were printed and then left on the bench. Use it together with the stage tiles on the Batch Management page to see both what is in batches and what is not. Related Features Ups

title: Retention Holds
text: Retention Holds { top} Overview Purpose. A retention hold stops a case's material from ever being offered for disposal, whatever its retention period. The Retention Holds screen lists every active hold across the laboratory, with the case, the reason, who placed it and when, so that someone can see what is being held back and let it go when it is no longer needed. Intended users. Laboratory managers and bench staff who manage stored material. Releasing a hold needs its own permission (Release a retention hold), checked for the case's facility. Exporting the list needs another. Placing a hold is done on the case itself, not here. Where it fits. A hold is placed from the case, in the Specimens & Reports section of the report screen ("Retention Hold: Blocks disposal until released"), for reasons such as a patient request, litigation or research. While a hold is active the case's material never appears in the Disposal Queue, and a scan to dispose is refused with the hold's note. Releasing the hold here returns the material to normal retention rules. Screen Tour The page title is Retention Holds . The subtitle reads: "Cases whose material is held back from disposal. Release a hold with a note when it is no longer needed." While the list is loading you see "Loading holds...". Field definitions Column or control What it means Search case, reason or person Filters the list as you type. It matches the accession number, the reason, the name of the person who placed the hold and the note. Count "(n) active hold(s)" for the rows currently shown. Case The case accession number. Reason Patient Requested Retention / Return, Litigation Hold, Research Hold or Other. Note The explanation typed when the hold was placed, or a dash. It can name people, so treat it as sensitive. Placed by The name of the person who placed it. Placed The date and time, in your language's format. The list is ordered oldest first. Actions The Release button. Only active holds are listed. A released hold disappears. If there are none, the screen says "No active retention holds." Release retention hold window Field What it means Title line The case number and the reason of the hold you are releasing. Release note Required. Why the hold is no longer needed, for example "Patient confirmed no further need for specimen return." Toolbar Button What it does Export CSV Downloads the rows currently shown as a spreadsheet with Case, Reason, Placed by and Placed at. The note is left out on purpose because it can name people. Greyed out when there are no rows; dimmed with a tooltip if you lack the export permission. Release Opens the Release retention hold window for that row. Dimmed with a tooltip if you may not release holds for that case's facility. Release hold In the window. Confirms the release. Greyed out until a release note is typed. Cancel Closes the window without releasing. Icons and status indicators Indicator Meaning "Hold released." The hold was released and the list refreshed. "Add a release note first." The note was empty. "This hold was already released." A colleague released it first. "This case could not be found." The case is no longer available. "You don't have permission to release this hold." Your role lacks the permission for that facility. "The hold could not be released. Try again." Any other failure. "You don't have permission to export this queue." The export was refused. Hotkeys None on this screen. Step by Step Procedures Standard workflow Review the holds 1. Open Batch Management and select the Retention Holds tile. The list loads. 2. Read the count. Type in the search box to find a case, reason or person. 3. Read each hold's reason and note to decide whether it is still needed. Release a hold 1. Find the row and select Release . The Release retention hold window opens. 2. Type the Release note . 3. Select Release hold . The message "Hold released." appears, the window closes and the row leaves the list. 4. The case's material may now appear in the Disposal Queue, once its retention period has ended. Alternative workflow 1. Export for a review meeting. Search to narrow the list if you want, then select Export CSV . 2. Place a hold. Open the case in the report screen and use its Retention Hold control. This screen cannot create holds. Exception handling 1. The Release button is dimmed. You do not have the release permission for that case's facility. Ask a manager. 2. A hold was released by mistake. Releasing cannot be reversed here. Place a new hold from the case, with a note explaining. 3. Someone else released it first. The message says it was already released. Reload the page. 4. The note is missing. Releasing requires a note; the button stays greyed out until you type one. Error recovery 1. "This case could not be found." The case may be archived. Contact support. 2. "The hold could not be released. Try again." Wait a moment and try again. If it keeps failing, note the case number and contact support. 3. The list is out of date. Reload the page. warning "Release only with authority" Releasing a hold re opens the way to disposal of irreplaceable material. Check with the person or department that asked for the hold (the patient, legal counsel, the research team) before releasing it, and record that in the note. Tips and Best Practices Common mistakes Releasing a hold without checking with the requester. Writing a vague release note such as "done". Say who agreed and when. Looking for a way to place a hold here. Place it on the case. Emailing the exported file without thinking: it names cases and people who placed holds. Efficiency recommendations Search by reason to review all litigation holds together. Review the list on a schedule so old holds are not forgotten. Workflow recommendations Review holds before each disposal run. Put clear notes in when you place holds so a reviewer can decide later. Related Features Upstream workflow Report: where a hold is placed on a case. Downstream workflow Disposal Queue:

title: Slide Scanning
text: Slide Scanning { top} Overview Purpose. Slide Scanning is the bench hand off to the slide scanners. Slides that were routed to Digital wait in a scanning queue. You choose a scanner, tick the slides to put on it and load them as a scan batch. You then send the batch to the scanner and, when every slide has a result, unload it. Slides that scanned and passed image quality check are marked Scanned. The rest go back to the queue. Intended users. Histotechnologists, cytotechnologists and molecular technologists, and laboratory managers. Loading, sending and unloading are separate permissions, checked against the scanner's laboratory. Administrators can open the screen but do not have those permissions unless they are added to their role. Where it fits. The Slide Distribution workstation decides where each slide goes: to a pathologist's desk, or Digital. A slide routed to Digital appears here. After scanning, images can be opened in the WSI viewer. note "Demonstration data today" Scanner traffic goes through the interface engine. In this version the scanner is simulated, so sending a batch does not drive a real machine, and the progress of the slides comes from the demonstration. The scanners listed come from the Equipment register. Screen Tour The page title is Slide scanning . The subtitle reads: "Load slides from the scanning queue onto a slide scanner, send the batch to the scanner, and unload it when every slide has its result. Slides that didn't scan go back to the queue." The screen has two parts: the scanning queue with a load bar, and the scan batches table. Field definitions Scanning queue Field What it means Scanning queue (n slides) The slides routed to Digital and not yet in a scan batch. STAT cases come first, then Rush, then the rest, oldest first. Slide scanner The scanner to load. The list holds the active slide scanners in the Equipment register ("— Select a scanner —"). Choose (tick box) One tick box per slide. Its label reads "Choose (block) (stain)". Case The case accession number. Slide The block and the stain, for example "A1 · H&E". Priority The case priority, or a dash. Routed to The scanner that Slide Distribution assigned, shown by name. Rack / slot The rack and slot recorded at distribution, or a dash. If no scanners exist: "No slide scanners are set up. Add them in Configuration → Equipment (kind "Slide scanner")." If the queue is empty: "No slides are waiting. Slides routed to Digital at the Slide Distribution Station appear here." Scan batches Column What it means Batch The scan batch barcode with an arrow. Select it to open or close the list of its slides. Scanner The scanner's name. Status Loaded, not sent; Scanning; Scanned, ready to unload; Finished with failures, ready to unload; or Unloaded. A failed send adds "Not sent ((code), (time))" in red. Progress "(n) scanned · (n) failed · (n) waiting (of (total))". Loaded When the batch was loaded. Newest batches first. Actions Send to scanner or Send again , and Unload . When a batch is opened, each slide row shows its position, the case, the slide, its status (Waiting, Scanning, Scanned or Scan failed), the failure reason if any ("Image QC failed: (reason)") and when the scan finished. If no batch exists: "No scan batches yet." Toolbar Control What it does Live status badge Shows whether the page is receiving changes by itself. The batch list updates without reloading when a scanner reports. Refresh Reads the queue, batches and scanners again. Reads "Refreshing..." meanwhile. Load (n) slide(s) Loads the ticked slides onto the chosen scanner as a new scan batch. Greyed out until a scanner is chosen and at least one slide is ticked (tooltip: "Choose a scanner and at least one slide"). Dimmed if you lack the load permission. Send to scanner / Send again Sends the batch's manifest to the scanner. Shown for a batch that is Loaded, not sent. "Send again" appears after a failed send. Unload Takes the batch off the scanner. Shown for a Loaded, not sent batch, and for a batch where every slide has a result. Icons and status indicators Indicator Meaning Green message "(n) slide(s) loaded on (scanner)." "(batch) sent to the scanner." "(batch) unloaded." Red message A refusal. See Error recovery. Status text The batch's state, as listed above. Hotkeys None. Step by Step Procedures Standard workflow 1. Open Batch Management and select the Slide scanning tile. The queue and the batches load. 2. In Slide scanner , choose the scanner you are loading. 3. Tick the slides you have placed on that scanner. The button now reads "Load (n) slides". 4. Select Load . The message "(n) slides loaded on (scanner)." appears, the slides leave the queue and a new batch appears in the table as "Loaded, not sent". Where Slide Distribution recorded a rack and slot, that position is used; otherwise positions are numbered in the order you ticked. 5. Select Send to scanner on the new batch. The message "(batch) sent to the scanner." appears and the status becomes Scanning. 6. Watch the progress column. When every slide has a result, the status changes to Scanned or Finished with failures and Unload appears. 7. Select Unload . The message "(batch) unloaded." appears. Slides that scanned and passed image quality check are marked Scanned. Others return to the scanning queue. Alternative workflow 1. Check a batch's slides. Select the batch name to expand it and read each slide's status and any failure reason. 2. Cancel a load. Before sending, select Unload on a Loaded, not sent batch. Every slide returns to the queue. 3. Rely on live updates. With the Live badge on, leave the page open; it refreshes when the scanner reports. Exception handling 1. A send fails. The batch stays loaded. The status shows "Not sent ((code), (time))" and the button reads Send again . Wait until the interface engine is reachable and try again. 2. A slide fails or fails image QC. It is marked Scan failed or "Image QC failed", with a reason. After you unload, it returns to the

title: Bench Contributions
text: Bench Contributions { top} Overview Purpose. Bench Contributions shows how bench work is going over the last 30 days: how many cases you accessioned, how many items you added to batches, how long batches are waiting, how long specimens take to move from one stage to the next, and how your molecular runs performed on quality control. Intended users. Bench roles such as histotechnologists, pathology assistants and laboratory managers. The tile appears only if your role may open it. Where it fits. Open it from the Home Dashboard when you want to review your work. It is a single page that you scroll; it has no buttons and changes nothing. The work itself is done in the Pathology Workspace. Screen Tour note "Your figures, and the shared ones" The page title line shows your name and says which figures are yours and which are laboratory wide: your accessioning, batch and molecular QC activity, plus laboratory wide queue aging and turnaround, for the last 30 days. Accessioning Rate, My Batch Throughput and Molecular QC count only your own work. Queue Aging and Stage to Stage TAT cover the whole laboratory, not just you. note "Demonstration data" Figures are worked out from the cases and batches held in the system. In a demonstration setup these are demonstration cases and batches, so the numbers are not real laboratory results. Field definitions Every figure uses the last 30 days. Days are counted in your facility's local time, not the time on your device. A figure that cannot be worked out is shown as a dash (—). Accessioning Rate (yours) Field What it means Cases accessioned The number of cases you accessioned in the last 30 days. Per active hour Cases accessioned divided by the number of different clock hours in which you accessioned at least one case. It is not divided by a full shift, so hours when you accessioned nothing do not count. Under the two figures, a Daily accessioning chart shows one bar for each day of the window, oldest on the left. A day with no cases has a short grey bar, and pointing at a bar shows the date and the count. The bars are scaled to your busiest day. When you accessioned nothing in the window, the tile says "No accessioning activity in this window." My Batch Throughput (yours) Field What it means Node name (for example Embedding, Microtomy / Sectioning, Staining) One box for each processing step where you added items. Items added How many items (cassettes or slides) you personally added to batches at that step in the last 30 days. It counts who added the item, not who created the batch. Steps with no items from you are left out. When there are none, the tile says "No batch activity in this window." Queue Aging — All Techs (the whole laboratory) Field What it means Open batches Batches at that step that are still Active or Reconciling right now. Oldest open batch How long, in hours, the oldest of those batches has existed since it was created. Average age The average age, in hours, of all open batches at that step. This answers "what is backing up right now". It is not limited to your own batches or to the 30 day window. When nothing is open, the tile says "No open batches at this node." Stage to Stage TAT (the whole laboratory) Turnaround time (TAT) is the time between two stages for the same cassette or slide. Each box is named group · from stage → to stage . Field What it means Surgical Accessioning → Embedding, then Embedding → Staining. Cytology Accessioning → Cytology Processing, then Cytology Processing → Cytology Staining. Mean The average time in hours between the two stages. Median The middle time in hours: half of the items were faster, half slower. It is less affected by a few very slow items. Samples How many items passed through both stages in the window. Only these named stage pairs are shown, and only pairs with at least one sample appear. When there are none, the tile says "No specimens passed through both stages in this window." The "Accessioning" time is the moment the case was accessioned, and it counts only if that happened inside the 30 day window. Molecular QC (yours) Field What it means Batches The number of molecular batches you created in the last 30 days. Pass rate Of the batches whose controls have a recorded result, the share where the controls passed. Batches still waiting for results are left out; they are not counted as failures. Controls evaluated The number of batches that have a recorded control result, which is the base for the pass rate. Rerun rate The share of your batches that were later replaced by a rerun. When you created no molecular batches in the window, the tile says "No molecular batches in this window." Toolbar The page has no toolbar and no buttons. Scroll to see all five tiles. Icons and status indicators Indicator Meaning — (dash) There is not enough activity to work out the figure. Number followed by h A time in hours, rounded to one decimal place. Percentage A rate, rounded to a whole number. Hotkeys None are specific to this page. Alt+H (Go Home) returns to Home, and F1 (View Help) opens this page. note "Not shown today" The page works out a day by day count of your accessioning, but no daily chart is displayed. Only the totals above are shown. Step by Step Procedures Standard workflow 1. On the Home Dashboard, select the Bench Contributions tile. The page opens and the figures fill in. 2. Read Accessioning Rate for your cases accessioned and your rate per active hour. 3. Read My Batch Throughput to see where you added items. 4. Read Queue Aging — All Techs to see which steps have old open batches. 5. Read Stage to Stage TAT to compare mean and median times between stages. 6. Read Molecular QC for your pass rate and rerun rate. Alternative workflow 1. Press F1 on this page for this guide page. 2. Laboratory managers can use Queue Aging and Stage to Stage TAT to decide where to add staff or move work. Exception handling 1. If a tile says there was no activity, you did not do that kind of work in the last 30 day

title: Case Flags
text: Case Flags { top} Overview Purpose. A flag is a short marker on a case or on one specimen, such as STAT — Rush Processing , Hold — Pending Info or Second Opinion Requested . Flags tell the next person something needs attention. This page shows how to set and clear them, how they look on the Worklist and in search, and what they do. Intended users. Anyone who handles cases. Applying flags needs the "apply flag" permission and clearing them needs the "remove flag" permission. Both are given by default to pathologists, accessioners, histotechnologists and the other case handling roles, but not to the Admin role. Where it fits. You set flags in the Flag Manager window, which opens from the Report screen, the Cytology Screening screen and the Cytology Worklist. Everyone then sees the flags in the Worklist, the case search bar and Search. note "Flag for MDT" Sending a case to a multidisciplinary meeting is a separate action. See Case Team and Tumor Board. Screen Tour Field definitions Left side: targets Item Meaning Case A flag on the whole case. All Specimens The same flag on every specimen. Each specimen A flag on that specimen only. Its applied flags show as chips with a count. You can pick the case, or one or more specimens, but not both. Trying shows "Case and specimens can't be selected together" ("Invalid selection"). Right side: the catalogue Item Meaning Search box Finds a flag by name, code or description. Flag card Shows a code chip, a severity dot, the name and + Apply (or Applied ). Only flags your administrator has made active for that level are listed. Severity dot Red for severity 5 or more, amber for 4, blue for 3, grey below. The tooltip reads "Severity N". Footer Item Meaning "No changes" / "You have unsaved flag changes" Whether anything is waiting to be saved. Cancel Closes the window. With changes, asks Discard changes? Save Saves ("Saving…"). Flags shipped with PathScribe include STAT — Rush Processing, Malignant, Second Opinion Requested, Clinical Correlation, Tumor Board Scheduled, Amended, QC Review, Hold — Pending Info, Discordant, Confidential — Restricted Printing, Intraoperative Consult, Margins Involved, Insufficient Specimen, IHC Panel and Molecular Panel. Your administrator can add or switch off flags in Configuration under System, Flags ("Case & Specimen Flags"). Toolbar Control Where What it does Flags Report, bottom bar Opens the Flag Manager (Alt+F). 🚩 Flags Cytology Screening Opens it for that case. Manage Flags Cytology Worklist Opens it for a row awaiting verification. Undo removal icon On a struck through chip Puts the flag back before saving. Icons and status indicators Indicator Meaning Solid flag icon on a Worklist chip A flag on the whole case. Dashed flag icon A flag on a specimen. Struck through chip Marked for removal, not yet saved. Grey chips Every flag chip on the Worklist is the same grey; colour does not tell flags apart. Padlock style restriction A flag with "Restricts printing" (Confidential) stops printing by anyone without the "Print a restricted case" permission. Messages in the Flag Manager window "Select a target on the left" appears on the right until you pick the case or a specimen. Underneath it says to choose the case or one or more specimens, then click a flag to apply it. "No case flags applied" or "No flags applied" (for a specimen) is shown under a target that has no flag yet. "No … level flags defined" means your administrator has made no flag available at that level (case or specimen). "No flags match …" shows what you typed in the search box when nothing fits. A flag that came from the laboratory system shows a padlock instead of the remove cross. Its tooltip reads "Applied by LIS — cannot be removed". Only the laboratory system can take it off. Remove from multiple specimens? If you remove a flag that is also applied to other specimens, a question says the flag "is also applied to" the others. Choose Remove from this specimen only , Remove from all … specimens (the count includes this one), or Cancel . Nothing is removed until you select Save , and every removal is recorded in the audit trail. Hotkeys Key Action Alt+F Open the Flag Manager (on the Report) Alt+S Apply STAT Flag (on the Report): puts the STAT flag on the open case straight away, with no window; a message at the screen says it was applied Ctrl+Alt+K Select the case Ctrl+Alt+L Select all specimens Ctrl+Alt+M Deselect all Ctrl+Alt+O Save Ctrl+Alt+Shift+X Cancel Alt+Shift+R On the Worklist, read the flags aloud Alt+F opens Search on other screens; on the Report it opens the Flag Manager. Use Alt+J then F if the key does not respond. Step by Step Procedures Standard workflow 1. Open the case in the Report. 2. Select Flags in the bottom bar. The Flag Manager opens. 3. On the left, select Case (or one or more specimens). 4. On the right, type part of the flag name in the search box, then select + Apply on the card. The card shows Applied and a chip appears on the left. 5. Select Save . The footer shows "Saving…" and then the window closes. Others now see the flag. Alternative workflow 1. Remove a flag. Select the target, then the remove control on the chip. The chip is struck through. Select Save . 2. Undo before saving. Select Undo removal on the struck through chip. 3. Flag every specimen. Select All Specimens , then apply. 4. Remove from many specimens. Removing a flag that is on other specimens asks Remove from multiple specimens? Choose Remove from this specimen only , Remove from all N specimens or Cancel . 5. Apply STAT without opening the window. On the Report, press Alt+S or say "flag stat". The STAT flag is put on the case and a short message confirms it. If the case is already STAT the message says so and nothing changes; the shortcut never removes STAT (use the Flag Manager for that). It needs the same "apply flag" permission, and is recorded in the audit log like a save from the Flag Manager. 6. Flags from the laboratory system. Flags sent by the LIS

title: Case Search Bar
text: Case Search Bar { top} Overview Purpose. The search box in the middle of the top bar takes you straight to a case. Type or scan an identifier, press Enter, and the case opens. Intended users. Anyone whose role may open Search. If you cannot open Search, the bar is not shown. Where it fits. It is on every screen. For filtering by date, status, flags and more, use the full Search screen instead. Screen Tour Field definitions Item Meaning Box, with the hint "Scan or enter ID…" Type at least 2 characters. Identifiers accepted Accession number, medical record number, national ID, requisition number and block ID, depending on the formats your laboratory has turned on. Support reference The reference from a support ticket; it opens the case, or its audit record. Results window (several matches) Column Meaning Accession The case number. Patient Name. DOB · Sex Date of birth and sex. Priority Case priority. Status Case status. Facility Where it belongs. Rows also show the number of specimens, up to four case flags in grey, and a "matched:" hint saying which identifier matched. Toolbar Control What it does Box Type or scan. Escape Clears the box. Icons and status indicators Indicator Meaning "Fetching Accession … from LIS…" Nothing was found here, so PathScribe is asking the laboratory system. "No case found for '…'" Neither place has it. Hotkeys Key Action Alt+Shift+B Focus the case search bar Enter Open the single match, or search Escape Clear Step by Step Procedures Standard workflow 1. Press Alt+Shift+B, or select the box. 2. Type or scan the identifier (at least 2 characters). 3. Press Enter. If there is one match the case opens in the Report. A barcode or QR scan opens a single match without Enter. 4. If several match, a results window opens. Select a row to open it. Alternative workflow 1. Paste a support reference to open the case or audit it points to. 2. Type part of an MRN to list a patient's cases, then pick one. Exception handling 1. Fetching … from LIS. Wait. If a case is found it opens. 2. No case found. Check the digits, or try another identifier. 3. Several patients with the same number. Check the DOB and facility columns before opening. Error recovery 1. If the wrong case opened, go back with the browser or select Home. Nothing was changed. 2. If you opened a case with unsaved work in another, the screen asks before leaving. warning "Check the patient before you act" Always confirm name, date of birth and accession on the Report before editing or signing out. Opening a case is recorded in the audit log. Tips and Best Practices Common mistakes Typing one character; at least 2 are needed. Searching for a block ID shared by several cases without reading the list. Efficiency recommendations Scan the label rather than typing. Use Alt+Shift+B to jump to the box. Workflow recommendations Use the Search screen for lists and reports; use this bar for one known case. Related Features Upstream workflow Accession: the identifiers are created here. Downstream workflow Report: where the case opens. Search: the full search screen. Case Flags: the grey chips in the results. Troubleshooting Common user issues Problem Likely cause No search bar Your role may not open Search. Nothing happens on Enter Fewer than 2 characters. Identifier not recognised Your laboratory has not enabled that format. Resolution steps 1. Retry with the accession number. 2. Try the Search screen. 3. Ask for the format to be enabled. When to contact support Contact your laboratory's PathScribe support when a case that exists never appears, or the LIS fetch always fails.

title: Clinical Links
text: Clinical Links { top} Overview Purpose. Open well known outside references without leaving PathScribe's tab order. There are two lists: a fixed one in the top bar, and a laboratory list called Quick Links. Intended users. Everyone who signs in. Where it fits. The link button is in the top bar on every screen. Screen Tour Field definitions Item Meaning Title Clinical Links , heading "External Resources" The fixed window. CAP Cancer Protocols College of American Pathologists protocols. WHO Classification of Tumours WHO reference. PathologyOutlines Online reference. UpToDate Clinical reference; may need a subscription. Quick Links Your laboratory's own list in three groups: Protocols, References and Systems. Toolbar Control What it does Link button in the top bar Opens Clinical Links. Close Closes the window. Icons and status indicators Indicator Meaning "Insecure link" tag The address does not use https and is shown as plain text, not a link. Hotkeys Key Action Alt+Q Open Quick Links (Worklist, Search, Audit Log) Voice "open clinical resources" does the same. Step by Step Procedures Standard workflow 1. Select the link button in the top bar. 2. Choose a reference. It opens in a new browser tab. 3. Close the tab to return to PathScribe. Alternative workflow 1. On the Worklist, Search or Audit Log, press Alt+Q to open Quick Links. 2. Choose a group and a link. Exception handling 1. Insecure link. Copy the address into a browser only if you trust it. 2. Site asks for a login. UpToDate and some others need your own account. Error recovery 1. If a link is wrong, tell your administrator; links are set in Configuration under System, External Resources. warning "Never paste patient details into an outside site" External sites are outside PathScribe. Do not enter names, dates of birth or case numbers. Tips and Best Practices Common mistakes Looking for a Quick Links button on the Worklist; none is shown, only the Alt+Q key. Assuming the list is complete; it holds four fixed links. Efficiency recommendations Keep the protocol tab open beside the report. Workflow recommendations Administrators: add the laboratory's own procedure sites to Quick Links. Related Features Upstream workflow Personal Settings: the other top bar items. Downstream workflow Report: where references are used most. Help Troubleshooting Common user issues Problem Likely cause Alt+Q does nothing Not on Worklist, Search or Audit Log. Link does not open Pop ups blocked. Quick Links is empty Nothing set by your administrator. Resolution steps 1. Allow pop ups for PathScribe. 2. Try the fixed list. 3. Ask your administrator. When to contact support Contact your laboratory's PathScribe support when a link goes to the wrong site or Quick Links will not open.

title: Critical Alert
text: Critical Alert { top} Overview Purpose. When a case has a critical finding, PathScribe can send the responsible physician a short message by secure email or text. The message carries a reference link. The link opens the Critical Alert page, a small reference page that shows which case and which physician the alert is for, and lets the physician mark it as reviewed. This article describes that page and what the laboratory sees afterwards. Intended users. The physician who receives the alert. The pathologist and laboratory manager, who track whether alerts were opened and acknowledged. Where it fits. The alert is sent in addition to the pathologist's own recorded verbal notification, never instead of it. The recipient opens the link, reads the reference page, and selects Acknowledge Reviewed . The laboratory follows the result on the Critical Alerts tab of the Audit Log. warning "The page never shows the patient or the finding" By design the page shows no patient name, date of birth, medical record number or clinical detail, and never says what the critical finding is. It shows only the accession number, the physician's name and the status of the link. The physician must get the result itself from the laboratory or from the hospital record. In production, tapping the link is meant to hand off to the hospital's own sign in; that handoff is not connected in this environment, so only the reference information is shown. warning "Demonstration and simulated delivery today" The page carries the banner "This is a demo/pilot reference link, not a production secure one." The channels that send the alert (secure email, text message, EHR inbox push) are stand ins in this environment. The Audit Log marks them Simulated and the alert text shows what would have been sent. Do not rely on this page to reach a real physician. Screen Tour The page is one dark card. There is no menu and no sign in. The link is the only way in, and it works for a limited time. Field definitions Field What it means Banner The notice described above, with a red warning triangle. PathScribe Critical Alert The heading line. Accession number The laboratory's number for the case. It is the only case identifier shown. For The name of the physician the alert was sent to. Active / Expired The status of the link. You will normally see Active; an expired link does not open. Link expires (date and time) When the link stops working. The time is shown in the time zone of the laboratory's facility, and the zone is named beside it (for example MST), so it means the same moment wherever you open the link. Viewed {{count}} time Reads "Viewed 1 time" or "Viewed 3 times" (the number replaces the braces). How many times the link has been opened, including this view. Acknowledge Reviewed The button that records your review. Thanks, this review has been recorded. Shown in place of the button after you acknowledge. Toolbar Button What it does Acknowledge Reviewed Records that you reviewed the alert, with the time. The laboratory sees it on the Critical Alerts tab. Icons and status indicators Indicator Meaning Green Active badge The link is valid now. Expired badge The link's time has passed. Green tick with the thank you text The review has been recorded. Hotkeys None. Step by Step Procedures Standard workflow For the physician 1. Open the link in the secure email or text. The page says "Loading..." and then shows the reference card. 2. Check the accession number and your name against what you expect. 3. Obtain the result itself from the laboratory or the hospital record. The page does not show it. 4. Select Acknowledge Reviewed . A green tick and "Thanks, this review has been recorded." replace the button. For the laboratory 1. Open the Audit Log and choose the Critical Alerts tab. 2. Find the case, using Filter by case if needed. 3. Read the Channels column to see how it was sent, the Reference Link column to see whether it is Active or Expired and how often it was viewed, and the Acknowledged column for the time of acknowledgement, or "Not yet acknowledged". 4. If an alert is not acknowledged within your laboratory's expected time, contact the physician directly and record the call as your procedure requires. Alternative workflow 1. An alert sent only by EHR inbox push has no reference link. The Critical Alerts tab says "No reference link (EHR push only)". 2. If no channel could be resolved (for example no contact details), the tab says "No channel could be resolved". Notify the physician by telephone. 3. Reopening a link after acknowledging shows the confirmation instead of the button, as long as the link has not expired. Exception handling 1. The link is invalid or expired. The page says "This link is invalid or no longer active. It may have expired or never existed. Contact the laboratory directly for this result." It does not say which. Do not wait: call the laboratory. 2. You opened the link on a shared device. The page shows an accession number and a physician name only. Close the tab. 3. The link was sent to the wrong person. Tell the laboratory. The Audit Log shows how many times it was viewed. Error recovery 1. If the page stays on "Loading...", check your connection and reopen the link. 2. If Acknowledge Reviewed seems to do nothing, wait a moment and look for the green tick. If it is still not there, reload; if the button returns, select it again. 3. If you acknowledged the wrong alert, tell the laboratory. The acknowledgement cannot be undone from the page. warning "Acknowledging is not receiving the result" Acknowledge Reviewed records that you opened the reference. It does not carry the finding. Never treat an acknowledgement as the clinical handover; the pathologist's recorded verbal notification is the handover. Tips and Best Practices Common mistakes Looking on the page for the finding. title: Cytology Worklist
headings: Peer-review queue views (Cytology QC and Surgical QA)
text: Cytology Worklist { top} Overview Purpose. The Cytology Worklist is the cytotechnologist's list of work. It shows the cases assigned to you, the shared pool you can claim from, the shared queue of slides waiting for a QC rescreen, the cases waiting for an HPV result, and a row of quality and compliance lists (recall, CSMS eligibility, the 5 year lookback, peer review, histology correlation, follow up due and completed scans). You open a case from here to screen it on the Screening Case page. This article also describes the two peer review queues that open inside the main Worklist: Cytology QC Peer Review Queue and Surgical Post Sign Out QA . See "Peer review queue views" below. Intended users. Cytotechnologists work from this page every day. Pathologists and fellows use it to see cytology cases and the quality lists, and the QC and QA queue views are for pathologists and quality staff. What you can open depends on your role: if the Cytology Workspace tile is missing from the Pathology Workspace, ask your laboratory manager. Where it fits. A cytology specimen is accessioned, prepared and (for a digital laboratory) scanned. It then appears here: on My Worklist if it was assigned to you, or in the Pool if nobody has taken it. After you screen it, the case moves on to QC rescreen, pathologist review and sign out, all on the Screening Case page. The quality lists on this page collect the cases that need a later quality step, such as a 5 year retrospective review or a histology correlation. Screen Tour The page has, from top to bottom: the title Cytology Worklist and a one line summary; the GYN Cytology / Non GYN / FNA Queue switch; organ site chips (Non GYN only); your workload counter and screening hours panel (for those who screen); the main tiles; the QA & Compliance tiles; and the list for the tile you selected. note "Two names for one place" The page title says Cytology Worklist. The breadcrumb at the top and the tile in the Pathology Workspace say Cytology Workspace. They are the same place. note "Demonstration data today" The lists are built from the demonstration cases and the demonstration settings. The molecular platform, the registers and the scanner are not connected to a real site yet, so results and scans that would arrive from them are either demonstration data or entered by hand (see "Record an HPV result by hand"). Field definitions The switch Item What it means GYN Cytology Cervical and vaginal screening cases (Pap, liquid based cytology). This is the default. Non GYN / FNA Queue Fluids, washings and fine needle aspirations. A lab may instead send non GYN cytology to the surgical pathology worklist; your laboratory manager sets that, and then those cases do not appear here. Changing the switch returns you to My Worklist and clears any organ site chip. Organ site chips (Non GYN only) Chip What it means All Sites No narrowing. Body Fluids/Washings, Breast, GI/Pancreatic, Lung/EBUS, Salivary Gland, Thyroid, Urine/Paris System, Other Narrows the list to one site. A chip appears only when at least one of your lab's Non GYN cases is at that site right now. Main tiles for GYN Cytology Tile What it lists My Worklist Cases assigned to you that are ready to screen. Pool Cases nobody has taken yet. You claim one to make it yours. QC / Rescreen Every GYN slide that was flagged for a mandatory QC rescreen and has not had that rescreen yet. It is one shared queue, not assigned to a person. HPV Triage Cases that wait for a primary high risk HPV result before any slide is screened (only in labs that screen by HPV first, then reflex to cytology). Main tiles for Non GYN / FNA Tile What it lists My Worklist Cases assigned to you. Unassigned Pool Cases nobody has taken yet. Cell Block / Ancillary Pending Specimens with a cell block or residual fluid whose stain orders are not finished. ROSE / Bedside Evaluations Specimens with a recent rapid on site evaluation on record. My Worklist and Pool do not repeat a case that already sits on a quality tile below. A case with a QC flag, for example, is on QC / Rescreen and not in My Worklist. QA & Compliance tiles (both switches) These tiles span GYN and Non GYN. The switch and the organ site chips do not narrow them. Tile What it lists Recall Needed A self collected HPV test came back positive (or invalid) and the programme asks for a clinician collected sample (Australia and New Zealand rules). CSMS QA Cases sent to England's cervical screening register that still need an eligibility answer. 5 Year Lookback Earlier negative results of a patient who now has a high grade or malignant diagnosis, waiting for a retrospective review. Peer Review Signed out cases picked for post sign out peer review. Histology Correlation Abnormal cytology for which a later biopsy was found and needs a cyto histologic correlation. Follow up Due Abnormal results whose histology follow up is due soon or overdue. Scans Completed Cases whose whole slide scan is complete and that are waiting to be screened. Each tile shows a count. The count is the number of rows in its list. A row in the list Item What it means Patient name Select it to open the case on the Screening Case page. Rows on the Pool tile are not openable: claim the case first. If the name is missing, the MRN or "Unknown patient" is shown. Case line "Case S26 5002 · MRN 100002" (demonstration values): the case number and the MRN. Final Diagnosis Recorded / Awaiting Review Green when a specimen on the case already has its final diagnosis chosen; amber otherwise. High Risk QC / Random QC On the QC / Rescreen tile: why the slide was picked. Your primary screen needs another screener On the QC / Rescreen tile: you did the first screen, so another screener must do the rescreen. AI: Review / AI: No Further Review (with a rank such as 2/5) The result of the slide level AI triage, when one has been completed. It is advice only.
