title: Screening Case
text: Screening Case { top} Overview Purpose. The Screening Case page is where one cytology specimen is screened, reviewed and signed out. You enter your finding in the lab's reporting system (Bethesda, the UK BSCC/RCPath terms, the German München III groups, the French SFCC wording, or the Dutch CISOE A six axis score), see the earlier reviews, the HPV result and the patient's history, take part in QC and peer review, and finally sign the report out. Intended users. Cytotechnologists record the first screen and QC rescreens. Pathologists and fellows review, choose the final diagnosis and sign out whatever a cytotechnologist may not sign out. The page works out your part in the case by itself. Where it fits. You get here by selecting a case on the Cytology Worklist (or, as a pathologist, from the Cytology Review tile in the Worklist). After sign out, the report is released (see Sign out and release). The cases that need a later quality step then show on the QA & Compliance tiles of the Cytology Worklist. note "Orchestration cases only" The page works only for cases that PathScribe manages itself. A case managed by an outside laboratory system shows "This case is managed by an external LIS (assist mode)..." and a Back to Worklist button. A case with no cytology specimen shows "No qualifying cytology specimen found on this case." Screen Tour The page has a header (case, patient and a row of buttons), several bars and banners that appear only when they apply, and two columns. The left column holds context: your role, the workload, Mandatory QC, HPV, patient history and the review history. The right column holds the form where you record your review. note "Demonstration data today" The HPV results, scans and AI triage come from the demonstration cases. The molecular platform, the registers and the scanner are not connected to a real site yet. The sample dictionary shown here is the demonstration dictionary; your laboratory manager sets the real one. Field definitions Header Item What it means Case number The case reference. Patient name, MRN The patient. A badge shows the patient's registry opt outs when there are any. LMP Last menstrual period. Type or pick a date; it saves when you leave the box. Required (marked ) on a GYN specimen if your laboratory requires it for the review. Specimen tabs When the case has more than one cytology specimen, a tab for each appears ("Specimen A" and its description) with its status: Draft, Revision requested or Signed out. Each specimen is reviewed and signed out on its own. " N of M specimens signed out" shows the progress. The case report goes out when the last specimen is signed (see "Finalize the case early" below). Left column Card What it shows Your Role for This Review Your role, set automatically. See the table of roles below. "Determined automatically from review history and your account role." If you already reviewed the case it says "You already reviewed this case editing your own review below." Review Mode (cytotechnologists only) How you screened this pass, which sets the weight toward your workload limit: Full Manual Screen (1.0 SCU), Liquid Based Non Gyn (0.5 SCU), FOV Assisted, No Rescreen (0.5 SCU), FOV + Full Manual Rescreen (1.5 SCU). A pathologist's review does not count toward the limit. The small hint beside the title reads "(CLIA workload weight)". Your workload (last 24 hours) The same counter as on the worklist, and a banner when you approach or reach the limit. Mandatory QC Whether the specimen is flagged for QC (see "QC rescreen"). HPV Co Testing The HPV result that arrived from the molecular platform. Read only; the hint beside the title says "(upstream molecular result — read only)". It lists "Co test ordered" (Yes or No), the reason, the result and its flag, the "Reference range" the laboratory sent, and the "Genotype" (for example 16 or 18). When no result has arrived it says so. Liquid based platform, HPV assay (name), Action on the positive HPV result Details you can record. See "HPV and reflex testing". When the action is Colposcopy referral, two dates appear: Referred on and Response received on . The UK failsafe report counts the referral and flags it if no response is recorded after 28 days. Patient Cyto/Histo History The hint beside the title reads "(prior cases for this patient)". Two lists: "Prior Pap Smears" with the final result (a smear that was never finalized reads "no final diagnosis on record"), and "Prior Surgical Biopsies", each biopsy with a View Case button. 5 Year Retrospective Lookback Shown when the diagnosis you are entering is high grade: the patient's earlier negative or low grade Paps in the last five years, with View Case . Review History Every review recorded on this specimen, newest information in each card (see below). Before anyone has saved a review it reads "No reviews recorded yet." Roles the page assigns Role shown When Primary Screener You are not a pathologist and nobody has reviewed this specimen yet. Secondary Reviewer You are not a pathologist and a review already exists. QC Random Selection / QC Targeted High Risk The specimen carries a QC flag that no matching rescreen has cleared. Pathologist Review You are a pathologist. Post Sign Out Peer Review Random Selection / Targeted High Risk You are a pathologist other than the signer, and the signed out specimen was picked for peer review. A card in Review History Item What it means Badge INITIAL REVIEW or the role The type of review. FINAL DIAGNOSIS The review chosen as the final diagnosis. CT ELIGIBLE / PATHOLOGIST REQUIRED Whether a cytotechnologist may sign out on this review. Hover to see the reasons. Name and date Who recorded it and when. Adequacy, General Categorization, Primary, Additional, Recommendations The review's content. Agreement with the initial review On every later review: exact, minor discrepancy or major discrepancy (with false negative, false positive or high grade skip), and "Adequacy differs from the initial review." text: Demonstration Tools { top} Overview Purpose. Two pages exist so PathScribe can be shown and taught without the hospital systems it normally talks to. Mock EMR stands in for the hospital's patient record, and Mock Interface Engine stands in for the interface engine that carries messages between PathScribe and other systems. warning "These are not production screens" Nothing on these pages is real clinical information or a real connection. The Mock EMR shows made up clinical details. The Mock Interface Engine answers messages that no real system received. They appear only in demonstration and training installations. In a production installation connected to a PathScribe server, neither page is there. Never use either to look up or decide anything about a real patient. Intended users. Trainers, laboratory managers and administrators running a demonstration or a training session. Pathologists see the Mock EMR only when they press the EMR button on a report in a demonstration installation. Where it fits. The Mock EMR opens from the report screen. The Mock Interface Engine is not linked from any menu or tile; it is opened by typing its address, , and it needs Configuration access. title: External Consult
headings: The External Consult Access window (for the person who issues links)
text: External Consult { top} Overview Purpose. An external consult link lets a pathologist outside your laboratory look at the case, or some of its slides, and send back an opinion, without a PathScribe account. This article describes the page the outside consultant opens. It is also for the pathologist or manager who sends the link, so they know what the recipient will see. Intended users. The outside consultant who receives a link. The ordering pathologist and laboratory manager, who issue links and track them. Where it fits. The ordering pathologist issues a link from the case (External Consult Access on the case) and sends it to the consultant by whatever channel the laboratory uses. The consultant opens it, reads the specimens and slides in scope, and submits an opinion. The ordering pathologist then sees the opinion on the case and records how it compares with the report. Every link, its status and its views are listed on the Consult links tab of the Audit Log, where it can be revoked. warning "Demonstration links only today" The page itself says so in a banner: "Demo link: no PathScribe server checks it yet. It opens only in the browser that issued it. Its token is random and kept only as a fingerprint." Until PathScribe's server serves consult links, a link works only in the browser where it was issued. Do not send a link to a real outside party as if it were production. warning "The page masks the patient by default" Unless the person who issued the link ticked the opt in, the consultant sees the accession number and a masked identity: initials with the rest hidden (for example J S ) and the date of birth as the year only ( 1980). The full name and date of birth are not on the page at all, not merely hidden. The link is still the only protection: anyone who has it can open it, and there is no passcode or identity check yet (Planned, needs the server). Send it through a channel you would use for patient information, and revoke it when it is no longer needed. info "Dates of birth are always written DD MMM YYYY" When the full identity is shown, the date of birth appears as day, three letter English month in capitals, and year (for example 24 OCT 1980), in every language and country. The masked form keeps the same style ( 1980). This is the one place PathScribe does not follow the reader's own date format: laboratory dates must not be ambiguous (03/04/1980 means different days in different countries). Other dates on the page, such as when the link expires, still follow the reader's format. Screen Tour The page is a single dark card with a banner across the top, the case, the specimens and slides, and the opinion form. There is no menu and no sign in. Field definitions Field What it means Banner The Demo link notice (see above). PathScribe External Consult The heading line. Accession number The laboratory's number for the case. Patient line Masked by default: first letters only (J S ) and "DOB 1980" (the year alone), with a note saying the identity is masked. When the issuer opted in: "Last, First" and "DOB 24 OCT 1980" (always day, English month, year). Expiry banner Appears only after a Signed opinion is in: "This secure link will expire in 2 views or 46 hours, whichever comes first." The numbers are worked out by the server each time the page opens. Scope line "Full case access" or "Scoped access" with the number of slides, then "Link expires (date and time)" in the reader's own date format. Specimens & Slides Each specimen as "label, description", and the slides the link covers. "No slides in scope for this link." if there are none. Your Opinion The form, or a confirmation once an opinion is in. Diagnostic Category (optional) Free text. The hint in the box reads "e.g. Benign, Malignant, Indeterminate". Status Draft or Signed . Opinion text The box with the grey prompt "Enter your diagnostic impression / opinion...". Required. On the laboratory's side, issuing a link asks for a consultant name or identifier, an optional organization, the access scope (Full Case or Specific Slides) and an optional internal note that the consultant never sees. The default lifetime is 24 hours, or 72 hours if that period would span a weekend. The External Consult Access window (for the person who issues links) The ordering pathologist opens this window from the case. It is headed "External Consult / Second Opinion" and titled External Consult Access . A red banner repeats that links are demonstration only today. Item What it means + Issue New Consult Link Opens the form for a new link. Needs the permission to issue links. Without it the button is greyed out and its tooltip reads "Requires permission to issue consult links." Shows the patient's name and date of birth on screen, for review only; nothing is sent to the consultant. Each use is recorded in the audit log. Each link The consultant's name and organisation, "Full case" or the number of slides, "Issued" and "Expires" times, a status (Active, Expired or Revoked) and Revoke while the link is active. title: Facility Operations Display
headings: The five views, and how the numbers are worked out
text: Facility Operations Display { top} Overview Purpose. The Facility Operations display is a wall screen for a laboratory bench or room. It shows, in large high contrast type, what is waiting and what is late in one department: Grossing and Intake, Embedding and Microtomy, Staining and IHC, Send Out and Reference Laboratory, or Diagnostic Sign Out and Scanner. A display can rotate through several of these views by itself. Intended users. Everyone who works in or walks past the area. The screen is read only for the people watching. It has nothing to click once it is running. An administrator sets it up once. Where it fits. The numbers come from the same batches, cases and scan runs that staff work in Batch Management, the Pathology Workspace and the other bench screens. Nothing is entered here. The display does not use anyone's sign in, so it carries no patient names or MRNs: only batch barcodes, accession numbers and counts. note "What the display needs" A display is bound to a Display Profile (which facility, which views, how fast they rotate) and needs a Display Token that an administrator issued for it. Without them it cannot start. Display Profiles and tokens are set up in Configuration, System, Display Profiles (see the Administrator Guide). The administrator's page has an Open Facility Ops Dashboard button; a bench screen can also simply be pointed at the page address. note "Demonstration data today" In the demonstration build the figures come from the demonstration batches, cases, referrals and scan runs held in the browser. The "Offline / Stale Data" badge reports on the screen's own refresh, not on any real instrument. The check on the Display Token is made in the browser; the server side check (refusing a revoked token on the server) is planned and not built. Screen Tour Field definitions First start (setup). The first time a display opens, it shows Bind This Display with the line "Select the Display Profile this wall unit should show." and a list headed "— select display profile —". After you choose one, Enter Display Token asks for the token ("Enter the Display Token an administrator issued for "<name " to start this display.") with Back and Confirm . If no profile has been set up the screen says "No display profiles are configured yet. Add one under Config → System → Display Profiles." If the token is wrong, expired or revoked, the display says so ("That Display Token is not valid for this display. Check it and try again.", "This display's token has expired. Ask an administrator to issue a new one.", "This display's token has been revoked. Ask an administrator to issue a new one.", or "No Display Token has been issued for this display. Ask an administrator."). A display that loses its token goes blank with Display unavailable and a button Enter a new token . The display checks its token again about every minute while it is running, so a revoked token blanks the screen within a minute. Header. The profile name, the title of the view being shown, the facility name, a live clock, a status note and, when the profile has more than one view, a row of dots marking which view is on screen. Item What it means Profile name (small, top) The display profile this unit is bound to. View title One of the five views. Clock The time on this unit, in your language's format. "Updated hh:mm:ss" When the figures last refreshed successfully. Offline / Stale Data The last refresh failed or the data is older than expected (see "Icons and status indicators"). Dots The views in the profile; the filled one is on screen. Stat tiles. A row of large numbers. A tile turns amber (warning) or red (overdue) when its state says so. Alerts. Rows under the tiles, each with a short kind label, a title and a detail. Critical alerts and warnings are styled differently. Queue. The list of items in the department, oldest first. Each row shows a label and detail, a STAT tag for urgent items, and on the right either a countdown or an age ("2h 10m ago"). "Nothing in queue right now." shows when the list is empty. A countdown row is tinted amber when 30 minutes or fewer remain and red once overdue ("Overdue 1h 5m"). The five views, and how the numbers are worked out All views are filtered to the profile's facility. A batch belongs to a facility through its case's accession number or the workstation it was made on. Grossing and Intake Tile or list Meaning Pending Intake Specimens or materials in the pending load queue, awaiting intake. Red if any is STAT. STAT Pending Pending items whose case is STAT. Decal / Special Processing Active batches at the decalcification or special processing step. Processing Batches Active batches at the Processing step. Alerts One critical STAT alert per pending STAT specimen, and a critical Decal Overdue alert per overdue decalcification batch. Queue Active batches at decal, processing or checkout, oldest first. A decalcification batch with a target time counts down; others show their age. Embedding and Microtomy Tile Meaning Embedding Batches Active batches at the Embedding step. Microtomy Batches Active batches at the Microtomy / Sectioning step. STAT Batches Active batches marked STAT (red when any). Cassettes/Slides In Process Total items in those batches. Alerts and queue A critical STAT alert for each STAT batch; the queue lists the batches by age. Staining and IHC Tile Meaning Active Staining Batches / Cytology Staining Batches Active batches at those two steps. Slides In Staining Stains whose status is Staining. Ready for Review Stains whose status is Ready for Review. Recut Requested Stains with a recut requested (amber when any). QC Failed Stains whose QC failed (red when any). Alerts Critical QC Failed and warning Recut Requested alerts with the accession number, block and stain name; critical STAT alerts for STAT batches. title: Grossing
text: Grossing { top} Overview Purpose. The Grossing screen is where the person cutting up a case records the physical work: which blocks (cassettes) each specimen produced and how many pieces are in each, the stains ordered on each block, how long the tissue was in fixative, the margins and the ink used on them, and then marks the case as grossed. It works from the protocol attached to each specimen, so the blocks and stains a protocol calls for appear ready for you to adjust. Intended users. Pathology assistants and pathologists who gross specimens. By default pathologists, fellows, residents and pathology assistants may complete grossing. If a button is greyed out, your role must allow it; ask your manager. Where it fits. Grossing comes after the case has been logged in Accession and before the tissue goes on to processing, embedding and cutting at the stations under Pathology Workspace. Completing grossing moves the case to Gross Complete, and the case can then be sent to a pathologist pool. note "How you reach this screen" There is no tile for Grossing on Home. Open the case on the report screen, select the Material tab, and choose Open Grossing Screen . Back to Case returns you to the report screen. Screen Tour The title reads "Grossing" followed by the accession number. Under it are the clinical history bar, the Complete grossing bar, and then one section for each specimen in the case. Work is saved as you go, except where a button says otherwise. note "Work done on other screens" This screen does not print cassette or slide labels, does not hold the triage checklist and does not take photos. Releasing and printing the cassettes, the triage checklist that must be confirmed before they are released, and the printed labels are on the report screen's Material tab. Gross description text is written on the report screen too. Photos taken during an intraoperative consultation are in the Intraop Queue. Block face photos are taken from the block editor on the report screen's Material tab, in a window headed "Capture Block Face Photo". Under a block's piece count or piece description the editor shows "Needed before grossing can be completed." when your laboratory requires the item. Field definitions Field What it means Specimen A, description The specimen's label and description from accessioning. Protocol: … (v…) The grossing protocol attached to the specimen and its version, for example "Protocol: Breast core (v2)". Protocol Modified A badge shown when you have changed what the protocol produced (for example by adding a stain). No protocol assigned The specimen has no protocol. You cannot add blocks from this screen. Fixation ended The time the tissue left fixative. Shows "Record now" until recorded. Fixative to tissue ratio Your confirmation that the ratio was adequate. Shows "Confirm adequate ratio" until confirmed, then who confirmed it and when. Block ID The specimen letter and block, for example A1. Piece Count The number of tissue pieces in the block. Starts from the protocol's default. Stains The stains ordered on the block. Each is tagged Auto generated (from the protocol) or User added. Status Where the block is. Only a block that is still Pending can be removed. Slide ID, Stain, Imager Batch, FOV Count For cytology preparations only. Imager Batch shows "Not yet imaged" until the slide has been imaged. Margins & Ink Applications The margins recorded on the specimen or on a block: name, orientation, laterality, Examined or Pending, and each ink applied with who applied it and when. They are grouped under "On specimen" and "On block …" (for example "On block A1"). Until one is recorded the section says "No margins recorded yet." Audit Trail (n overrides) A collapsible list of changes you made to what the protocol produced: piece counts changed, stains added, protocol stains removed. When there are none it says "No overrides recorded." Toolbar Button What it does Back to Case Returns to the case on the report screen. Complete grossing Marks grossing finished and moves the case to Gross Complete. Greyed out while required items are missing. Record now Records the current time as the end of fixation. Add Stain Opens a list of the stains allowed for that block, which starts at "— select stain —"; choose one and select Add . x beside a stain Removes the stain. Hover text: "Remove stain". Add margin / Add ink application Records a margin, or a further ink on an existing margin. The margin form starts with a list "Attach to: specimen" or "Attach to: block …" (for example "Attach to: block A1"), then boxes prompting "Margin name (e.g. Lateral, Deep)", "Orientation (optional)" and "Laterality (optional)", and an ink list that starts at "Select ink color". Audit Trail Opens or closes the list of overrides for the specimen. Icons and status indicators Indicator Meaning Grossing completed (with a tick) Grossing has been completed for this case. This case is past grossing. The case has moved beyond the stage where grossing can be completed. Highlighted block row The block was changed from the protocol. Auto generated / User added Whether a stain came from the protocol or you added it. Examined / Pending Whether a margin has been examined. Deficiency raised A fixation deficiency is already open for the specimen. Note under the Complete grossing button "Still required" lists what is missing and where, for example "Piece count (A2)". You can also say "complete grossing", "finish grossing" or "grossing done". Alt+Shift+F10 Confirm completing

title: Home Dashboard
text: Home Dashboard { top} Overview Purpose. The Home Dashboard is the first screen after you sign in. It is a set of tiles, one for each part of PathScribe you are allowed to use. Choose a tile to open that part of the system. Intended users. Everyone who signs in. What you see depends on your role. Where it fits. Home is the starting point of every workflow. From here you go to Accession to log a new specimen, to the Worklist to continue your cases, or to any other area your laboratory has given you. Screen Tour note "You only see your own tiles" A tile appears only if your role may open that area. A colleague with a different role will see a different set. If a tile you expect is missing, ask your laboratory manager to check your access. Field definitions Item What it means Welcome back, name Greets you by your family name. Tiles One per area of PathScribe. Each has a title and a one line description. Registry exception count A small count on the tile that leads to registry exceptions, shown when cancer registry submissions need a person to look at them. Latest research article A line showing a recent pathology article chosen for your subspecialty. Select it to read it in a separate window. System status At the bottom of the screen. It says "Checking" while PathScribe asks the server, then "Operational", "Degraded" or "Unavailable". If the check itself fails it says "Status unavailable", which means the status is not known, not that the system is fine. It is checked when Home opens and again when you return to the tab after five minutes. In a demo with no server it adds "(demo: simulated)". Beside it is the line "© 2026 PathScribe AI Systems". Tile descriptions. The My Contribution tile reads "Workload • Quality • TAT • Trends". The Search tile reads "Search completed and in progress cases". From PubMed. The small badge on the research article line. The dot beside it is a button: its tooltip is "Click to check for a more recent article", and while it works it says "Checking for a more recent article…". Toolbar The Home Dashboard has no toolbar of its own. Icons and status indicators Indicator Meaning Tile highlight when you point at it The tile you are about to open. Number on a tile Items on that tile that need someone's attention (for example registry exceptions). Green dot, "Operational" The server reports that every part it checks is working. Amber dot, "Degraded" The server reports a part is working below normal. Tell your administrator if it persists. Red dot, "Unavailable" The server reports a part is not working. Empty circle, "Status unavailable" The check did not get an answer, so the status is not known. Hotkeys None are specific to this screen. Alt+H (Go Home) returns you here from most screens, and Alt+J then H works from every screen. F1 (View Help) opens the guide page for the screen you are on. The Help button does the same. The tiles Tile What you do there Guide Accession Log new specimens and assign grossing templates. Accession Worklist View and manage pending pathology cases. Worklist Bench Contributions See accessioning rate, batch throughput, queue aging, stage to stage turnaround time and molecular quality control for bench roles. Bench Contributions Configuration System settings and AI preferences (administrators). Administrator Guide Intraop Queue Match unlinked intraoperative entries to a formal accession. Step by Step Procedures Standard workflow 1. Sign in. The Home Dashboard opens. 2. Find the tile for the work you want to do. 3. Select the tile. The screen for that area opens. 4. When you finish, return to Home with Alt+H (or Alt+J then H). Alternative workflow 1. Select the round ? Help button in the top bar, beside the microphone (or press F1) to open the guide page for the screen you are on. 2. To reach a case without Home, use the Search screen. Exception handling 1. If a tile you expect is missing, your role does not include that area. Tell your laboratory manager which tile you need and why. 2. If tiles are missing after a refresh, sign out and sign in again. Tips and Best Practices Common mistakes Looking for Configuration on a tile when your role does not include it. Configuration is for administrators. Using Home for every move. Once you know the screen, the keyboard shortcuts are faster. Efficiency recommendations Accession and Worklist are always shown first because they are used most. Use the latest research line to keep up with your subspecialty during quiet moments. Workflow recommendations Start the day at the Worklist, then work through your cases. text: Intraop Queue { top} Overview Purpose. The Intraop Queue is where an intraoperative consultation (a frozen section) is recorded before the formal case exists. You identify the patient, record the operating room and surgeon once, then record each specimen: its quick gross description, the touch prep and frozen block work, the frozen section diagnosis and the verbal report given to the surgical team. Entries that have no formal case yet wait in a list until someone merges them into the accession. Intended users. Pathologists and other staff at the bench or in the operating room corridor (the screen works on a phone browser as well as on a desktop). Accessioners and pathologists use the same screen to match a waiting entry to its case. What you can open depends on your role; if the Intraop Queue tile is missing from Home, ask your laboratory manager. Where it fits. The frozen section usually happens before the specimen reaches the laboratory for formal accessioning. Record it here first. When the formal case is logged in Accession, PathScribe looks for a waiting entry that belongs to it and offers the merge there. You can also merge from this screen. The frozen results then travel with the case that you report in the report screen. Screen Tour The screen has two halves. The top is the form for a new entry. Below it is the log of entries that are still unlinked ("Pending Match"). note "Demonstration data today" The patient lookup (ADT) uses a small set of demonstration records, and the "Simulate scan (no camera)" link invents a number. Try the lookup with MRN 12345 to see a matched patient; any other number gives "No ADT match" and you type the name and date of birth yourself. text: Lockbox Drop Off { top} Overview Purpose. Lockbox Drop Off records specimens that arrive in the laboratory lockbox outside staffed hours. Whoever collects the containers scans each barcode, and PathScribe writes a permanent "Received in Lockbox" receipt with the time and the name of the person who scanned. The morning team then works from the Overnight folder , which lists everything received but not yet accessioned. Intended users. Accessioners, histotechnologists and laboratory managers. Scanning a container needs one permission and working the Overnight folder needs another, so your role decides which parts you see. Where it fits. The lockbox sits before Accession. A container scanned here is only received . Nothing is accessioned and no accession number is made until the morning team logs the case on the Accession screen. note "Demonstration data today" In this version the receipts, the pending orders that barcodes are matched against, and the "server time" all come from demonstration data held in your browser session. The time stamped on a receipt is your device's clock, and the name is the person signed in. A device bound kiosk sign in (a screen that stays signed in for the lockbox) is not built yet. Resetting the demonstration restores a fresh set of example receipts. Screen Tour The screen is titled Lockbox Drop Off , with the line "Scan each container that arrives in the lockbox. title: Margin Exception Review
text: Margin Exception Review { top} Overview Purpose. When a pathologist types a margin distance in words into a synoptic report field (for example "close to the inked edge" instead of "2 mm"), PathScribe tries to read a number from it. Where it cannot do so with confidence, it does not guess. The answer goes into this review list so that a person can either type in the real distance in millimetres ( Resolve ) or close the item with a reason ( Dismiss ). The number matters because laboratories can set rules that send a case to a tumor board when a margin is closer than a set distance. Intended users. Pathologists, fellows, residents and pathology assistants. These are the roles that have the screen and the permission to resolve exceptions by default. Resolving is a clinical judgment about what the pathologist's words mean, so the buttons are greyed out for anyone without that permission. Where it fits. Items arrive in this list after a case is signed out, one for each margin distance answer that could not be read. The case's report stays as written. The number you record here is kept separately, out of sight of the report, and is the value the tumor board rules use. See Tumor Board. The screen is one of the tiles in the Pathology Workspace. note "What is and is not changed" Resolving or dismissing never changes the text of the report. It records a hidden number (or a reason for having none) beside the answer, writes an entry in the audit log, and then checks the tumor board rules again for that case straight away. If the number you recorded trips a rule, the case is flagged for that board at once and the screen says so. Screen Tour The screen is titled Margin Exception Review . Under the title: "Margin distance free text answers the extraction layer couldn't confidently parse into a number. Tag the real distance, or dismiss with a reason." Below is a list with one row for each pending item. When none are waiting the list reads "No pending margin distance exceptions." Under it, a second list titled Resolved and dismissed shows what has already been decided (see below). Field definitions Each row shows the following. Part What it means Patient and accession The patient's name and the case number. If the case cannot be found the case identifier is shown instead. Field name The name of the report field the answer was typed into, for example the distance to the closest margin. What was typed The exact text the pathologist entered. Reason Why it could not be read: "No answer given yet", "No number found in the text", or "A number was found, but surrounded by text this parser doesn't trust". Margin distance (mm) A number box, labelled "mm", where you type the real distance. Zero or more, in steps of 0.1. How the system reads an answer. PathScribe looks only at free text fields whose names end in a unit of millimetres or centimetres. It accepts a number with its unit ("2mm", "0.5 cm", "<1 mm") and converts centimetres to millimetres. A bare number ("2") is read in the unit the field is named for. Anything else is sent here: no number at all ("cannot be assessed"), or a number in a sentence with other words besides a few plain ones such as "approximately" or "from the margin". Examples (demonstration wording). Typed in the field What PathScribe does 2mm Reads 2 mm. Not listed here. 0.5 cm Reads 5 mm. Not listed here. <1 mm Reads "less than 1 mm". Not listed here. approximately 2 mm from the margin Reads 2 mm: a few plain filler words such as "approximately", "from the margin" are allowed. Not listed here. 2 (field name ends in mm) Reads 2 mm. Not listed here. cannot be assessed No number found in the text. Listed for review. 2 mm from the deep margin, 5 mm from the lateral margin A number surrounded by other text. Listed for review. (field left empty) Nothing is read and nothing is listed. Toolbar Button What it does Resolve Saves the number in the mm box as the margin distance for that field, moves the item to Resolved and dismissed , writes an audit log entry, and checks the tumor board rules again for the case. Dismiss Opens the window Dismiss exception : type why the field has no distance to give (for example the margin could not be assessed), then select Dismiss . The item moves to Resolved and dismissed , no number is recorded, an audit log entry is written, and the tumor board rules are checked again for the case. Cancel closes the window. Open Case Opens the case's full report page so you can read the answer in context. Its back control returns to this list. Resolve and Dismiss are greyed out for a person without the permission to resolve margin distance exceptions. Open Case is available to anyone who can open this screen. title: Messaging
text: Messaging { top} Overview Purpose. Messaging is PathScribe's built in way to talk to colleagues without leaving the case. It holds your inbox, lets you write a new internal message or reply to one, and lets you send a secure email to someone outside your organisation. It is also where PathScribe delivers notices about your work: a follow up that is overdue, a report that could not be delivered, an access request waiting for you, a case corrected in the laboratory system. Intended users. Everyone who signs in. Reading messages needs no special permission. Sending a message or a reply ("Send a message or reply") and sending a secure email ("Send a secure email") are two separate permissions. Most roles have both by default, and your administrator can change that. Without the permission the Send button is grey and a line under the form says so; you can still read everything. Where it fits. Messaging is not a page of its own. It is a panel that slides in over whatever screen you are on, opened from the speech bubble button in the top bar (or with Alt+I). Close it and you are back exactly where you were. A message that mentions a case gives you a link that opens that case; from the case you can return to the panel with one click. note "Demonstration data today" In this version the people you can message come from a small demonstration list of staff and departments (for example Lab Manager, System Admin, QA Team, Billing Dept). Messages are kept in the browser. Secure email is Simulated : the window works from start to finish, but no gateway is connected, so nothing is delivered and the window says so. After a send, the window also shows "This message is recorded in the audit log." once the Audit Log entry has been written. Screen Tour The panel has a top bar, a list of messages on the left and the open conversation (or the new message form) on the right. On a phone sized window only one side shows at a time and a back arrow at the top returns you to the list. A reply does not change it; open the conversation to read the replies. A reply, sent or received, moves the conversation to the top of the list (urgent conversations stay first). Time Today's messages show the time of day, yesterday's say "Yesterday", the past week shows the weekday, older ones the date (with the year once it is over a year old). Blue dot The message is unread for you. A message you wrote, or a conversation where your reply is the latest, never shows a dot to you. Urgent pill The message was marked Urgent. Urgent messages sort to the top; within each group the newest comes first. Search box Filters the list by the sender's name or the message text. It does not search the subject line. Open conversation (right) Item What it means Name and Urgent badge Who the message is with, and whether it is urgent. Subject The subject of the conversation. Case link ("Case" plus the number) Opens that case. Shown when the message belongs to a case, and for case numbers PathScribe finds written in the subject or text (only for cases you are allowed to open). Tick the people you want. The button at the foot reads Add recipients (greyed) until you tick someone, then Add 1 recipient , Add 2 recipients and so on. "No users found." means nothing matches what you typed. Type your message here… is the hint inside the empty message box of a new message. Send as secure external email is the tooltip of the Secure Email button. It is greyed until the message can be sent that way. Synoptic Template Request is the title of the banner on a message that asks for a new synoptic template. Open configuration page is the tooltip of Open Configuration on a system notice. Back to message list is the arrow shown on a narrow screen to leave an open message and return to the list. Permanently Delete Messages. In Edit mode, Delete on ticked messages asks this question first. It says how many messages will be removed and that this cannot be undone. Confirm with Delete or cancel.
