title: Migration Jobs
text: Migration Jobs { top} Overview Purpose. Migration Jobs is where records from a laboratory's old information system are brought into PathScribe, and where you check how each import went. Every import is a job. The screen lists the jobs, shows how many records succeeded, failed or need review, and checks the count against the number the old system claimed. Intended users. Laboratory managers and administrators who convert historical data. The screen needs Configuration access. The Import legacy file button also needs the permission to manage migration mappings. Where it fits. Before any import, an administrator sets up field mappings for the old system under Configuration (Migration field mappings): which old field name becomes which PathScribe field. You then import a file here. Records that succeed can become draft cases. Records whose patient cannot be matched with certainty are sent to the Patient Match Review queue rather than guessed. warning "This import is a simulation today" The import runs in your browser as a demonstration. The screen says so in a banner: "Simulated bulk import. Records are mapped, validated and matched to patients here in the browser, and records that succeed become draft cases marked Simulated. A server side bulk import replaces this. The file itself is not kept." Do not use it as the real conversion of a laboratory's history. note "No link leads here" No button or tile in PathScribe opens this screen. You reach it by its address, , or your administrator gives you the link. The screen has an Administrator Guide Help button, and you can press F1 for this page. Screen Tour The screen is titled Historical Data Migration Jobs . Under the title is a Help button for the Administrator Guide, then the Import legacy file button, then the list of jobs. Field definitions The job list Item What it means Source system name The old system the records came from, as named when the mappings were set up. Status tag Pending, Running, Completed, Completed with Errors or Failed. Simulated tag The job was a simulated import. Cross validation discrepancy A warning tag. The number of records processed differs from the number the old system claimed. Counts "(n) ok · (n) failed · (n) review". "No migration jobs on file." Shown when nothing has been imported. The job window (select a row) Item What it means Heading The source system and the job status. Simulated banner "Simulated bulk import: the draft cases from this job are marked Simulated." Cross validation Reconciled (all claimed records processed), Discrepancy (claimed and processed counts, how many missing or extra), or "No claimed source count on file, cannot reconcile". Counts line "(n) succeeded · (n) failed · (n) need review (of n processed)". Records needing attention Each failed record with its error message, and each record that "Needs MPI review". Records Every record with its outcome (Succeeded, Failed, Needs MPI review) and, for a success, "Draft case (number)". The Import legacy file window Field What it means Source system The old system. Only systems with active field mappings are listed. If there is just one, it is chosen for you. Legacy file (CSV or the other accepted data format) The file to import. The window lists the accepted file types: comma separated (.csv), tab separated (.tsv), plain text (.txt) and one structured data format. Record count claimed by the source system (optional) The count the old system reports. If you give it, the job checks it against the records processed. Create draft cases from succeeded records A tick box, on at first. Toolbar Button What it does Import legacy file Opens the import window. Greyed out without the permission. Run import Starts the import. Greyed out until a system and a readable file are chosen. View job After an import, opens the job's window. Cancel / Close Leaves the import window. Help Opens the Administrator Guide at this screen, in a new tab. Icons and status indicators Indicator Meaning Grey Pending The job exists but has not started. Blue Running The job is in progress. Green Completed Every record was processed without errors. Amber Completed with Errors Some records failed or need review. Red Failed The job failed. Amber or red text next to a record Needs MPI review (amber) or Failed (red). Records list. Under All records each source record is listed with its outcome and, when it became a case, the case number. "No record results on file." means no record outcomes have been kept for this job. Hotkeys Key Action F1 Opens this User Guide page in a new tab. Step by Step Procedures Standard workflow 1. Confirm with your administrator that the field mappings for the old system are active. If none are, the import window says "No source system has active field mappings yet. Add them under Configuration → Migration field mappings, then import a file." 2. Open Migration Jobs and select Import legacy file . The import window opens with the Simulated banner. 3. Choose the Source system . 4. Select the file. A line appears, for example "250 records with 18 fields read from the CSV file". If some values were lists or groups inside a record, a second sentence reads "Nested values left out: {{count}}." with the number in place of the braces; those values are not imported, only the plain fields. A CSV needs a first row of field names; a structured data file must hold a list of records. The limit is 2000 records per file. 5. Optionally type the count the old system claims. 6. Leave Create draft cases from succeeded records ticked unless you only want to test the mapping. 7. Select Run import . "Importing records…" shows while it runs. 8. When it finishes the window shows the counts, the number of draft cases created (Simulated), records skipped because their legacy accession number was already imported, and any source fields no mapping covers. 9. Select View job . The job window shows the cross validation result and the records needing attention. Alternative workflow 1. To c

title: Batch
text: Batch { top} Overview Purpose. A batch is one plate that goes on one analyser in one run. This screen, headed "New Molecular Batch" while you build and by the batch barcode and test name afterwards, is where you choose the test and the instrument, enter the reagent lots, lay out the wells (controls and patient specimens), and create the batch. Once it is created you can print its labels, send its worklist to the instrument, read the run's results, trace any result back to its source, and, if the plate was built wrongly, retire it and start a corrected copy. Intended users. Molecular technologists. Laboratory managers read batches to review runs. Where it fits. You reach it from the Molecular screen: + New Batch opens a blank plate, and a click on any row in the batch lists, or on a plate link in the Order Queue, opens an existing one. Before you build, the specimens should be racked (Rack). Afterwards the run's results flow into the Order Queue and the report. note "An existing batch is read only" A batch is built once. After you select Create Batch , the layout, lots and instrument cannot be changed. You can look at the wells, send the worklist, read the results, and print labels. If the plate is wrong, use Clone & Supersede . note "Sending a worklist and receiving results are stand ins in the demonstration" PathScribe never talks to an analyser directly. The worklist is passed to your laboratory's interface engine, which drives the instrument, and the engine sends the results back. That connection is not built . In the demonstration the worklist is accepted only when the development "Mock Interface Engine" tool has been switched on; otherwise sending fails with a message that PathScribe could not reach the service. Results then arrive only through the Demo buttons on the Order Queue (see Molecular) or the same development tool. Nothing on this screen sends a real run to a real instrument yet. Screen Tour Field definitions Batch Info (new batch only) Field What it means Assay The molecular test, chosen from the molecular tests in your diagnostic catalog. Required. The test's name is filled in for you. Target Instrument The analyser the plate is for. The list holds only active analysers from the equipment register, with the ones at this workstation's laboratory first. Before you choose, the list reads "— Select an instrument —". An instrument with an open malfunction or overdue maintenance or calibration is shown in red, for example "⚠ Panther 3 (PANTHER 03): Malfunction". You may still pick it. A red box under the list says "… has an open malfunction. You can still choose it, but check it before running this batch." (or "… is past its maintenance or calibration due date. …"). When no analyser is active the list shows "No active analysers. An administrator can add them under Configuration → System → Equipment." Deck Slot Where the plate sits on the instrument. If the instrument has a deck layout this is a list of its extraction plate slots, each shown with its deck. The list starts with "Select a slot". Otherwise it is a text box with the example "e.g. SLOT A1". Your laboratory decides whether it is required; a star shows when it is. Plate Layout The size of the plate: 6 well, 12 well, 24 well, 48 well, 96 well (the default), 384 well, 1536 well, an 8 well strip or a 12 well strip. Changing it clears the grid. Reagent Lots (new batch only) Each lot has: Component (Master mix, Primer / probe, Extraction buffer, Detection reagent, Positive control, Negative control or Control), Lot Number , Expiration (a date) and QC Status (Signed Off, Pending or Failed). A star on the heading shows when your laboratory requires at least one lot. Well panel (new batch, after you select a well) Field What it means Sample Type Unassigned, Specimen, NTC (no template control), PTC (High), PTC (Low) or Calibrator. Control Lot Number, Control Expiration, Expected Result For a control or calibrator. The lot number and expiry are required for every control well: the batch is refused without both. The control's identity follows the lot number as you type it, so the Trace shows the whole lot. The expiry box shows the date you entered when you select the well again; clearing it clears the date. Expected Result is Negative or Positive and starts at the usual answer for the type (Negative for NTC; Positive for PTC (High), PTC (Low) and Calibrator). Change it if your control is different; it travels to the instrument with the worklist. Container Barcode For a patient specimen: the tube's barcode. Accession Number For a patient specimen: the accession. A patient well must have a container barcode or an accession. Aliquot Volume (µL) For a patient specimen. Your laboratory decides whether it is required. Existing batch Item What it means Heading The batch barcode and the test name. Plate Layout (rows×columns) The grid. A filled well can be clicked to see its sample type, accession (and the molecular order or control it holds). Molecular order For a well that holds an in house order: "Placed from the Order Queue; take it off the plate there." Run Results A table of Well, Accession, Ct Value, Internal Control Ct, Interpretation, Flag and Trace. It appears once the instrument's results have arrived. Until then there is no table. When it is shown but empty it reads "No per well results received yet." Toolbar Button What it does ← Back to Batches Returns to the Molecular screen, on the tab that shows this batch (Worklist & Plate Builder for a draft, Active Runs for a running batch, History & Archive for a finished one). Plate Label Prints the plate's label. Deck Location Label Prints the label for the plate's place on the instrument. It reads LOC INST followed by the instrument and the slot. Specimen Labels Prints a label for each specimen on the plate. Dispatch Worklist Opens the scan check. Shown only for a batch whose worklist has not been sent and that is not superseded. Clone & Supersede Opens the retire and copy panel.

title: Control Rules
text: Control Rules { top} Overview Purpose. This screen, headed "Assay Control Rules", defines which controls a molecular test must carry on every plate before the plate can be created, and whether each control is fixed to one well or may go anywhere on the plate. A rule can also name the instrument deck slots where that test's sample rack is allowed to go. The plate builder and the rack screen enforce what you set here. Intended users. Laboratory managers, quality staff and administrators who set or review the rules. Molecular technologists open the screen to see what a plate will be checked against. Who can open it, and who can change it. The page has its own permission and no longer depends on the Molecular screen. Opening it and reading the rules needs "View molecular assay control rules"; holding "Manage molecular assay control rules" also opens it. By default the Administrator, the Laboratory Director and the Quality Reviewer hold the view permission, and so does the Molecular Technologist (and any role that holds the Molecular screen). An administrator can give it to other roles in the Role Dictionary. Changing rules needs the manage permission, which needs the view permission with it; by default the Administrator and the Laboratory Director hold it. Without it the screen is view only: a line under the title reads "You can read these rules but not change them…", and + New Rule , Edit and Delete stay on the screen but greyed out. Hold the pointer over one and the tip reads "Your roles don't include" followed by the name of the permission. The same permission is checked again when you save, so a change is never made without it. A person who holds neither permission is shown the "no access" page if they type the address, and the Control Rules button on the Molecular screen is not offered to them. The rules themselves are still applied to every plate and rack for everyone who works one, whatever they hold here. note "This page is not behind the Configuration screen or the Molecular screen" Only the Molecular Order Queue demonstration page (Order Queue) needs the Configuration screen. Control Rules opens for anyone with the view or the manage permission, with or without the Molecular screen. What a person can do on it depends on the manage permission. Where it fits. Rules are set up before plates are built. When a plate is created (Batch), PathScribe checks its wells against the rule for its test. The Order Queue also keeps the fixed control wells free when it puts orders on a plate. Rack placement (Rack) offers only the deck slots a rule allows. A test with no rule has no control requirement at all: the plate builder does not insist on any control for it. Screen Tour The page opens with a ← Back to Batches button, the heading "Assay Control Rules", the line "Define which controls a given assay requires before a batch can be created, and whether each one is fixed to a specific well or allowed anywhere on the plate.", and a + New Rule button. Field definitions The list of rules Column What it means Assay Code The test, shown by its name. Required Controls One line per control: the control type, then "fixed at A01" or "random position". For example "NTC: fixed at A01" and "PTC (High): fixed at A02". Sample rack slots The deck slots the test's rack may use, or "Any sample rack slot" when none are named. Actions Edit and Delete . When there is no rule yet the table reads "No control rules defined yet." The rule form ("New Control Rule" or "Edit Control Rule") Field What it means Assay The molecular test, chosen from the active molecular tests in the diagnostic catalog ("— select assay —" until you choose). Required. Each test can have one rule. Required Controls: control type NTC (no template control), PTC (High), PTC (Low) or Calibrator. Patient specimens are not on this list. Required Controls: Position Fixed position (the control must sit in one exact well) or Random position (it must be on the plate but may sit in any well). Required Controls: Well For a fixed control: the well, for example A01 (the box shows "A01" as an example). Disappears for a random control. Reason for this change Required, for a new rule, a change and a delete. Type why (for example "new kit lot" or "rule corrected"). It is written to the audit log with your name, the test and the controls. Deck slots for this assay's sample rack Tick boxes, one for each deck slot that takes a sample rack on any active analyser. The hint reads "Rack Loading offers only these slots for this assay. Leave all unticked to allow any slot that takes a sample rack." When no analyser has a deck layout the section reads "No analyser has a deck layout yet (Configuration → Equipment)." Choosing "random" is meant to prevent the same control always falling in the same place on every plate, which protects against a pattern of cross contamination. Toolbar Button What it does ← Back to Batches Returns to the Molecular screen. + New Rule Opens a blank rule form. Needs the manage permission. Hidden while a form is open. Edit Opens the rule in the form. Needs the manage permission. Delete Asks "Delete this control rule?" and for a reason; the confirming Delete waits for the reason. Needs the manage permission. + Add Required Control Adds a control line to the form. Remove Removes that control line. Save Rule Saves the form ("Saving…" while it works). Needs the manage permission and a reason. Cancel Closes the form or the delete question without changing anything. Icons and status indicators Indicator Meaning Greyed out button You do not hold the manage permission (the screen is view only). Red message above or inside the form A rule was refused, with the reason in words. Delete question A box titled "Delete this control rule?" with the text "New test name plates will no longer be checked for these controls, and its sample racks can go in any sample rack slot." Hotkeys None. Step by Step Procedures Standard workflow Adding a rule for a test: 1. Open Con

title: Molecular
text: Molecular { top} Overview Purpose. The Molecular screen (the page title reads "Molecular Workspace") is the one home for molecular testing in PathScribe. From it you see the orders that are waiting for a plate, build the plates (batches) that go on an analyser, follow each run while it is on the instrument, look back at finished runs, and check which specimens each instrument run covered. It also leads to the extraction racks and to the control rules that every plate is checked against. Intended users. Molecular technologists, who run the bench. Laboratory managers use the same screen to follow runs. Pathologists see the effect of the work in the report: a finished test can fill in the matching question of the synoptic report. The Molecular tile in the Pathology Workspace opens this screen. By default only the Molecular Technologist role has the Molecular screen; if the tile is missing, ask your laboratory manager or administrator to add the screen to your role. Where it fits. A molecular test starts as an order (usually an add on order placed from a case), waits in the Order Queue, is put on a plate with its controls, is sent to the analyser as a worklist, and comes back as a run result. The result goes onto the order, and, when it can be trusted, into the matching question of the pathologist's report. note "Several parts are demonstration only" The screen, the plate rules, the order queue, result handling and the report link are all built and work in the demonstration. What is not built is the live connection to a real analyser or reference laboratory. Sending a worklist and receiving a run result are stand ins today. See "Exception handling" below and the notes on each tab. Screen Tour The top of the page shows the title, the line "Batch and plate management for molecular diagnostics runs (HPV, CT/NG, respiratory PCR panels, targeted NGS)", three buttons on the right, and a row of five tabs. When you open the screen without choosing a tab, it opens on Active Runs & Batches . Field definitions Batch tabs (Worklist & Plate Builder, Active Runs & Batches, History & Archive) These three tabs show the same table; each tab shows batches in different states. Click a row to open that batch (Batch). Column What it means Batch The batch barcode PathScribe gave the plate. Assay The test the plate is for. Instrument The analyser the plate is for, by name, with the deck slot in brackets when one was recorded. Plate The plate barcode. Created When the batch was made. Status A coloured badge: Draft, Active, Awaiting Results, Completed, Aborted or Superseded. Tab Shows batches that are Empty message Worklist & Plate Builder Draft (being built, or built and not yet answered) "No draft batches yet. Use "+ New Batch" to start building one." Active Runs & Batches Active or Awaiting Results "No active runs right now." History & Archive Completed, Aborted or Superseded "No completed, aborted, or superseded batches yet." A row whose instrument has an open malfunction, or is past due for maintenance or calibration, is shaded as an alert. Hold the pointer over the instrument name to read "This instrument has an open malfunction or is past due for maintenance or calibration — check it before running this batch." The alert does not stop you; it asks you to check the instrument first. Order Queue tab The queue lists in house molecular orders. Above the table: "In house molecular orders from pathologists' add on orders. Select queued orders for one test, choose a draft plate of that test, and assign them: they take its free wells (never a control position)." Column What it means Select A tick box. It appears only on orders that can be put on a plate now. Order The order number, with who ordered it and when. Case The accession number, and the specimen block when there is one. Test The molecular test ordered. Performed In house or Send out (with the reference laboratory's name for send out). A warning may appear here, see Exception handling. Status Queued, On a plate, Running, At the reference lab, Resulted or Cancelled. Plate · well The plate barcode and well once the order is on a plate. Click it to open the plate. "—" when not on a plate. Result The result once there is one: Positive (detected), Negative (not detected), Indeterminate, Invalid, or Report received. Under it a short note says what happened to the report (see "Results and the report"). Actions The buttons that apply to that row. QC & Specimen Association tab A read only list of instrument runs reported by the molecular platforms, headed "Molecular Batch Management". Columns: Run Date, Instrument, Assay, Reagent Lot, Samples Run and Specimens Linked. Click a row (the arrow turns from ▸ to ▾) to list the specimens linked to that run by Accession, Specimen and Patient MRN. Nothing on this tab is typed in: runs and links arrive from the instrument. When there is none you see "No molecular batches on file yet." A run with no specimens shows "No specimens are yet linked to this batch via an inbound event." Toolbar Button What it does Extraction Racks Opens the list of extraction racks (Rack Board). Not shown on the QC tab, or to a person who holds neither the view nor the manage permission for control rules. Control Rules Opens the controls each test requires on a plate (Control Rules). Not shown on the QC tab. + New Batch Opens a blank plate to build (Batch). Not shown on the QC tab. Tabs Order Queue, Worklist & Plate Builder, Active Runs & Batches, History & Archive, QC & Specimen Association. The address changes with the tab, so a tab can be bookmarked. Reference lab list (Order Queue, send out rows) Chooses the reference laboratory for a send out order. Greyed out unless you may choose labs. Plate list and Assign to plate (Order Queue) Choose a draft plate for the ticked orders, then put them on it. Take off plate Returns an order on a plate to the queue. Send out instead Moves an in house order to send out when your laboratory no longer runs that te

title: Order Queue
text: Order Queue { top} Overview Purpose. This screen, titled "Molecular Order Queue", lists the outbound molecular order messages that PathScribe has produced: an HPV co test order raised when a specimen was accessioned, a reflex genotyping order raised by a positive HPV screen, and instrument orders. Above the list is a small demonstration panel where you can place an HPV order and then simulate the laboratory's result coming back, to show the whole HPV order and reflex workflow without an analyser. Intended users. This is a testing and demonstration page, not a bench screen. It is meant for laboratory managers, administrators and trainers who need to show or test the HPV order and result path. note "Do not confuse this with the Order Queue tab" The Order Queue tab on the Molecular screen is where technologists put in house molecular orders on plates. It is a different list with different content. This article is about the separate page at "Molecular Order Queue". Orders placed from the Add on Orders page appear in the tab, not here. Who can open it. The page is protected by the Configuration screen permission, the same one that opens Configuration. By default that is the Administrator, Template Author, Template Approver and Laboratory Director roles. A Molecular Technologist, who has the Molecular screen, does not have it by default and sees "You don't have access to this screen" with a Back to Home button. An administrator can add the Configuration screen to another role in the Role Dictionary. Where it fits. There is no tile for it on Home. Open Configuration , choose the Demo Reset tab, find the heading "Testing & Demo Tools", and select Open beside "Molecular Order Queue". The card describes it as "Simulate ordering and inbound HPV results against a fixed seed case. A testing/demo surface, not a production ordering workflow." The Demo Reset tab works only in a demonstration environment. At a site connected to live servers it shows "Demo reset is unavailable" and this link is not offered. Screen Tour The page has a heading and a line under it: "Outbound molecular assay and instrument orders — fired automatically at accession, or by an HPV reflex genotyping trigger on a positive standalone screen." Then the demonstration panel, then the table. Field definitions Demonstration panel ("Demo: HPV order & reflex workflow") The panel says "Operates against real seed case S26 5003 CYT 001, Specimen A — already configured with an HPV co test pending. Queue the assay order, then simulate the lab result coming back." The case and specimen are fixed. You cannot pick another case on this page, and the case is demonstration data, not a real patient. Field What it means Assay used Which HPV test the simulated order and result are for. st hpv highrisk screen (standalone) is the high risk HPV screen on its own. st hpv reflex (bundled) is the version that already includes reflex testing. Simulated result The result the simulated laboratory returns: Positive or Negative . Message line under the buttons The outcome of your last action (see the list under Error recovery). The table of queued orders The newest entry is at the top. With nothing queued you see "No orders queued yet." Column What it means Type Molecular for an assay order, or Instrument for an order that was prepared for an instrument. Accession The accession number followed by the specimen letter, for example S26 5003 CYT 001 A. For an instrument order it shows the master barcode instead. Assay The assay code ordered (for an instrument order, the instrument vendor). Reason Protocol configured (accession) when the order was raised automatically at accessioning because the specimen's protocol says so. HPV reflex genotyping when a positive standalone screen raised it. A dash for instrument orders. Status Queued (waiting to be sent), Sent , or Failed . Queued at The date and time the order was placed, in your language's format. A row raised by an HPV reflex is tinted so it stands out. Toolbar Button What it does Queue HPV co test order Places an order for the chosen assay on the demonstration case, as if the accession had raised it. You see "Order queued." and a new Queued row appears at the top of the table. Simulate inbound HPV result Plays the part of the laboratory: sends a result (Positive or Negative) for the chosen assay on the demonstration case, through the same result handling that a real interface would use. Both buttons are greyed out for a moment while they run. Icons and status indicators Indicator Meaning Queued The message is waiting to go out. Sent The message has gone out. Failed The message could not be sent. Tinted row The order was raised by an HPV reflex. Hotkeys None. Step by Step Procedures Standard workflow Demonstrating the standalone HPV screen with a reflex: 1. Sign in as someone with the Configuration screen and open Configuration. Choose the Demo Reset tab and, under "Testing & Demo Tools", select Open by "Molecular Order Queue". The page opens. 2. In Assay used , leave st hpv highrisk screen (standalone) selected. 3. Select Queue HPV co test order . The line under the buttons reads "Order queued." and a Molecular row for S26 5003 CYT 001 A with the reason Protocol configured (accession) and status Queued appears at the top. 4. In Simulated result , choose Positive . 5. Select Simulate inbound HPV result . The line reads "Result applied — genotyping reflex order fired below." (If you press it again, the line says the reflex order already exists and no second row is added.) 6. Look at the table. A second, tinted row has appeared, for the genotyping test, with the reason HPV reflex genotyping . That is the reflex: a positive result on the standalone screen orders genotyping automatically. 7. If you want to see the result on the specimen, open case S26 5003 CYT 001 in the cytology screen. See Cytology. Alternative workflow 1. Negative result. Choose Negative in step 4. The line reads "Result applied." and no reflex row

title: Rack Board
text: Rack Board { top} Overview Purpose. The Rack Board is the list of extraction racks. On screen its heading is "Extraction Racks", with the line "Physical tube racks holding input specimens prior to or during lysis/extraction, ahead of plate loading." Each row is one physical rack of specimen tubes, with how full it is and where it stands: still being loaded, waiting for sample IDs, or already placed on an instrument. From here you start a new rack or open an existing one. Intended users. Molecular technologists who prepare specimens for a run. Laboratory managers use it to see what is waiting. Where it fits. The rack comes before the plate. Specimens are scanned into tube positions on a rack (Rack), the rack is placed on the instrument's deck, and then the plate for the run is built and its worklist sent (Batch). You reach the board from the Extraction Racks button on the Molecular screen. Like the rest of the Molecular screens it needs the Molecular screen permission; by default that belongs to the Molecular Technologist role. If the button or the address does not open, you will see "You don't have access to this screen" with a Back to Home button; ask your administrator to add the Molecular screen to your role. Screen Tour The page has the heading and subtitle at the top left, a + New Rack button at the top right, and a table below. Field definitions Column What it means Rack The rack's own barcode, for example RK HPV 0417. If you did not give a barcode when you created the rack, PathScribe made one that starts RACK MOLE followed by a number. Capacity How many tube positions the rack has. Occupied How many positions hold a tube, shown as for example "9 / 24". Status Where the rack stands (see the table of indicators). Created The date and time the rack was created, in your language's format. The newest rack is at the top. While the list loads you see "Loading…". When there is no rack at all you see "No extraction racks yet." Toolbar Button What it does + New Rack Opens a blank "New Extraction Rack" form (Rack). A row Click anywhere on a row (or select it with the keyboard and press Enter) to open that rack. There is no search box, filter or sort control on this page. The board shows every rack, newest first. Icons and status indicators Status Meaning Loading The rack is still being filled, and every tube on it already has its accession. This word means the rack is being loaded, not that the page is loading. Needs sample IDs At least one tube is on the rack but has no accession against it. The rack cannot be placed on an instrument until each tube has one. On instrument The rack has been placed on that instrument. On instrument , slot The rack has been placed on that instrument in that deck slot. The status is worked out each time the page opens from what is on the rack. A rack that has been placed always reads as placed, even if a tube was added afterwards. Hotkeys None on this screen. Step by Step Procedures Standard workflow 1. On the Molecular screen select Extraction Racks . The board opens with the newest rack first. 2. Look at the Status column. Racks that read Needs sample IDs are the ones that still need work before they can go on an instrument. Racks that read On an instrument are done. 3. To start a rack, select + New Rack . The "New Extraction Rack" form opens. Complete it as described in Rack. 4. To carry on with a rack, click its row. The rack's page opens with its positions. 5. When you are finished, use ← Back to Racks on the rack's page. The board shows your rack with its new Occupied count and Status. Alternative workflow 1. Finding a rack for a run. Go to the Rack Board, look for the rack barcode written on the physical rack, and click it. The barcode in the Rack column is what is printed or scanned. 2. Checking what is ready to run. Read down the Status column. A rack on an instrument is ready for the worklist. Then go to the plate in Batch. 3. Going back from a plate. The plate screen has no link to the Rack Board. Use Extraction Racks on the Molecular screen. Exception handling 1. A rack reads "Needs sample IDs" and you cannot see why. Open the rack. Positions that hold a tube without an accession are marked in a different colour and a line under the instructions lists their numbers. Give each one its accession. 2. The rack count looks wrong. Occupied counts positions that hold a tube barcode. A position that was never scanned does not count. 3. A rack you expect is missing. The board lists every rack. Check you are signed in to the right site, and look at the barcode on the physical rack. A new rack is created only by someone using + New Rack . 4. A rack was placed on the wrong instrument. Open it and record a new placement. See Rack. Error recovery 1. You created a rack by mistake. There is no delete on the board or on the rack's page. An empty rack that is never used does no harm; leave it. If it carries a wrong barcode, create a new one and use that. 2. The page says "Loading…" for a long time. Reload the page. If the board is still empty and you know racks exist, tell your laboratory manager. 3. You opened the wrong rack. Select ← Back to Racks and choose the right row. Nothing changes until you scan or save. Tips and Best Practices Common mistakes Reading "Loading" as a problem. It is the normal word for a rack being filled. Placing a rack with tubes missing accessions. The rack will not place; fix the tubes first. Creating a second rack for the same physical rack. Check the board first and open the existing one. A duplicate barcode is refused ("Another rack already has this barcode."). Searching for a patient here. The board shows racks, not patients. A tube is found by opening its rack. Efficiency recommendations Use the rack's barcode label: scan or type it when you create the rack and the barcode shown in the Rack column will match the physical rack. Start each shift on the board and clear the Needs sample IDs racks first. Leave the barcode blank when you

title: Rack
text: Rack { top} Overview Purpose. This screen, titled "Extraction Rack Loading" in its breadcrumb and headed by the rack's barcode, does two jobs. First it creates a new extraction rack. Second, for an existing rack, it lets you scan each specimen tube into a numbered position, give every tube its accession (the sample ID), and then place the finished rack on an instrument's deck, with a check that the deck slot is the right one. Intended users. Molecular technologists preparing specimens for lysis and extraction. Where it fits. It sits between accessioning and the plate. Open the rack from the Rack Board. When the rack is on the instrument, build the plate and send the worklist in Batch. Each tube you scan records a movement from the primary vial to the rack, with your name, the workstation and the time. That record appears later in the Trace of the run result. note "No tube can be removed here" A position holds one tube at a time. The screen has no way to take a tube out or replace it once it is scanned in. Tubes that have no accession can be given one. If a tube was scanned into the wrong position, tell your laboratory manager before you place the rack; see Error recovery. Screen Tour There are two forms of the page. With the address ending /new it is the new rack form. With a rack's own number it is the rack itself. Field definitions New Extraction Rack Field What it means Rack identifier / barcode Scan or type the rack's own barcode (the box shows the example "e.g. RK HPV 0417"). Leave it blank and PathScribe generates one (RACK MOLE and a number). Letters are made upper case. It must be 3 to 40 letters, digits, dashes or underscores, starting with a letter or digit. Capacity How many tube positions the rack has. It starts at 24; the box accepts 1 to 384. The rack Item What it means Heading The rack barcode. Position grid One button per position, numbered 1, 2, 3 and so on. Instruction line "Select an empty position, then scan a specimen vial to load it. Each load records the vial to rack movement with the current user and station. When every tube has its sample ID, place the rack on its instrument below." "Needs a sample ID: position 3, 4. Click a flagged position to record its accession." Shown when a tube has no accession. It lists the positions. Hover text on a position "Position 1 — empty"; "Position 1: SPEC 0001 (S26 1001)" for a tube with its accession; "Position 1: SPEC 0001, no accession yet" for a tube without one. Loading a tube Field What it means Tube barcode The tube's barcode, when you type it. Accession number The accession the tube belongs to. Optional when you load, but the rack cannot be placed until every tube has one. Accession for position N (barcode) Appears when you click a flagged position, to record the missing accession. Place on instrument Field What it means Instrument The active analyser the rack is going on. The list shows the analysers of this workstation's laboratory first. Until you choose, it reads "Select an instrument". Assay The test the rack is for. Optional unless your laboratory requires it. Until you choose, the list reads "Select an assay". It narrows the slots to the ones the test's control rule allows. When the rule names slots, a line reads "This assay's sample rack goes in A1, A2." Deck slot The slot on the instrument. Until you choose, it reads "Select a slot". It lists only slots that take a sample rack and suit the test. Required only when the instrument has more than one such slot. Otherwise you see "This instrument has one slot for a sample rack, so no slot is needed." or "No deck layout is recorded for this instrument (Configuration → Equipment)." Placed line After placing: "Placed on PANTHER 01, slot A1, by Name, date." Toolbar Button What it does ← Back to Racks Returns to the Rack Board. Create Rack Creates the rack and opens it. Shows "Creating…" while it works. Scan into position N Waits for a barcode scan for the selected empty position. The button then reads "Waiting for scan into position N…". Scan not working? Enter specimen ID manually Opens boxes for the tube barcode and accession. Load puts the tube in the position (Enter does the same). Cancel closes the boxes. Save Records the accession for a flagged tube (Enter does the same). Scan deck position Waits for a scan of the label on the instrument's deck slot. The button reads "Waiting for the deck position's barcode…". Place rack Places the rack on the chosen instrument and slot. After a first placement the button reads Record new placement . Shows "Placing…" while it works. Icons and status indicators Indicator Meaning Plain position Empty. Occupied position Holds a tube. Not selectable unless it is flagged. Flagged (unmapped) position Holds a tube but no accession. Click it to record one. Selected position The one that the next scan will fill. "Still required: …" The placement fields still missing: for example "Sample ID for every occupied position", "Instrument", "Deck slot". The rack must also hold at least one tube. Red warning under Place on instrument The slot or scan is wrong. See Exception handling. Green "Scanned: …, slot …." (for example "Scanned: PANTHER 01, slot A1.") A deck scan was accepted. Hotkeys Key Action Ctrl+Alt+Shift+P Place the rack. Works on a saved rack and acts exactly as Place rack , including all the checks. You can also say "place rack" or "rack on instrument". Step by Step Procedures Standard workflow Creating a rack and loading it: 1. On the Rack Board select + New Rack . You see "New Extraction Rack". 2. In Rack identifier / barcode , scan or type the barcode on the physical rack. Leave it blank if the rack has none. 3. Set Capacity to the number of tube positions on the rack. 4. Select Create Rack . The rack opens, headed by its barcode, with an empty numbered grid. 5. Click position 1. It is highlighted, and the button Scan into position 1 appears. 6. Select the button, then scan the first tube. You see the tube in position 1; position 2

title: My Contribution
text: My Contribution { top} Overview Purpose. My Contribution (the screen is titled Contribution Dashboard ) shows your own work: how many cases you finalized, how much is still in progress, how fast your cases move, the quality issues linked to your cases, and how these change over time. Intended users. Pathologists and pathology assistants looking at their own figures. Residents and fellows also see their teaching cases and progress here, and supervisors see their supervisees under the Mentor tab. Bench staff have their own screen, Bench Contributions. Where it fits. Open it from the My Contribution tile on the Home Dashboard. It is a place to review, not to work cases. Selecting a quality flag opens the case; for open deficiencies see Quality & Compliance. Your daily work stays on the Worklist. Screen Tour note "Some figures are illustrations" Most Overview figures are worked out from the cases in the system. The AI Contribution tab shows a Demo data label on figures that are illustrative only and not yet calculated from your real cases. Treat any figure carrying that label as an example. At the top are your name and the tabs: Overview , Productivity , Quality , AI Contribution and Mentor . Field definitions Overview tab: Field What it means Cases Finalised (or Cases Signed Out) Cases you completed in the last 30 days. The wording follows your organization's setting. Cases In Progress Cases assigned to you that are not yet complete. AI Assisted Cases Your cases from the last 30 days where the AI assistant was used. ▲ / ▼ with "vs prior period" The change compared with the period before. Green up and red down arrows show direction only. Peer avg The average of your peers for the same figure (see below). % of target Shown when your organization has set a performance target for that figure. TAT Performance Average First Touch and Total Case turnaround time in hours, each as a percentage of its target, and the share of cases on target, weighted across the facilities you cover. RVUs Last 30 Days Your workload units for the last 30 days, the change against the previous 30 days ("New" if there was nothing before), and the average per case. This Week A bar chart of daily cases and RVUs. Performance targets and client service levels Your actual figures against the targets, and how each client's cases did against its agreed turnaround. Case Mix Your cases by area such as breast, GI, GU and dermatology, with counts. Quality Flags Up to three recent cases with a flag, an open deficiency or a frozen to final discordance. "No open quality items right now." when there are none. Active Intraop Sessions Your intraoperative entries still waiting to be linked to a formal accession, or "all merged". My Teaching Cases For trainees: cases you drafted that an attending reviewed, with a concordance percentage and the latest feedback. My Progress For trainees with a supervision assignment: progress toward the expected case numbers. Other tabs: Tab What it shows Productivity Monthly cases and year to date RVU accumulation, with last year for comparison, and a Peer Comparison panel (see the notes below). Ranges: 1M, 3M, 6M, YTD. Quality Tiles for Discordant Cases, Amended Reports and Concordance Rate, and sections for Frozen vs Final, Amended Reports, TAT Outliers and TAT by Facility. Choose a range of 30 Days, 90 Days or 1 Year. Select a turnaround tile to see its trend against target and peer lines. AI Contribution How often AI suggestions were accepted or overridden, with reasons. Marked Demo data . Mentor For supervisors: your active supervisees, their countersigned cases and progress. "You have no active supervisees right now." if none. More wording on the Overview tab: TAT Performance shows each average with a bar and a line such as "…% of …h target" (how the average compares with the target in hours). Under the bars it says "(n)% on target" and "weighted across … facilities", meaning the on target figure is combined across the facilities you cover. RVUs — Last 30 Days ends with "vs prev 30d" after the change and "Avg / case" for the average per case. This Week has the subtitle "Daily cases and RVUs — shared scale": cases and RVUs are drawn on one scale, so a day with many RVUs and few cases looks different from the reverse. My Teaching Cases lists each subspecialty with "… of … expected" when a target has been set for it, or a concordance percentage when no target is set. My Progress names your supervision programme and "supervised by …", with a bar headed "Progress toward graduation". Peer average On the Overview tab, "Peer avg" compares you with colleagues, using this rule: A peer is another active member of staff with the same role as you who works at at least one facility you also work at . Someone with no facility restriction counts as working at all facilities. You are never counted as your own peer. The average is the mean of each peer's own figure, worked out the same way as yours. There must be at least three peers. With fewer, the row shows Not enough data , so that no individual colleague can be identified. The row is shown only if your organization allows you to see peer comparison. Pathologists see it only when their organization has turned that on; if you do not see it, that is the reason. note "The Productivity tab uses a different peer group" The Peer Comparison panel on the Productivity tab is anonymized and shows the average and top performer for year to date RVUs. It compares you with all other active pathologists, not only those who share your facility, and it does not use the three person minimum. Do not read the two comparisons as the same measure. Tab details Productivity tab. Two views, chosen with the buttons Monthly Cases and YTD RVU Accumulation . Monthly Case Counts shows finalized cases per month as a volume overview (the legend reads Finalized cases). Year to Date RVU Accumulation shows the subtitle Cumulative RVUs · finalized cases only, and plots your running total; the series

title: My Exports
text: My Exports { top} Overview Purpose. My Exports lists the files you have asked PathScribe to prepare from the screens that offer an export (the audit log, quality reports, case search reports, registry transmission audit and similar). A small export downloads at once. A large one is prepared in the background, so you can carry on working, and then appears here as Ready with a Download button. You can also cancel one that is still waiting or being prepared. Intended users. Anyone who exports a report. You see only your own exports, and only you can download them. The screen needs no special permission to open; each export's own permission is checked again when you download. Where it fits. You start an export on the screen that offers it. While it is prepared, a notice appears on the screen you are on. Select My exports in that notice, or the download arrow in the top bar, to reach this list. Files are kept for 7 days and then deleted. note "Simulated export server in the demonstration build" In the demonstration build there is no export server connected. A banner reads Simulated : "No export server is connected, so exports are prepared in this browser and kept only until you sign out." A small export still downloads straight away; a larger one takes about 10 milliseconds per extra row (up to 30 seconds) and appears here. A tick box, Make exports take longer (to try the waiting experience) , makes each export take 8 seconds so you can see the Preparing state. This box exists only in the demonstration build. Screen Tour The page has the title My exports , the line "Exports you asked for. Files are kept for 7 days, and only you can download them.", a Refresh button, and the table. Field definitions Column What it means Export The export's name, taken from the file name, for example "audit log 2026 10 23". Status Waiting , Preparing , Ready , Failed , Cancelled or Expired . For a failed export, the reason is written under the status. Rows How many rows the file holds, once known. Requested When you asked for it. Deleted after When the file will be deleted (7 days after it was made, by default). (actions) Download on a ready export, Cancel on a waiting or preparing one. Other lines you may see: "Loading your exports…", and "You have no exports from the last 7 days." when the list is empty. What an export notice says. On the screen where you started the export, an inline notice shows "Preparing your export. We'll tell you when it's ready; you can carry on working." and then "Your export is ready (N rows)." with Download , My exports and Dismiss buttons. If it failed it shows the reason with Dismiss . A quick export shows no notice at all. Toolbar Button What it does Refresh Reads the list again. Download Saves the file of a ready export. Cancel Stops a waiting or preparing export. Make exports take longer (tick box, demonstration only) Slows simulated exports to 8 seconds. Icons and status indicators Indicator Meaning Waiting In line behind others. Preparing Being built now. Ready The file can be downloaded until the "Deleted after" time. Failed The file could not be made; the reason is shown. Cancelled You stopped it. Expired The 7 days passed and the file was deleted. Number on the top bar download arrow How many exports from this window are ready to download. The arrow itself is always shown. Simulated tag The demonstration export server is in use. Reasons shown for a failed export or a refused download include: "The export couldn't be made. Try again; if it fails again, tell your administrator.", "The export took too long and was stopped. Narrow the filters and try again.", "Too many rows for one export. Narrow the filters and try again." (with the number of rows that matched, when known), "You already have 3 exports being prepared. Wait for one to finish, or cancel one in My exports.", "You don't have permission to export this report.", "This export has expired and its file was deleted. Export it again.", "This export is no longer available.", "Your session has ended. Sign in again, then export again." and "The PathScribe server can't be reached. Try again in a moment." Hotkeys None. Step by Step Procedures Standard workflow 1. On the screen that offers an export, set the filters you want and select its export button. If the file is small it downloads at once and nothing else is needed. 2. If it takes longer, an inline notice says "Preparing your export…". Carry on with your work; you do not have to wait. 3. When the notice says "Your export is ready", select Download in the notice, or select My exports to see the list. In the top bar the download arrow shows a number while exports are ready. 4. On My Exports, find the row with status Ready and select Download . The file is saved by your browser. 5. Select Dismiss on the notice when you have finished with it. Alternative workflow 1. Select the download arrow in the top bar at any time to open the list, even if you dismissed the notice. 2. Select Refresh to see the latest status if the list seems behind. Exception handling 1. Three exports are already open. You can have only 3 waiting or preparing exports at a time. Wait for one to finish or select Cancel on one you no longer need. 2. Too many rows. An export holds at most one million rows. Narrow the filters (a shorter period, one facility) and ask again. 3. Taking too long. Exports are stopped after 30 minutes. Narrow the filters and ask again. 4. A ready file has expired. Ask for it again from the original screen. Error recovery 1. If Download shows an error under the row, read it. "You don't have permission to export this report" means your role no longer holds that export permission; ask your administrator. 2. If you were signed out, sign in and ask for the export again; a list left from before is not kept. 3. If Cancel was selected by mistake, ask for the export again from the original screen. 4. A repeated request while the first is still running sends nothing new, so selecting the e

title: Notifications
text: Notifications { top} Overview Purpose. This page explains how PathScribe gets your attention, what each signal means and how to clear it. PathScribe does not have one single notification centre or a bell icon. Instead it uses a small number of signals, each in a fixed place: numbered badges on the top bar, urgent messages, a critical finding window at sign out, short messages that appear after an action, and banners and warnings about your session and connection. Intended users. Everyone who signs in. Which badges you see depends on what your role may open. Where it fits. These signals are always on, whatever screen you are working on. The top bar is the place to look first. Most notices arrive as a message in Messaging, so that is also where you clear most of them. note "There is no bell" If you were expecting a bell icon with a list of alerts, there is not one in this version. The speech bubble button with its number is the closest thing, and automatic notices land in your Messages. This page lists every signal that exists today. Screen Tour Field definitions What raises a notice, and where it appears Signal Where you see it What caused it Number on the speech bubble button Top bar Messages you have not opened. Includes notices sent by PathScribe itself. Red speech bubble and a two beep tone Top bar An unread urgent message. Notice from "PathScribe System", "Delivery monitor", "PathScribe follow up tracking", "LIS Integration" or "System Admin" Messages Something happened that needs a person (see the table below). Amber triangle with a number Top bar Registry submissions that need attention. Shown only when the number is above zero and your role may open Registry Exceptions. Download arrow, with a number when exports are ready Top bar Exports you asked for. Shown when large exports are prepared in the background on your installation. Critical Finding Detected window Report, when you sign out or finalize The text of the case contains a term that may need an urgent call to the physician. Short message at the foot of the screen Report and other screens The result of something you just did: saved, refused, failed. Coloured strip under the top bar Every screen Your connection to PathScribe is offline, reconnecting or has been restored. Session Expiring Soon window Every screen You have been idle and your session will end in under a minute. Live status badge (Live, Local updates, Offline) Some work screens Whether the list updates by itself. Notices PathScribe sends to your Messages Notice Who gets it What to do "Follow up due soon" or "Follow up overdue" for a case Staff responsible for follow up. Overdue ones are urgent. Open the case link, then record the outcome or email the ordering clinician in Quality Assurance, Operations, Follow up. "Delivery failed after N attempts" Administrators and laboratory directors. Urgent. Resend the report from its queue; the notice names where the failure is listed. "Case … corrected in LIS, review required" The pathologist who signed the case. Urgent. Review the correction and decide whether your synoptic data also needs amending. "High Priority: Interface Exception" Staff who resolve interface problems. Urgent, with an Open Configuration button. Use the button to go to the exception. "You're presenting at …" A tumor board presenter. Open the case link before the meeting. Access request or decision Case owners, administrators, and the person who asked Grant or refuse in the screen the notice names, or read the decision. Request for a review or a consultation, or being added as a collaborator The colleague named Open the case link and leave an internal note. "Your template request is ready" The person who asked for a new synoptic template The template is in the Synoptic Library. Support access request Approvers. Urgent, with Open Configuration . Approve or refuse in Configuration. Toolbar Control What it does Speech bubble button Opens Messages (Alt+I). Amber triangle Opens the Registry Exceptions screen. See Registry Exceptions. Download arrow Opens My exports. See My Exports. × on a short message Closes it at once. Clicking anywhere on it closes it too. Stay Logged In / Log Out The two choices in the Session Expiring Soon window. Icons and status indicators Indicator Meaning Blue number badge A count: unread messages, registry submissions, exports ready. Red badge or red bubble Urgent. ✓ green short message Success. ℹ blue short message Information. ⚠ amber short message Warning: something needs your attention. Read it; it is announced to screen readers as an alert. ✕ red short message An action failed. Nothing was changed unless the message says so. Coloured dot in the strip under the top bar Orange when reconnecting, red when offline, green when restored. Hotkeys Key Action Alt+I Open Messages Ctrl+Alt+Shift+7 Send the secure email (in the secure email window) No key opens the registry or exports buttons; select them with the mouse. Step by Step Procedures Standard workflow 1. Look at the top bar when you start work. A number on the speech bubble means unread messages; red means at least one is urgent. 2. Select the bubble. Urgent messages are at the top. Open each one. 3. Act on it. Most notices include a case link or a button that takes you to the right screen. 4. When you have dealt with it, leave it read, or delete it from the list. The number on the bubble drops by one each time you open a message. 5. If the amber triangle is showing, select it and work through the submissions listed; the number falls as each is resolved. 6. If the download arrow shows a number, open My exports and select Download for each file that is ready. Responding to Critical Finding Detected 1. title: OR Suite Display
text: OR Suite Display { top} Overview Purpose. The OR Suite display is a wall screen for an operating room or a group of rooms. It lists every frozen section request in progress for that room: how long the tissue has been in the laboratory, which step it has reached, and, once the pathologist has given the frozen section diagnosis, the preliminary result for the surgical team. The OR staff can log that a verbal report was given and, after reading the result back to the surgeon, dismiss the case from the board. Intended users. Operating room nursing and support staff who watch the board and act on it, pathologists and bench staff whose work feeds it, and the administrator who sets up each terminal. The board is a shared screen, so it does not use a personal sign in. Each action on it (logging a verbal report, dismissing a case) is attributed to a person by a four digit PIN. Where it fits. The rows come from the frozen sections recorded in the Intraop Queue: the specimen's arrival, gross, touch prep, frozen section cut and diagnosis. Record the work there; the board follows. Once the case is formally accessioned, the frozen results travel with it into the report. note "Demonstration controls on the board" The board has a Start demo button. It adds four demonstration frozen sections (named "DEMO" cases, labelled "Demo mode — not real patient data" while running) to the board's location, so a salesperson or trainer can show every state, and then advances one of them every 25 seconds. Stop demo stops the advancing and removes the demonstration cases it added, so nothing invented stays in the intraoperative data. Both buttons need the permission "Run the OR Suite demo" (given to administrators by default); without it the button is greyed out, and its tooltip names the permission. Do not use it on a board that staff are relying on: while the demonstration runs, its four DEMO rows sit among the real cases. Screen Tour Field definitions First start (setup). The first time a screen opens it shows Bind this display : "Select which OR Suite Terminal this monitor represents. This binding is sticky — it survives reloads and restarts." Choose a terminal from "— select terminal —", then type the Display Token an administrator issued for that terminal ( Enter Display Token , Confirm , Back ). If no terminal exists the screen says "No terminals configured yet — add one under System Configuration." If the token is wrong, expired or revoked the screen says so and a revoked or expired display goes blank with Display unavailable and Enter a new token . The board re checks its token about once a minute. Header Item What it means OR suite terminal / terminal name The terminal this screen is bound to. Location line The terminal's location, for example "OR Suite · Room 3". Connection badge Live (changes from every display appear at once), Connecting… , Reconnecting… , Offline (refreshing every 15 seconds meanwhile) or Local updates (no live update server: this computer's windows update at once, other screens every 15 seconds). Hold the pointer over it for the explanation. Demo mode badge "Demo mode — not real patient data". Shown only while the demonstration is running. Start demo / Stop demo Described above. Multi suite overview A tick box, shown only if the terminal was given the multi suite privilege. Multi suite overview. When ticked, a list appears of the locations of the terminal's facility ("Point of care — Room"). Select one or more (hold Ctrl or Command to choose several). The board then shows the rows from all the chosen locations instead of its own. With none chosen, it shows its own location. Each row (one per specimen). Item What it means Large label The OR number, and the location after a dot when it differs. The patient's name and MRN are deliberately not shown on the wall. Small line "Specimen A · Surgeon: Dr. … · Pathologist: Dr. …". Timer Minutes and seconds (m:ss) counted up from the time the tissue arrived. It runs while the diagnosis is outstanding and stops at the moment the diagnosis was rendered. Step Grossing , Touch Prep , Sectioning or Pathologist Review , from the latest step logged for the specimen: nothing yet is Grossing; gross logged is Touch Prep; touch prep performed or skipped is Sectioning; frozen section cut is Pathologist Review. Result line Once a diagnosis is rendered, "PRELIMINARY: <diagnosis " replaces the step. In progress (inactive button) and Log verbal report Shown on a row that has no diagnosis yet. Dismiss case Shown on a row that has a diagnosis. The clock. The target time and the warning come from your laboratory's turnaround settings for the frozen section, which can differ by facility and between STAT and routine specimens. If none is set, the board uses 20 minutes with a warning for the last 5. The clock counts from the specimen's arrival. More than the warning time left: the row is plain. Within the warning time: the row shows the warning colour. Time is up: the row shows the overdue colour. Diagnosis rendered: the row takes its completed look and flashes three times, once only, the moment the diagnosis first appears, whichever device it was entered on. The board makes no sound. All signals are visual. Toolbar The only buttons on the board are in the header (Start demo, Stop demo, the Multi suite tick box) and on rows (Log verbal report, Dismiss case). Windows opened from rows are described under Procedures. Icons and status indicators Indicator Meaning Plain row In progress, inside the target. Warning coloured row In progress, in the last minutes before the target (5 by default). Overdue coloured row In progress, past the target. Completed row ("PRELIMINARY: …") The diagnosis was given; the timer is frozen; Dismiss case is available. Row sliding out The case was dismissed; it leaves the board after about 0.4 second. Connection badge Live / Connecting… / Reconnecting… / Offline / Local updates. "No active frozen section requests right now." Nothing is on the board

title: Outbound Queue
text: Outbound Queue { top} Overview Purpose. The Outbound Queue is the one list of everything PathScribe sends out of the building: results, patient movement (ADT) messages, accession messages, LIS sync messages, billing charges, report delivery, cytology results, referrals, molecular orders and registry submissions. For each message you can see where it is going, whether it is waiting, held, sent, acknowledged, failed or rejected, when it is due to go, and how close it is to its reporting deadline. You can stop a message, let it go again, retry a failed one, and fix or close a message that a registry refused. Intended users. People who look after the connections to other systems: administrators, interface analysts, and laboratory managers who watch billing and registry reporting. It is not a screen for pathologists or bench staff, and by default only administrators can open it. Each action needs its own permission (see "Who may do what"). Where it fits. A message joins the queue when something happens elsewhere, for example a case is signed out or a charge is made. PathScribe decides what is sent and when (the delivery schedule); the interface engine decides how it is carried and reports back whether the receiver accepted it. This screen shows both. Open it from Home, then Quality & Compliance , then Outbound Queue . Registry submissions that need a person are also listed, with more detail, in Registry Exceptions. note "Demonstration build" In the demonstration build the queue is built from the demonstration queues held in the browser, and nothing is really delivered to an outside receiver. Statuses change when you act here, not because a real receiver answered. The screen works the same way with a live installation, where the interface engine's acknowledgements update the status. Screen Tour From the top: the title and description, a row of count tiles, a row of feed filter buttons, a row of search, facility and sort controls, the action buttons, an optional reason panel, a result line, and the message table. Field definitions Count tiles. Every tile is a count and a filter. Selecting a tile limits the table to that group; select it again to remove the filter. Several tiles can be on together. Tile What it counts Overdue Open messages past their reporting deadline. Due soon Open messages whose reporting deadline is within 3 days. Needs review Billing charges parked for a person (an unmapped CPT code, no technical component facility, or a delta charge from an amended case), plus registry reports the state profile parked for a person. Selecting it shows only those. Amendment deltas Billing delta charges from amended cases. This tile is a count only; it does not filter. Waiting, Held, Sent, Acknowledged, Failed, Rejected, Not reportable, Retracted Messages in that state (see "Icons and status indicators"). The state tiles ignore the state filter itself, so each shows how many messages are in that state under your other filters. Opening the screen with no filters shows everything. Filters and sort Control What it does Feed buttons (Results, Patient ADT, Accession, LIS sync, Billing, Report delivery, Cytology results, Referrals, Molecular orders, Registry) Limit the list to one or more feeds. Accession number box Finds messages whose accession number contains what you type, ignoring capitals. Facility All facilities or one facility. The list shows the facility codes that appear in the queue. A message with no known facility disappears when you choose one. Sort by State (the default: rejected first, then failed, held, waiting, sent, acknowledged, closed), Reporting deadline , Scheduled time , Queued time , Feed or Attempts . Arrow button Reverses the sort direction. Table columns Column What it means Tick box Selects the message. The tick box in the heading selects all those listed. Accession The case the message concerns, or a dash. Feed The feed and, in small type, the kind of message (for example "finalReport"). Destination Interface engine, Billing system, LIS partner, Delivery service or Registry, with the transport (for example SFTP) under it when known. State The status badge. Scheduled When it is due to go: the delivery schedule's time when one applies, otherwise the time it was queued. Attempts How many retries so far. Detail Why it is in this state: the error (Missing ICD 10 code, Missing provider NPI, Timed out, Receiver unreachable, Rejected by the receiver), the registry's error codes, the correction due date, who held it and why, why it was closed, "Amends an earlier message", the billing type (TC, 26 or Global), "Needs review" reasons, the scheduled release time of a charge, and "Released ahead of schedule (user …)". Deadline Overdue or Due soon when it applies, with the due date and time. A row with a deadline that is overdue or near is tinted. Deadlines count from the time the report was signed out, using the number of days in the delivery schedule for that feed. A message that is already sent, acknowledged or closed carries no flag. Toolbar The action buttons act on the ticked messages. A button is greyed out if none of the ticked messages can take that action in their current state, or if your role lacks the permission (hold the pointer over it to see which permission). The line "Selected: N" shows your selection. Button What it does Hold Stops waiting or failed messages from going. Opens a panel asking for a reason. Release Lets held messages go again. Retry Sends a failed message through its own queue again. For a message a registry rejected, it opens a panel asking why it was fixed, then resubmits it. Release now Billing charges only. Forces a waiting or held charge out immediately, ahead of its schedule. The user is recorded. Retract charge Billing charges only. Cancels a waiting, held or failed charge before release. Opens a panel asking why. Final. Mark not reportable Closes a rejected registry message with a reason. Nothing more is sent for it. Reason panel. Appears bel

title: Pathology Workspace
text: Pathology Workspace { top} Overview Purpose. Pathology Workspace is the doorway to the laboratory's workstations. It is a second level screen of tiles: cytology screening, molecular diagnostics, the microtomy, embedding and slide distribution workstations, batch management, and the margin exception review queue. Choose a tile to open that workstation. Intended users. Histotechnologists, pathology assistants and laboratory managers. Cytology and molecular staff reach their own workstations here too. What you see depends on your role. Where it fits. The bench work follows Grossing: cassettes are embedded, sectioned into slides, and the slides are handed out to pathologists or sent to a scanner. When the slides are ready, cases continue on the Worklist. To see how your own bench work is going, open Bench Contributions. Screen Tour note "You only see tiles you may open" A tile appears only if your role may open that workstation. A colleague with a different role will see a different set. If a tile you expect is missing, ask your laboratory manager to check your access. Field definitions Item What it means Pathology Workspace The screen title. Subtitle "Cytology screening, molecular diagnostics, the microtomy, embedding, and slide distribution workstations, and batch management". Tiles One per workstation. Each has a title and a one line description of what it is for. The tiles, when your role allows them: Tile One line description on the tile Cytology Workspace Primary screening hub for GYN Paps, Non GYN triage, cell block tracking, and mandatory QC. Microtomy Workspace Real time on demand or batch slide label printing, stain management, and cytology/decant prep at the microtome bench. Embedding Workspace Cassette scan/verify, piece count confirmation, mold selection, and discrepancy flagging at the embedding bench. Slide Distribution Workspace Continuous scan checkout to pathologists or ingestion into a digital scanner, with split destination warnings and exception handling. Molecular Workspace Batch and plate management, active runs, and QC/specimen association for molecular diagnostics (HPV, CT/NG, respiratory PCR). Batch Management Track cassettes and slides through processing nodes via container barcodes. Margin Exception Review Margin distance free text answers the system could not confidently read: tag the real distance or dismiss with a reason. note "Workstation names" The tile for the microtomy workstation is called Microtomy Workspace, but once you open it the page is titled Microtomy Workstation. The same applies to Embedding and Slide Distribution, which are titled Embedding Station and Slide Distribution Station. Toolbar Button What it does ← Back to Home Returns to the Home Dashboard. Icons and status indicators Indicator Meaning Tile highlight when you point at it or tab to it The tile you are about to open. Coloured tile with a picture Each workstation has its own colour. Some pictures are placeholders until real photographs are added. Hotkeys None are specific to this screen. Alt+H (Go Home) returns you to Home, and F1 (View Help) opens the guide page for the screen you are on. You can move between tiles with the Tab key and open one with Enter or the space bar. Cytology Workspace What it is for. The cytology worklist: your assigned cases, the shared pool and the shared QC rescreen queue. A switch at the top chooses GYN Cytology or Non GYN / FNA Queue . How to start. 1. Select the Cytology Workspace tile. The Cytology Worklist opens. 2. Choose GYN Cytology or Non GYN / FNA Queue . 3. Pick a list such as My Worklist or Pool . Use Claim on a pool case to take it. 4. Open a case row to go to the screening page. Molecular Workspace What it is for. Batch and plate management for molecular runs (HPV, CT/NG, respiratory PCR panels, targeted NGS). How to start. 1. Select the Molecular Workspace tile. The screen opens on Active Runs & Batches . 2. Use the tabs to move between Worklist & Plate Builder , Active Runs & Batches , History & Archive and QC & Specimen Association . 3. To build a new run, select + New Batch . Control Rules opens the molecular control rules. Microtomy Workspace What it is for. The microtome bench: label printing for slides, stains to cut, and preparation of cytology fluids and decants. How to start. 1. Select the Microtomy Workspace tile. The Microtomy Workstation opens with the prompt "Scan a block or decant/fluid container barcode to begin". 2. Scan the block (or type the barcode in the box) and select Go . 3. A Block Summary appears with the patient and block details, and a Slide Grid shows the slides for the block. Embedding Workspace What it is for. The embedding bench: confirming each cassette, counting pieces, choosing a mold and reporting problems. How to start. 1. Select the Embedding Workspace tile. The Embedding Station opens with the prompt "Scan a cassette barcode to begin". 2. Scan the cassette (or type the barcode) and select Go . 3. The Block Summary appears, with Piece Count Verification , Base Mold Size , Orientation Instructions and Discrepancy Reporting for the block. The station takes block cassettes only. Slide Distribution Workspace What it is for. Handing finished slides to pathologists or pools (physical checkout) or sending them to a slide scanner (digital). How to start. 1. Select the Slide Distribution Workspace tile. The Slide Distribution Station opens with the prompt "Scan a slide or block/cassette barcode — the queue grows continuously". 2. Scan slides or blocks. They collect in the Work Queue . 3. Choose a slide, then set its Destination & Assignment : Physical Checkout or Digital Scanner , and confirm the routing. Barcodes that cannot be read are listed in the Scan Exception Log . Batch Management What it is for. Following groups of cassettes and slides through processing steps (decalcification and special processing, processing, embedding, microtomy, staining, checkout) by their container barcodes. title: Personal Settings
text: Personal Settings { top} Overview Purpose. This page explains the settings that belong to you: the language of the screen, your own spelling dictionary, the voice commands PathScribe has learned from you, your text shortcuts (macros), the bench your computer is set to, and how compact the report header is. It also describes the account menu at the top right of every screen. Intended users. Everyone who signs in. Where it fits. There is no single "Settings" screen. Your personal choices are spread over the top bar, the account menu, the Report screen and, for macros, the Configuration screen. This page tells you where each one lives and who it stays with. note "Whose setting is it?" Some choices follow you to any computer you sign in on (screen language, your dictionary, learned voice commands). Some belong to the browser on the computer you are using (compact report header, light or dark editor). Some belong to the computer (the scan station). The table in the Screen Tour shows which is which. note "Things that are not in this version" There is no page wide light or dark theme choice, no personal signature setting, and no screen for managing the dictation corrections PathScribe learns. Each is explained below. The tooltip says whether it is fixed to this terminal, your own default, or not set.
