title: Access Requests
text: Access Requests { top} Overview Purpose. Access Requests shows how quickly requests for access to cases are answered, lists the requests still waiting, and lets an authorised person deny a request or take back access that was given to see a patient's other cases. Intended users. Quality staff and laboratory managers who answer for response times, and administrators who decide requests. Where it fits. Open Quality Assurance , stay on the Operations pillar and choose the Access Requests tile. Requests are raised elsewhere in PathScribe; this screen is where the answers are tracked. See Quality & Compliance. Screen Tour The screen shows "Loading access request data…" while it opens. Field definitions At the top is a monthly chart of the average turnaround in hours for the last six months. Hover a point to see the average and how many requests were resolved. A month with no answers says "No requests resolved this month". Four tiles follow. Tile What it means Avg Turnaround Average hours from request to answer, for requests that have been answered. Pending Requests still waiting. Turns amber when above zero. Granted Requests that were approved. Denied Requests that were refused. Pending requests table: Column What it means Type Pediatric, Pool, Orchestration, or Patient's other cases. Requested By Who asked. Case The case the request names, if any. Select the row to open it. Requested At When the request was made. Waiting Hours since the request. Actions Deny on every row; Approve as well on Patient's other cases requests. Patient case access in force lists access to a patient's other cases that you may take back. Its columns are Requested By, Resolved By (who allowed it, and when) and Actions. It says "No patient case access to revoke." when there is none. The Resolved list has the columns Type, Requested By, Status (Granted or Denied), Turnaround and Resolved By. Until a request is answered in the chosen scope it says "No resolved requests in this scope yet." Toolbar Button What it does Scope switcher Chooses the organisation or referring facility whose requests are listed. Its groups are By Organisation and By Referring Facility. Pool and Orchestration requests belong to no referring facility, so they appear only under the whole enterprise or an organisation. Export Saves the listed requests as a spreadsheet file. Your role must allow it. Deny Opens the window Deny this access request? Revoke In Patient case access in force. Opens the window Revoke access . Icons and status indicators Indicator Meaning Granted (green) The request was approved. Denied (red) The request was refused. Amber Pending tile At least one request is waiting. Hotkeys None. Step by Step Procedures Standard workflow 1. Open the Access Requests tile. Read the tiles to see how many requests wait. 2. In the Pending table, find the oldest by the Waiting column. 3. To refuse, select Deny . In the window Deny this access request? type a Reason and select Deny . The person asking gets a message with your reason. 4. For a Patient's other cases request, select Approve to allow it. The request moves to the Resolved list. Alternative workflow 1. To take back access already given, find the person under Patient case access in force and select Revoke . 2. In the window Revoke access , type the Reason for revoking and select Revoke access . The person can no longer open that patient's other cases and is told why. Exception handling 1. If Deny or Approve is greyed out, your role may not decide that kind of request. 2. Pediatric, Pool and Orchestration requests are granted where the access itself is managed; the request then closes by itself. Only Deny and, for Patient's other cases, Approve are offered here. Error recovery 1. "The request couldn’t be denied." means nothing changed. Try again. 2. "The access could not be revoked." means the access is still in force. Try again. Tips and Best Practices Common mistakes Denying without a useful reason. The reason is sent to the person. Reading the average turnaround while a request waits: the average counts only answered requests. Efficiency recommendations Sort your day by the Waiting column. Workflow recommendations Review Avg Turnaround each month and export the list for your records. Related Features Upstream workflow AI Discordance: the previous report. Downstream workflow Patient Match and Management: the next screen in the Operations pillar. Troubleshooting Common user issues Problem Likely cause Nothing pending Every request has been answered. A request type is missing It is outside the scope you chose. Buttons are greyed out Your role may not decide that request type. Resolution steps 1. Set the scope to the whole enterprise. 2. Refresh the page. When to contact support Contact your laboratory's PathScribe support when a request is stuck as Pending after it was answered. Have the requester's name and the time ready.

title: AI Discordance
text: AI Discordance { top} Overview Purpose. AI discordance is a report inside Quality Assurance. It shows how often pathologists disagreed with each AI screening product the laboratory uses, and which AI screenings were ordered but have not been answered for too long. The screen is titled AI vs pathologist discordance . Intended users. Quality staff and laboratory managers who watch the AI products; pathologists who want to see how the products perform. Where it fits. Open Quality Assurance from the Quality & Compliance hub, stay on the Operations pillar and choose the AI discordance tile. It is read only apart from one setting, the stalled result time limit. See Quality & Compliance for the rest of the Quality Assurance screen. Screen Tour Field definitions The first section is Discordance by AI product , one row per AI product. Column What it means Vendor The company that supplies the AI product. Product The AI product. Ordered How many AI results were ordered from it. Reviewed How many of those a pathologist has judged. Agreed Reviewed results where the pathologist agreed with the AI. Disagreed Reviewed results where the pathologist disagreed with the AI. Discordance rate Disagreed as a percentage of Reviewed. Shows "Not yet reviewed" when nothing has been judged. Only results a pathologist has marked as agreeing or disagreeing are counted. A result nobody has judged is never counted as agreeing. When the laboratory has no AI products or results the table says "No AI products or results yet." The second section is Stalled AI results , with the number of stalled results in brackets. Item What it means Stalled after (hours) The time limit. An AI result that was ordered and has had no answer for longer than this is called stalled. The first value is 24 hours. Enter a whole number of hours from 1 to 720. Case The case the AI result belongs to. Select the row to open the case. Vendor The AI product supplier. Ordered When the AI result was ordered. Waiting How long it has been waiting, in hours. When nothing is stalled the table says that no AI result has been waiting longer than the limit. Toolbar Button What it does Export discordance rates Saves the Discordance by AI product table as a spreadsheet file. Your role must allow it. Export stalled results Saves the Stalled AI results table, with the time limit that was in force, as a spreadsheet file. Your role must allow it. Save Next to Stalled after (hours). Saves a new time limit. It is greyed out until you change the number. Icons and status indicators Indicator Meaning Not yet reviewed No pathologist has judged any result for this product, so no rate can be given. Highlighted row in Stalled AI results Rows can be selected; the pointer changes when you hover. Hotkeys None are specific to this report. F1 (View Help) opens the Quality & Compliance article. Step by Step Procedures Standard workflow 1. Open Quality Assurance , choose the Operations pillar, then the AI discordance tile. The report opens. 2. Read Discordance by AI product . Compare Reviewed with Ordered : a low Reviewed figure means the rate rests on few judgements. 3. Look at the Discordance rate for each product. 4. Read Stalled AI results . Select a row to open the case and find out why the AI result has not arrived. 5. To change what counts as stalled, type a new number in Stalled after (hours) and select Save . 6. To keep a copy for a meeting, select Export discordance rates or Export stalled results . Alternative workflow 1. To see disagreement for your own cases, use the AI Contribution tab on My Contribution. Exception handling 1. If a product shows Not yet reviewed , ask the pathologists to record whether they agree with the AI on those cases. Nothing is assumed. 2. If the stalled table is empty, no AI result has waited longer than your limit. Lower the limit to look for earlier delays. Error recovery 1. If you see "Enter a whole number of hours from 1 to 720.", correct the number and select Save again. 2. If you see "You don't have permission to change this setting.", your role may not change the limit. Ask your manager. 3. If you see "Could not save — please try again.", the new limit was not saved. Select Save again; tell your administrator if it keeps happening. Tips and Best Practices Common mistakes Reading a rate when only one or two results were reviewed. Check the Reviewed column first. Setting the stalled limit so short that normal processing time is flagged. Efficiency recommendations Select a stalled row to jump straight to the case. Workflow recommendations Review the report at each quality meeting and export it with the minutes. Related Features Upstream workflow Quality & Compliance: the Quality Assurance screen that holds this tile. Downstream workflow Access Requests: the next report in the Operations pillar. Troubleshooting Common user issues Problem Likely cause Save is greyed out The number has not been changed. The export button is greyed out Your role does not allow the export. A product is missing The laboratory has not set the product up, or no result has been ordered from it. Resolution steps 1. Refresh the page. 2. Check your role with your manager. When to contact support Contact your laboratory's PathScribe support when the counts do not match the cases, or the limit will not save. Have the product name and the time of the problem ready.

title: Cytology QA
text: Cytology QA { top} Overview Purpose. Cytology QA gathers the quality and compliance reports for gynaecological cytology in one place: agreement between screeners and pathologists, workload limits, HPV testing, registry reporting, proficiency testing and backlog. Each report is a tile; choosing a tile shows that report below. Intended users. Quality staff, laboratory managers and cytology supervisors. Where it fits. Open Quality Assurance and choose the Cytology QA pillar. Day to day screening happens on the Cytology Worklist and the Screening Case page; this screen reports on that work. See Quality & Compliance. Screen Tour The screen says "Loading Cytology QA data…" while a report opens. At the top is Scope: followed by the chosen scope and a scope switcher; hover over a tile to see "View:" and its name. Field definitions The tiles are: 10% Random Rescreening, High Risk Rescreening, CT vs. Path Correlation, Peer Review Correlation, Primary vs Final Diagnosis, CT Statistical Comparison, ASC US / HPV Reflex, Workload Tracking, Registry Transmission, Secondary Screening Audit, 5 Year Retrospective Lookback, Histology Correlation, Unscreened Backlog, UK HPV Failsafe, EU Compliance, HPV Positivity, Molecular QC Failure, Molecular Lot Trend and APAC Proficiency Testing. Agreement reports (random and high risk rescreening, CT vs. Path, Peer Review, Primary vs Final). Each opens with a card: Item What it means Overall Agreement Share of compared cases with the same result. Major Concordance Share with no major difference. Cases Compared How many cases were compared. Exact, Minor Discrepancy, Major Discrepancy The counts of each level. False Negative, False Positive Major differences where the first read missed or over called. Adequacy Discrepancy Cases where the two readers disagreed on adequacy. Diagnostic Upgrade, Diagnostic Downgrade Cases where the second read raised or lowered the category. A table lists each case: Case, Initial Screen and Follow Up Review (with reader), Result, and Adequacy ( Discrepant or a dash). With nothing to show it says "No comparisons on file for this report yet." CT Statistical Comparison. One row per cytotechnologist: Total Screened , the share of Unsat, NILM, ASC US, ASC H, LSIL and HSIL+, the ASC US:LSIL ratio, the Lab Avg ratio and Variance. An Outlier badge marks someone whose ratio differs from the laboratory average. Empty: "No reviews on file for this scope yet." ASC US / HPV Reflex. Per cytotechnologist: Total ASC US , Reflex HPV Ordered , Reflex Order Rate , HPV+ Count , ASC US HPV+ % and a status: Normal, Over Calling, Under Calling or Insufficient Data. Empty: "No calls on file for this scope yet." Workload Tracking. One row per screener per day: Shift Date , Hours Screened (marked signed off, not signed off, or signed off before more was recorded), Recorded hours, Manual Slides , Imager Slides , Total Equiv. Slides , Max Allowed and Exceedance (an Exceeded badge). A Correction flagged badge and the reason appear when the screener corrected their hours. Empty: "No ledger entries on file for this scope yet." Registry Transmission. Choose the Registry (Australia, South Korea, England, Ireland, Netherlands or Northern Ireland). The table shows Accession, MRN, HPV Result, Cytology Result, Transmitted, Status (Queued, Sent or Failed), Error, Sent, Registry status (such as Accepted, Awaiting answer, No answer in 72 h, Rejected, fixable) and Response code. Secondary Screening Audit. Case, Trigger, Outcome (Concordant or Discordant), Added By Event , Missed By Event and Reviewer. Empty: "No events on file for this scope yet." 5 Year Retrospective Lookback. A card shows Total Flagged , Pending, Completed and Corrective Action Rate . The table lists Case, Accession, Triggered, Status, Outcome (Confirmed Negative, Interpretation Error, Sampling Error or Screening Error), Corrective Action and Reviewed By. Empty: "No specimens flagged for this scope yet." Histology Correlation. A line reports how many cases correlated , how many were concordant, the correlation rate and the PPV for HSIL+ . The table has Patient MRN, Cyto Accession , Cyto Date , Cyto Diagnosis , Hist Accession , Hist Date , Hist Diagnosis , Days to Biopsy and Correlation Category (Concordant, Minor Discrepancy, Major Discrepancy or Discordant (Unspecified)). Unscreened Backlog. Case, Accession, Collected, Received, Status ( Unscreened or Pending Path Review ), Elapsed Hours and TAT Exceeded . Empty: "No backlog on file for this scope yet." UK HPV Failsafe. Per jurisdiction: HPV Primary Positives , Cytology Triage Performed , Inadequate Cytology Rate , Colposcopy referrals and No response after 28 days . EU Compliance. Per country: Total Cases , HPV Primary , HPV Co Test, Internal Audit Non Conformities , National registry ID , ThinPrep, SurePath and interval adherence. HPV Positivity. Per Testing Site : indication, assay, Total Tested , HR HPV+ %, HPV16 %, HPV18/45 %, Other HR % and Variance vs. Mean , in percentage points against the average of all sites. Molecular QC Failure. Run date, instrument, reagent lot, samples run, Invalid Controls , Inhibitors , Failure Rate and threshold, with an Exceeded badge when the rate is above the limit. Molecular Lot Trend. For each reagent change: instrument, Old Lot , New Lot , Control Level , Mean Ct (Old) , Mean Ct (New) , the shift, and Pass or Fail. APAC Proficiency Testing. A summary line counts satisfactory events. The table has Received, Accession, Provider, Challenge , Outcome (Satisfactory or Unsatisfactory), Score Detail and Deficiency, with a Flagged badge for a provider with repeated deficiencies. Empty: "No grades on file for this scope yet." Above the table is the Proficiency test panel card (see below). Where a report has no rows for a scope, other tables say "No data on file for this scope yet." Toolbar Button What it does Scope switcher Chooses the facility or organisation the reports cover. Report tiles Select a tile to show that report. Do

title: FPPE Tracking
text: FPPE Tracking { top} Overview Purpose. FPPE Tracking (focused professional practice evaluation, shown as Credentialing Review among the Operations tiles) lists the supervision periods in which a provisional hire has their cases reviewed by a proctor. It shows who is being reviewed, how far each review has progressed, and which periods have finished and why. Intended users. Quality staff and laboratory managers who manage credentialing. Where it fits. Open it from the Operations pillar of Quality Assurance . Supervision periods are created in the laboratory's configuration; this screen only reports on them. See Quality & Compliance. Screen Tour The screen says "Loading FPPE assignments…" while it opens. Field definitions Item What it means Active Assignments Supervision periods still running. Completed Periods that have finished. Threshold Reached — Needs Formal Graduation Active periods that have reached their case count or duration but have not yet been formally graduated. Red when above zero. The active table has these columns: Column What it means Provisional Hire The person being reviewed. Proctor The pathologist reviewing their cases. Scope The subspecialty the review covers, or "All subspecialties". Cases Reviewed How many cases the proctor has reviewed. Progress Percentage of the target reached. It turns red at 100 percent or more, which means the person is ready to be graduated. Started The start date. When nothing is running the table says "No active FPPE assignments." The completed table shows Provisional Hire, Proctor, Cases Reviewed, Completed and Reason, or "No completed FPPE assignments yet." The Reason tells why a period ended: Reason Meaning Case count reached The target number of cases was reviewed. Duration elapsed The set time ran out. Graduated early A manager ended the period before either limit. Toolbar Button What it does Scope switcher Offers facilities only. Choose the facility whose assignments you want. Export Saves active and completed assignments as a spreadsheet file. Your role must allow it. Icons and status indicators Indicator Meaning Red Progress figure The target is reached; formal graduation is due. Red Threshold Reached tile One or more people are waiting for formal graduation. Hotkeys None. Step by Step Procedures Standard workflow 1. Open the Credentialing Review tile. 2. Read the three tiles. If Threshold Reached — Needs Formal Graduation is above zero, find the red rows in the active table. 3. Graduate those people through your laboratory's configuration screen. 4. Use Export to keep a record for credentialing committees. Alternative workflow 1. A supervisee sees their own progress on My Contribution. Exception handling 1. If a person is missing, check the facility chosen in the scope switcher. Error recovery 1. If the table stays on its loading message, refresh the page. Tips and Best Practices Common mistakes Forgetting to graduate people whose Progress is 100 percent. Reaching the target does not end the period by itself. Efficiency recommendations Check the red tile once a week. Workflow recommendations Export completed periods at each credentialing review. Related Features Upstream workflow Countersign, Linkage and Drift: the previous report. Downstream workflow QA Dashboards and Inspection: the department wide reports. Troubleshooting Common user issues Problem Likely cause Progress shows a dash The period has no case count target. Nobody listed No supervision periods exist for that facility. Resolution steps 1. Choose another facility. 2. Refresh the page. When to contact support Contact your laboratory's PathScribe support when a person's case count does not match the cases reviewed. Have the person's name ready.

title: Quality & Compliance
text: Quality & Compliance { top} Overview Purpose. Quality & Compliance is where problems found in the laboratory's work are recorded, dealt with and checked. Its main working area is the Quality Assurance queue: a list of deficiencies (a specimen or case that did not meet the standard), what was done about each one, and whether the fix worked. It also shows the frozen to final diagnosis reconciliation results. Intended users. Quality staff and laboratory managers, who run the queue, and pathologists, who are asked about the cases in it. Which buttons are active depends on your role. Where it fits. The screen opens from the Quality & Compliance tile on the Home Dashboard. That first screen is a hub: it shows a tile for each area you are allowed to open. Choose Quality Assurance to reach the working queue. Cases in the queue open on their report screen (see Report). Screen Tour The hub The hub is titled Quality & Compliance . A tile appears only if your role may open it. Tile What it is Audit System activity logs, error and interface exception logs, and the financial audit trail. This is a read only view of what happened in the system. Only people whose role allows it see the tile. It is not used to change anything. Quality Assurance The working queue described in this article. Registry Exceptions Cancer registry submissions that were held, not delivered, rejected or never answered. Autopsy Dashboards Turnaround, consent, organ retention and cause of death figures. Outbound Queue Hold, release and retry outbound messages, and fix registry rejections. Select ← Back to Home to return to the Home Dashboard. note "Demonstration data" In the demonstration version the queue holds demonstration records. Nothing you do there reaches a real quality system. Field definitions At the top of the Quality Assurance screen is a row of buttons called pillars. Under it is a row of tiles, each with a count. Item What it means Operations The deficiency list and the clinical quality views: Deficiencies, Follow up not received, Frozen Linkage, Discordance, Countersign Turnaround, Credentialing Review, Post Final Drift, Patient Match Review, Patient Management, Access Requests and AI discordance. Financials Billing and coding deficiencies: Billing Deficiencies, Resolved, Code Review Pool and Charges awaiting approval. CAPA Engine Corrective action follow through: Recommended, Discordance Patterns (only if your role allows), Escalated to CAPA, Closed and Mgmt Reviews. Cytology QA, Enterprise Rollup, QA Dashboard, Inspection Mode, Activities Reports and evidence views, each a single screen. Deficiencies tile Number of open deficiencies. A line under it shows how many are overdue. Escalated to CAPA tile Number of deficiencies waiting for an effectiveness check. Closed tile Number of closed deficiencies. The deficiency list is split into Case Level and Specimen Level groups. Its columns are: Column What it means Status Open or Pending Verification . Case The case number. Select it to open the case. Specimen The specimen, or "Case level" if the problem is with the whole case. Issue The type of deficiency. A small ↺ and a number show how many times it was reopened. Detail What was observed (open items) or the corrective action taken (pending items). When Who raised it and when (open items), or "Due" with the effectiveness check date (pending items). An overdue date is highlighted. Actions The buttons for that row. More wording on the Quality Assurance screen Tile tooltips. The tile you are on says "Showing: … — click to switch"; the others say what they will show. Empty lists. "No open case level deficiencies.", "No open specimen level deficiencies.", "No escalated case level deficiencies." and "No closed deficiencies yet." mean exactly that for the group you are viewing. Under Financials: "No open billing deficiencies." and "No resolved billing deficiencies." Under CAPA Engine: "No management reviews recorded yet." In the Code Review Pool: "No cases pending code review." Code Review Pool columns are Flagged, Flagged By and Source. Source is Manual (someone put the case in the pool) or Random sample (the system picked it). Review opens the window below. Review Code Review Pool Entry. The first line names the case and why it is in the pool ("flagged by …" or "random sample") with any note. Choose a Review Outcome : No Issue Found , or Raise Billing Deficiency . For a deficiency, choose the type, then the Charge the deficiency is about (starting at "— Select a charge —"), or "A charge is missing" when the problem is a charge that was never made. Auditor Notes are required for a deficiency. Submit Review records the outcome. Management reviews table: Reviewed, Reviewed By, Items in Scope (the closed items the review covered) and Findings . CAPA owner: … appears under a deficiency once a corrective action has an owner. Closure trend (CAPA Engine). A line chart of deficiencies closed per month for the last six months; hovering a point shows "Closed: …" and "Reopened at least once: …". Toolbar Button What it does Scope switcher Chooses which facilities' deficiencies are listed. Export Saves the list you are looking at as a spreadsheet file. Your role must allow it. Raise Deficiency Opens a window to record a new deficiency by hand. Shown on the Deficiencies tile. Immediate Containment On an open row: closes it at once as a quick fix. Escalate to CAPA On an open row: starts a corrective action that must be checked later. Verify Effectiveness On a pending row: records whether the corrective action worked. Start Management Review On the Closed tile: records a review of closed items not yet reviewed. When there is none, the window reads "Nothing closed since the last review." Each action needs its own permission. If a button is greyed out, your role does not allow it; ask your manager. Icons and status indicators Indicator Meaning Open The deficiency has been raised and nobody has acted yet. Pending Verification A corrective actio

title: Patient Match and Management
text: Patient Match and Management { top} Overview Purpose. Two Quality Assurance screens look after patient identity. Patient Match Review is a queue of new patients whose MRN, name or date of birth only partly matched an existing patient. PathScribe never settles these by itself, because a wrong guess would show one person's history on another person's case. Patient Management lets you search for any patient and merge, link or move a case on purpose. Intended users. Quality staff and laboratory managers who are allowed to correct patient identity. Where it fits. Both are tiles on the Operations pillar of Quality Assurance . Records reach the review queue from Accession. Every action is recorded in the Audit Log. See also Quality & Compliance. Screen Tour Field definitions Patient Match Review. Each waiting record is a card. Item What it means Name, MRN, DOB, Flagged The new record and when it was flagged. Needs Review The status of the card. Reason line Why PathScribe could not decide. From this accession The case that created the record: accession number, specimen, "referred by" the requesting provider, "accessioned by" the person and the date. It helps you judge whether two records are one person. Possible existing matches The existing patients that partly match, each with MRN and date of birth. Organisation Only for people who may work across organisations. Choose one organisation, or All organisations. Until chosen the screen says to select an organisation, and the box reads "Select an organisation…". While the queue opens it says "Loading review queue…". When empty it says nothing is pending review for the organisation. Patient Management. The search box reads "Search by name or MRN…" and finds patients once you have typed two characters. Choose Select beside a result. The patient card then shows name, MRN, date of birth, a list of Real Cases , and any links: "Same person:" followed by names, and "Family relation:" followed by names. The card also warns about the record's state: Warning Meaning This record was merged into another patient You are looking at a retired record; the surviving record is usually the right one. Flagged for review The record is waiting in the match review queue. Downtime/placeholder identity The record was created during a downtime and stands in for a real patient. If the patient has no cases the list says "No real cases under this identity." Toolbar Button What it does Confirm as new patient On a review card. Says this person is genuinely new. The window offers Confirm as new . Link Beside a possible match. Records the two as the same person under a different identity, without merging their cases. The window is Link patient records . Merge Beside a possible match. Moves every case from the new record to the existing patient. The window is Merge patient records . It cannot be undone from this screen. Merge Into… In Patient Management. Merges the selected patient into another. Link To… In Patient Management. Links the selected patient to another; choose the relationship first. Move a Case… In Patient Management. Moves one case to another patient. Greyed out when the patient has no cases. New Search Returns to the search box. Continue After choosing the target patient. Opens Confirm Patient Management Action . Export On Patient Match Review. Saves the waiting records as a spreadsheet file. Your role must allow it. Icons and status indicators Indicator Meaning Amber dot, Needs Review Waiting for a decision. Green banner after a merge Says how many cases were moved to the confirmed patient. Relationship: the same real person The two records are one person with different names (for example a maiden and married name). Relationship: a family relation Distinct real people who are related, for example a newborn and mother. Hotkeys None. Step by Step Procedures Standard workflow 1. Open Patient Match Review . If you may work in several organisations, choose one. 2. Read the reason and the From this accession details. Compare the possible matches. 3. If it is the same person as a listed match, select Merge (cases move to the match) or Link (both records stay, joined as one person). Read the window and confirm. 4. If none is the same person, select Confirm as new patient , then Confirm as new . The card leaves the queue. Alternative workflow 1. In Patient Management , search by name or MRN and select the patient. 2. Choose Merge Into… , Link To… or Move a Case… . 3. For a link, choose the relationship. For a move, answer Which case? . 4. Search for the target. The title asks Merge into which patient? , Link to which patient? or Move to which patient? . Select the person and choose Continue . 5. The window Confirm Patient Management Action states what will happen. Choose Confirm . 6. A green line reports the result. A merge says how many cases and encounters moved. Exception handling 1. When the target is in a different organisation the confirm window adds a warning, and the action is recorded in the audit log. 2. A downtime or placeholder record is retired by the restricted Map Patient tool on the Audit screen, not here. See Audit Log. Error recovery 1. A move that cannot be done shows "⚠ Move failed:" and the reason. Nothing moved. Correct the cause and try again. 2. A merge cannot be undone from this screen. If you merged in error, contact support before doing anything else. Tips and Best Practices Common mistakes Merging two people who only look alike. Use Link, or Confirm as new patient, when unsure. Using Merge for a family relation. Relatives stay separate people. Efficiency recommendations Read the accession details first; they often settle the question. Workflow recommendations Clear the queue each day so reports are never filed under a doubtful identity. Related Features Upstream workflow Accession: where a partly matching patient is entered. Downstream workflow Audit Log: the record of every merge, link and move. Troubleshooting Common user issues Problem Likely

title: QA Dashboards and Inspection
text: QA Dashboards and Inspection { top} Overview Purpose. This article covers the summary screens of Quality Assurance: the frozen to final Discordance (reconciliation) view, the Enterprise Rollup , the QA Dashboard and Inspection Mode , plus the Clinical impact and root cause fields used when a discordance is recorded. Intended users. Quality staff and laboratory managers preparing reviews and inspections; pathologists who record discordances at sign out. Where it fits. The Discordance tile is on the Operations pillar. Enterprise Rollup, QA Dashboard and Inspection Mode are pillars of their own. See Quality & Compliance for the queue itself. Screen Tour Field definitions Discordance (reconciliation). The screen says "Loading reconciliation data…" while it opens. The chart shows the monthly concordance rate; an empty month says "No reconciliations this month". The tiles are Concordance Rate, Total Reconciliations, High Severity Discordances (red when above zero), Medium Severity Discordances, Requiring Escalation and Teaching Cases. Further columns and the 25 row limit are described in Quality & Compliance. Clinical impact and root cause fields. When a pathologist records a discordance (at sign out of a case that had a frozen section, or in a review form), the same group of fields appears: Field What it means Delta Whether the final diagnosis is an upgrade, a downgrade or a minor variance compared with the first. Clinical impact Low, medium or high. A short hint below explains each level so colleagues apply the levels alike. Root cause Sampling error, interpretation error, technical artifact or Other. Brief explanation Appears only when the root cause is Other. Say in a few words what it was. Comments Free text. Do not type a patient's name. Enterprise Rollup. Figures are added up inside each jurisdiction first, then across the enterprise, so no case is ever shown across a jurisdiction boundary. The top card shows the number of jurisdictions and facilities, Case Volume , Total Work RVU , the AI assisted share and On Target TAT . The By Jurisdiction card has one line per jurisdiction with cases, facilities, RVU, AI share and on target share. A notice states how many cases could not be placed in a known facility and were left out. If the data cannot be read the screen says "Unable to load enterprise rollup data." QA Dashboard. The screen says "Loading QA Dashboard…" while it opens. The Overall card shows Total Reviews , Concordance, Discordant and Mandatory Follow Up counts. A chart plots total and discordant records per month. Three tables then group the same records: By Activity Type , By Organ System (Subspecialty) and By Reviewer . Their columns are the group name (Activity Type, Organ System or Reviewer), Total, Concordant, Discordant, Concordance and Mandatory Follow Up. With no records a table says "No real QA activity records on file yet." Inspection Mode. The screen says "Loading Inspection Mode…" while it opens. Choose the Window (12, 24 or 36 months). The Summary card shows Total Records in Window , Activity Types Represented and the date range. Below, one card per activity type shows the regulatory bases set for it, its record count, discordant count and number meeting the CAPA threshold. Select a card to expand its records: Case, Specimen, Outcome, Severity, Recorded, Reviewer and CAPA Threshold (Yes, or a dash). Meeting the CAPA threshold means the record's severity reached the level the laboratory set for that activity; it does not mean a deficiency was raised. Toolbar Button What it does Scope switcher Limits the report to an organisation or referring facility (not on Enterprise Rollup). Export On the Discordance view. Saves all reconciliations. Export by Activity Type On the QA Dashboard. Saves the By Activity Type table. Download Full Binder (CSV) On Inspection Mode. Saves every record in the window, grouped by activity type, as a spreadsheet file. Export (Enterprise Rollup) Saves the jurisdiction lines only; no case or patient data. All exports need the matching permission; the button is greyed out without it. Icons and status indicators Indicator Meaning Red count Discordance, or a CAPA threshold record, above zero. ▲ / ▼ beside an activity type Expanded or collapsed. No jurisdiction configured for this activity No regulatory basis has been set for the activity type. Hotkeys None. Step by Step Procedures Standard workflow 1. For an inspection, open Inspection Mode and choose the Window . 2. Select an activity type card to check its records. 3. Select Download Full Binder (CSV) to take the evidence with you. 4. For a regular review, open the QA Dashboard , read the Overall card, then the tables. 5. Select Export by Activity Type for the minutes. Alternative workflow 1. For groups of facilities, use Enterprise Rollup and read the By Jurisdiction lines. Exception handling 1. If a case is missing from Enterprise Rollup, its facility is not a known enterprise facility. The notice counts such cases. 2. If Inspection Mode shows no records, the window may be too short or the scope too narrow. Error recovery 1. Refresh the page if "Unable to load enterprise rollup data." appears. Tips and Best Practices Common mistakes Reading Mandatory Follow Up as completed follow up. It counts records that require follow up. Treating the CAPA threshold column as proof a deficiency exists. Efficiency recommendations Pick the widest window once, then filter by activity type. Workflow recommendations Take the QA Dashboard to each quality meeting; take the binder to inspections. Related Features Upstream workflow Report sign out: where discordances are recorded. Downstream workflow Cytology QA: the cytology reports. Troubleshooting Common user issues Problem Likely cause Dashboard is empty No QA activity recorded in the scope. A reviewer is missing They recorded nothing in the scope. Resolution steps 1. Widen the scope. 2. Refresh the page. When to contact support Contact your laboratory's PathScrib

title: Countersign, Linkage and Drift
text: Countersign, Linkage and Drift { top} Overview Purpose. Three Quality Assurance reports watch for work that is slow or has gone wrong after the fact. Countersign Turnaround measures how long attending pathologists take to countersign reports released by residents. Frozen Linkage (the intraoperative linkage report) shows intraoperative entries that have not yet been joined to a formal case. Post Final Drift lists cases whose content changed after the report was finalised, and whether PathScribe put it right. Intended users. Quality staff, laboratory managers, and pathologists who supervise residents. Where it fits. All three are tiles on the Operations pillar of Quality Assurance . Each report is read only apart from opening cases. See Quality & Compliance. Screen Tour Each report opens with the scope switcher and an Export button on the first line, then a chart, tiles and tables. The screens say "Loading countersign data…", "Loading intraoperative linkage data…" or "Loading drift correction data…" while they open. Field definitions Countersign Turnaround Item What it means Chart Average turnaround in hours by month. A month with none says "No countersigns this month". Avg Turnaround Average hours from release to countersignature. Pending Countersign Released reports still waiting for the attending. Avg Fields Changed Average number of report fields the attending changed when countersigning. With Feedback Countersigned reports where the attending left feedback. Pending table Cases waiting, with the resident, attending, release time and how long they have waited. Countersigned table Resident, Attending, Released At, Turnaround, Fields Changed and Feedback ("none" when empty). Frozen Linkage (intraoperative linkage) Item What it means Chart Average hours between an intraoperative entry being created and being merged into a case, by month. "No merges" for an empty month. Merged Entries already merged into a case. Pending Linkage Entries not yet linked to a case. Pending Over 24h Entries waiting more than 24 hours. Turns red when above zero. Pending table Entry ID , the OR, who performed it and when it was created. Select a row to open the intraoperative queue. Merged table Entry ID , the case it was merged into, Merged At , who performed it and how it was resolved. Post Final Drift Item What it means Drift Events Detected Cases where a change after finalisation was found. Auto Corrected Cases PathScribe put right by itself. Unresolved — Needs Review Cases still needing a person. Amber when above zero. Cases with unresolved drift correction Case, Status, Detail and Detected time, with an Open button. All drift events Every event, newest first: Case, Event, Detail and Timestamp. "No drift events recorded in this scope." when there are none. Toolbar Button What it does Scope switcher Limits the report to the whole enterprise, an organisation or a referring facility. Export Saves the report as a spreadsheet file. Your role must allow it. On Frozen Linkage the file holds merged and pending entries together. Open In the unresolved drift table. Opens the case. Icons and status indicators Indicator Meaning Deferred (conflict) PathScribe held back its correction because it conflicted with something else. A person must decide. Failed The automatic correction did not work. Red Pending Over 24h tile At least one entry has waited more than a day. "no audit record — merged before the resolution logging fix" In the Frozen Linkage export: an older merge with no recorded detail. Hotkeys None. Step by Step Procedures Standard workflow 1. Choose the report tile and set the scope. 2. Read the tiles. For Countersign Turnaround, look at Pending Countersign and Avg Turnaround . 3. Select a row to open the case or queue behind it. 4. Use Export to keep the figures for a meeting. Alternative workflow 1. Residents and attendings see their own figures on My Contribution. Exception handling 1. If Unresolved — Needs Review is above zero, open each case, read the detail and decide whether the report needs a correction. 2. An intraoperative entry pending over 24 hours should be linked in the Intraop Queue. Error recovery 1. If a report stays on its loading message, refresh the page. Tips and Best Practices Common mistakes Treating a high Avg Fields Changed as a fault of the attending. It shows how much the resident draft needed changing. Efficiency recommendations Rows open the related case directly; you do not need to search. Workflow recommendations Review Pending Over 24h daily; the other figures weekly. Related Features Upstream workflow Patient Match and Management: the previous screen. Downstream workflow FPPE Tracking: supervision of newly hired pathologists. Troubleshooting Common user issues Problem Likely cause Report is empty Nothing in the chosen scope. Frozen Linkage ignores the scope for pending entries Pending entries are not tied to a case yet, so all pending entries show. Resolution steps 1. Set the scope to the whole enterprise. 2. Refresh the page. When to contact support Contact your laboratory's PathScribe support when an entry stays pending after the case exists. Have the Entry ID ready.

title: Registry Exceptions
text: Registry Exceptions { top} Overview Purpose. Registry Exceptions lists every cancer registry or screening programme submission that needs a person. A submission lands here when it was held and never sent, could not be delivered, was rejected by the registry, has had no answer for 72 hours, was answered twice with different results, or was changed by the registry after it had accepted it. For each one you see what went wrong in the registry's own words, can open the case, correct the patient's identifiers, and then re validate and resend. Intended users. Laboratory managers, laboratory directors, quality reviewers and administrators who are responsible for registry reporting. Everyone who can open the screen can read and open cases; resending and marking a revision reviewed need their own permissions (see "Who may do what"). Where it fits. Cancer and screening results are sent to registries automatically after sign out. Most go without anyone touching them. This screen shows only the ones that did not. A live count appears as a badge on the warning triangle in the top bar for anyone who can open the screen. The same messages also appear, with less detail, in the Outbound Queue. A screen to the side of the sign out workflow, it lets you correct the data and send again without redoing the case. note "Only your own organisation's cases" The list shows only the cases of the organisation you are signed in to. The count in the top bar follows the same rule. note "Demonstration build" In the demonstration build submissions are held in the browser and nothing reaches a real registry. Acknowledgements and rejections you see come from demonstration data or from the test sender, and resending produces a new demonstration entry. Screen Tour At the top are the title, a description, and three header controls: a Transmission audit for choice, Download transmission audit and Refresh . Below are the filter tabs, then the table. Field definitions Filter tabs. Each tab carries a count. All shows everything; the others show one kind of exception. Tab (and the status shown in the row) What it means Rejected outright ( Rejected outright ) The registry refused it and a resubmission as it stands will not be accepted. Rejected, fixable ( Rejected, fixable ) The registry refused it because of data you can correct. Conflicting answers ( Conflicting answers ) The registry accepted it, then a different answer came back. Revised after acceptance ( Revised after acceptance ) The registry changed data it had already accepted. A deficiency is raised in Quality Assurance automatically. It stays on the list until someone marks it reviewed. Not delivered ( Not delivered ) The interface engine could not be reached and retries have stopped. No answer ( No answer in 72 h ) Sent, and the registry has not answered for 72 hours. Attestation required ( Held: attestation required ) Never sent because the registry is switched to its live system but the go live approval is not current. Held ( Held, not sent ) Never sent. The patient identifier, codes or eligibility were not ready, or the registry's required data is missing. Rows are ordered by kind in the order above, then newest first. Only the latest version of each result is shown: an older version replaced by a newer one is finished with. Patients excluded by their consent or not eligible are never listed, since they are never sent. Table columns Column What it means Case The accession number. Registry The registry or screening programme. When the submission has a version, a second line reads "Version N · new / correction / amendment". A TEST tag marks a send to the registry's test system. Status The kind, as above. What went wrong The first finding: a code (in a code box) and the registry's message, or PathScribe's own message for a hold. "and N more" shows when there are further findings. A no answer row reads "Sent; the registry has not answered for 72 hours." A row with nothing to say reads "No details were given." When The time of the last acknowledgement, otherwise the last attempt, otherwise when it was queued. Actions The buttons below. Details row. Details opens the row to show every finding with its severity ( Fatal , Rejected , Warning , Information ), its tier number and location where given, and Acknowledgement as received : the registry's reply as it arrived (shown in a monospace box, tagged as patient data). If no reply has arrived it says "No acknowledgement has been received for this submission." Toolbar Header Control What it does Transmission audit for Choose Screening and cancer , Screening (cytology) or Cancer registry . Download transmission audit Downloads a file listing what was sent to the registries: when, the registry's status and its response code. It holds no patient names or MRNs. The screen then says "Transmission audit downloaded: N submissions." (or, with the PathScribe server, a notice says when the file is ready; see My Exports). Refresh Reloads the list. It is greyed out while loading. Row actions Button What it does Details / Hide details Opens or closes the findings and the acknowledgement. Open case Opens the case in the right place: the Cytology Workspace for a screening submission, the report for a cancer submission. Patient details Opens "Patient identifiers and registry opt outs" for the case. Changes apply to the patient, not only this case, and are sent to the hospital's system as a demographic update. title: Billing Review
text: Billing Review { top} Overview Purpose. Shows the billing codes PathScribe suggests for a case, lets the pathologist confirm, replace or remove them, and covers the three related windows used after sign out: Smart Capture, the approval list for charges, and the billing correction window. Intended users. Pathologists review and confirm codes. Laboratory managers and quality staff approve or correct charges. Where it fits. The review sits on the Report screen (Orchestration mode) beside the report, before sign out. Charge approval and billing correction are opened from the Financials area of Quality & Compliance. Screen Tour Field definitions Field What it means AI Billing Code Review Title of the panel. Suggestions come from the stains and blocks recorded on the case. Pending review Suggestions waiting for a decision. A line reads "N codes need review before sign out". Specimens The list of specimens on the case. A line reads "No specimens on this case yet." when there are none. Each specimen can be expanded to show its blocks. Expand stains / Collapse stains The small arrow beside a block shows or hides the stains under it. Billing codes The detail for the specimen or block you select. Base code The main code for the specimen. When none is set the panel says "No base code applied yet." (the list shows "No base code"). Applied codes Codes already confirmed for the selected block. AI source The stain that produced a suggestion. When the stain is unknown the line says "stain not recorded". Replace with The area where you choose a different code when overriding a suggestion. Search codes… Opens the code search. After a code is picked the button shows the code and its description. This code is already applied here. Warning when the code you picked is already on that block. Add a code manually Adds a code that the system did not suggest. Evaluated / Reviewed for Diagnosis A tick box, one per specimen, in the Biopsy Array section. Biopsy Array — Evaluated Cores Section for a case with a biopsy array. Billing only counts a core that a pathologist confirms was evaluated on the stained slide. Ordering a stain for a core does not bill it by itself. Code search window (Search Billing Codes). It opens from Search codes… and from the block's code buttons. "Start typing to search." shows before you type. Matches are grouped; codes that fit the level you are working at are listed first, and Other codes lists the rest. If none fit the level, "No matching … codes found." names the level (block, specimen or stain). All stains ticks every stain of the block in one step and then reads Deselect all stains . Added this session lists the codes you have added since the window opened. Toolbar Button What it does Confirm All (N) Applies every pending suggestion in one step. N is how many are waiting. Override Opens a card to replace a suggested code with another one. Remove this billing code (bin icon) Removes a code that was already applied. Dismiss — no code needed for this stain (bin icon) Rejects a suggestion because the stain needs no billing code. No replacement needed — reject only Inside Override: rejects the suggestion and adds nothing in its place. Save Evaluation Saves which cores you ticked as evaluated. Reject In the Biopsy Array section: rejects the suggested code for that stain. Smart Capture Opens the Smart Capture drawer (see below). Icons and status indicators Indicator Meaning Applied A code has been confirmed. Pending review A suggestion waits for a decision. Declined — no code applied The suggestion was rejected and nothing replaced it. No codes Nothing was suggested or applied. After a decant is added, changed or removed on the Material tab, a notice says that expected charges were recalculated. If a material change could not be saved, a notice says the charges are back to the saved state. Hotkeys None. Step by Step Procedures Standard workflow 1. Open the Report screen in Orchestration mode and choose $ Billing review . The panel titled AI Billing Code Review opens. 2. Read the line that says how many codes need review. 3. Select a specimen, then expand a block with the arrow ( Expand stains ) to see its stains. 4. Check each pending suggestion and its AI source line. 5. Choose Confirm All (N) to accept all of them, or decide one at a time as described below. 6. Make sure each specimen shows a base code before you sign out. Alternative workflow 1. To replace one suggestion, open its card and choose Override . 2. Select Search codes… , pick the new code, then confirm. The original suggestion is rejected and the new code applied together. 3. To reject without a replacement, choose No replacement needed — reject only , or the bin icon ( Dismiss — no code needed for this stain ). 4. To add a code the system did not suggest, choose Add a code manually under Billing codes , then Search codes… . Exception handling 1. If a specimen has no base code, add one with Add a code manually . Sign out opens this panel when an ancillary code exists without a base code. 2. For a biopsy array, tick Evaluated / Reviewed for Diagnosis for each specimen you actually evaluated on the slide, then choose Save Evaluation . 3. To remove a code that was applied by mistake, use Remove this billing code . A removed suggested code can come back as a new suggestion, because the stain evidence has not changed. Error recovery 1. If the code search shows This code is already applied here. , pick a different code. 2. If a notice says a material change was undone, check the Material tab and repeat the change. 3. For a code that was already charged, use the billing correction window described below instead of removing it. Smart Capture (prototype) Smart Capture is a prototype that suggests charge lines for a person to check. It only appears when your laboratory has switched it on, and it carries the badge "Prototype, not compliance reviewed". In the demonstration it talks only to a simulated engine and nothing reaches a payer. 1

text: Case Team { top} Overview Purpose. A case has a team: the people who work on it, each in a role called a participation type (Attending / Primary Pathologist, Resident / Fellow, Grossing / PA, Consultant and so on). This article explains how to see and change the team, how to bring in a colleague for a second look ( Add Collaborator , Req. Intended users. Pathologists, fellows and residents who share a case; pathology assistants and technologists who appear on the team as grossing staff; MDT coordinators who follow flagged cases. Which buttons work depends on your role (see "Who can do what"). Where it fits. The team matters at the end of the case: only an active team member whose participation type can finalize is allowed to sign the case out (see Sign Out and Release). Everything here is on the Report screen's bottom action bar. note "Demonstration data" Messages and review requests are stored in PathScribe's message centre. They do not leave the system. The Consult button for an outside reviewer is demonstration or pilot only and is not real security; see External Consult. title: Report
headings: Buttons, banners and tooltips on the Report screen
text: Report { top} Overview Purpose. The Report screen is where a pathologist completes a case: reads the clinical history, gross description and intraoperative findings, answers the synoptic (structured) checklist, writes or reviews the narrative report, adds codes, and signs the case out. It also holds the actions that go with a case in progress: comments, flags, delegation, the case team, history, and corrections after sign out. A second, read only view of the same report opens from the Worklist, Search, messages and the quality queues. Intended users. Pathologists. Pathology assistants and others open the same screen for grossing and material work (see Grossing); this article covers the reporting and sign out side. Where it fits. You normally arrive from the Worklist by opening a case. When the report is signed out, the case can be flagged for tumor board (Tumor Board) and is reviewed by quality staff (Quality & Compliance). Finished cases can be found again with Search. note "Two reporting modes" Each case has a reporting mode, set when it is created. You do not choose it. Orchestration mode. PathScribe owns the report. You get a Report Draft tab where the AI drafts the narrative from your synoptic answers, and you sign the case out in PathScribe with Sign Out Case . Assist mode. Your laboratory information system (LIS) owns the official report. PathScribe helps you complete the structured (synoptic) data and sends it to the LIS. You finish with Finalize ; the official sign out happens in the LIS. There is no Report Draft tab, no Sign Out Case button and no Release as Preliminary button. A case with no mode recorded is treated as Assist mode. The sections below say which mode each item applies to. note "Demonstration data" In this version many connected services (the LIS, the printing service, the release timer, similar case matching, AI suggestions) use demonstration data or are simulated. Where this changes what you see, it is noted below. Screen Tour The screen has five zones, from top to bottom and left to right: 1. Header across the top, with the patient and case identity, status, priority and counters. 2. Specimens & Reports list on the left. 3. Main area with tabs: Report Draft (Orchestration only), Synoptic Reporting and Material . 4. Synoptic panel on the right: the checklist you answer, with AI suggestions. 5. Bottom action bar with the case level actions and the save, finalize and sign out buttons. Below the header a banner reads Some required fields are incomplete. while the active synoptic still has required fields open. Select Click to review → (or Review required fields → in the Report Draft tab) to jump to the first one. The arrow at the right of the banner shows or hides a reminder to complete every required data element (marked with an asterisk) before finalizing. Field definitions Header Field What it means Accession, Patient, MRN, Date of Birth, Sex at birth, NHS number (with a status badge), Referring Identify the case. The header can be shrunk to a single line with Compact view and restored with Full view to give the report more room. In the Report Draft tab of an Orchestration case it is compact automatically. Priority (Routine, Rush, STAT) The case priority. If your role may change it, select it and choose Change case priority . Case status The overall status of the case, for example Case: In progress . Shown separately from the AI review indicator. Releasing in / remaining A live countdown, shown after sign out while the report waits in its release hold (see "Release hold and recall" below). Stage chips Grossing, Processing, Synoptic, Finalise and Sign Out: where the case is in the workflow. AI status chip No AI suggestions yet , AI Drafted (no required field below the confidence limit) or Review Pending (a required field is below it). Selecting Review Pending opens AI Review Mode (see "AI suggestions"). Data as of (Assist mode) When the LIS last confirmed this case. Check now asks the LIS for the current state. Counter chips Signed versions, signatures recorded, recorded saves and specimen deficiencies. Each opens its own history window (see "History windows"). Also opened by Colleagues who have this case open now, and whether they are viewing or editing. Your own other window is listed too. Specimens & Reports (left list) Item What it means Specimen row Letter and description of each specimen. Icons let you edit the specimen's details and add or view a specimen comment. Gross, Micro, Synoptic entries The reports under each specimen. A coloured dot shows Not started , Partially answered or All fields answered . N unverified The number of AI suggestions on that report you have not yet confirmed or overridden. Add Synoptic Report, Add Microscopic Description Add a checklist or a microscopic narrative to a specimen. Case Comment A comment that applies to the whole case. Add Case Comment becomes Edit Case Comment once one exists. Case Hold Marks the case as on hold. A hold blocks finalizing and sign out until it is released. Retention Hold Blocks disposal of the material until released. Review (on a specimen) The AI re check suggests that the specimen's checklist template may need to change. Select it to see the proposed change. Main area Field What it means Report Draft tab Orchestration only. Three panes: a section navigator, the formatted report (read only) in the centre, and the section editor. The centre pane shows the template in use ( Chosen by the system , or pathologist override ) with a Change list. Changing the template regenerates every section. text: Microscopic and Material { top} Overview Purpose. This article covers the parts of the Report screen that surround the diagnosis: the Microscopic Description entry panel, the Material tab (the case's specimens, blocks and slides, with cassette and label printing and the grossing triage checklist), the clinical history line, the History window (prior and related cases), report images, frozen section findings, the version and change history, case and specimen comments, internal notes, and the spell checker with your personal dictionary. Intended users. Pathologists, fellows and residents write the microscopic description and read the history. Pathology assistants and histotechnologists use the Material tab to see block and slide status and to print labels. Where it fits. These are the supporting tools on the Report screen. The structured checklist is in Synoptic Reporting; signing the case is in Sign Out and Release. note "What is demonstration only" The Similar Cases list in the History window is marked "(Demonstration)" and its similarity score is a demonstration figure. Frozen section code suggestions are unconfirmed: accepting one records your decision but does not post a charge. Label printing needs a workstation with a connected label printer. Without one, the print actions are not able to produce a physical label. Screen Tour The left side of the Report screen shows the Full Patient Report (read only text of the case) and the Material tab. The panel on the right changes with what you select: the synoptic checklist, the billing review, or, when you choose a specimen's microscopic entry in the side list, the Microscopic Description panel. Field definitions Full Patient Report (left panel) Field What it means Case / Patient / MRN / DOB Identifiers for the case. A value that was never recorded shows "(not recorded)". Clinical History The history supplied with the request. Gross Description The grossing text. Intraoperative Diagnosis The frozen section diagnosis recorded for the case, when there is one (see "Frozen section and intraoperative findings"). Microscopic Findings The microscopic text. Preliminary Diagnosis, Ancillary Studies Further sections of the case. Received from LIS, read only A notice when the content came from the LIS and cannot be changed here. Hint Explains that you can type or dictate (press the microphone with this field focused), or insert the standard attestation and add detail only when clinically indicated. The text is optional when the specimen's synoptic template has its own required fields complete. It also says that saving the narrative re checks whether a different protocol fits better. + Insert "Microscopic examination performed." Puts that standard sentence into the text. Spelling A small control that sets the spelling language for this report (see "Spell check and your personal dictionary"). Editor A rich text box with the placeholder "Type the microscopic description, or press the mic with this field focused to dictate...". Fonts offered: Arial, Times New Roman, Calibri, Courier New. A light or dark appearance can be toggled. Dictating indicator "Dictating into this field..." while the microphone is feeding the box. Save Saves the text (shown as the check mark and Save). Greyed out when nothing has changed. Clear Empties the box and saves it as left blank. Shown only when there is text. Status One of: "Unsaved changes", "Saved", "Deliberately left blank" (saved with no text), or "Not started". Material tab Item What it means Specimen rows One block of rows per specimen, with its blocks and the slides cut from each. "No specimens on this case yet." when empty; "No blocks or decants recorded yet." when a specimen has nothing. Block chip The block name and status. In an Assist case, new specimens are accessioned in the LIS: the panel says "New specimens are accessioned in the LIS" and only recuts and additional blocks on an existing specimen remain. Attach images (bottom bar) Opens "Attach images to the report". Hover text: "Attach images to this report; they print after its pages". History (bottom bar) Opens the History window with prior pathology, similar cases and related patients. Codes (bottom bar) Opens the Codes window (see Synoptic Reporting). text: Sign Out and Release { top} Overview Purpose. This article covers everything that happens at the end of a case on the Report screen: the review checks, signing the case out, the short release hold that follows, recalling a report, and correcting a report after it has gone out. It also covers the quick variants, Sign Out & Next and Finalize & Next , and trainee sign out with an attending's countersign. Intended users. Pathologists and fellows, who sign out. Residents and other trainees, who release a case for an attending's countersign. Attendings, who countersign. Pathology assistants and quality staff read the same banners. Where it fits. You arrive here when the synoptic checklist and the narrative are complete (see Synoptic Reporting and Microscopic and Material). After sign out the case moves to Pending Release, then to Finalized. Quality review and tumor board listing follow (see Quality & Compliance). note "Two reporting modes" Orchestration cases are signed out in PathScribe with Sign Out Case . Assist cases are finalized in PathScribe with Finalize , and the official sign out happens in your laboratory information system (LIS). Each section below says which mode it applies to. The mode is set when the case is created; you do not choose it. note "Demonstration data" In this version the LIS, the outbound interfaces and the sign in confirmation use demonstration data or are simulated. A release that "goes out" is recorded in the case and its audit log; whether anything reaches a real outside system depends on how your laboratory has connected it. Screen Tour The sign out and release controls are on the bottom action bar , in two banners under the header, and in a small number of windows that open on demand. Field definitions Sign out window (Orchestration) Field What it means Title: Sign Out Case The window for the signing pathologist. For an attending reviewing a trainee's case the title is Countersign Case . Body text "All synoptic reports for Case (accession) have been finalized." for a normal sign out; "Released by (name) for your countersign" for a countersign. Coding Summary The billing codes applied to each specimen and block. A specimen that has ancillary codes but no base code shows a warning with Assign now . Codes suggested but not applied are listed as "suggested, not applied". A follow up specimen (resection or excision) is expected Optional tick box. When ticked, the laboratory is warned if no follow up specimen arrives within the biopsy to resection window. Feedback for (trainee) Countersign window only. Optional to countersign, required to return the case. Signature confirmation How you prove who is signing. Depending on your laboratory this is your password, your organisation's sign in page, or a second factor code. The button reads Sign Out Case with the method added, for example "(Password Required)". Review before finalising window (Assist) Field What it means Review before finalising Title of the window. A tag shows Assist mode . Preview, as transmitted to LIS The synoptic answers exactly as they will be sent. Each specimen shows how many fields are filled, for example 12/21, and its place in the sending order ("Transmits 1st"). Drag specimens to set transmission order Drag a specimen to change the order. Synoptics stay locked to their specimen. Required field incomplete, sign out blocked A count of required fields still empty on a report. Optional fields empty A count of optional fields left empty (a reminder only). Finalise now / Finalise & Next The buttons that finalize. Finalise & Next shows "next case queued". Release banners Field What it means Release countdown banner (signed out report) Shows the status and the time left. The pathologist who signed sees "releasing automatically in (time)" with Recall Report . Everyone else sees that the signing pathologist's recall window closes automatically in (time). Held report line For other held outputs (a preliminary, a correction or addendum): "(type) (what) held for the release delay until (time) (released by (name))." The person who released it sees Recall . Releasing in Countdown in the case header while a release is held. Watermark A diagonal watermark across the report while it is Pending Release. Its wording is set by your laboratory (see "The release hold"). Correction window (Request Amendment / Addendum) Field What it means Mode buttons Addendum , Minor Amendment and Major Amendment . A new window opens set to Major Amendment. Applies to The report being revised (shown as "Amending:" or "Correcting:"). Reason A required pick list. Addendum title Addendum only, for example "Addendum: Immunohistochemical Staining Results". Explanation What changed and why. Required for every kind; it is the audit trail. Clinical Notification Log Who was told and how. Required for a Major Amendment, and for a Minor Amendment when your organisation requires it. Fields: Clinician notified , Method (Verbal / Phone Call, Secure Page, Secure Email, Fax, Direct LIS Flag) and Date / time notified . Toolbar Button What it does Sign Out Case Orchestration. Runs the review checks, then opens the sign out window. Hidden while grossing is unfinished, while the case is Pending Release, after it is Finalized, and for a pool case you have not claimed. Sign Out & Next Orchestration. The same sign out, then opens the next case in your list when it completes. Finalize, Finalize & Next Assist. Runs the review checks, then opens the Review before finalising window. Release as Preliminary Orchestration, before final sign out. Sends the current preliminary findings now (held for the release delay like any output). Does not sign out or finalize. Request Amendment / Addendum Shown on a Finalized case. Greyed out when your role may not release any kind of revision. Mark follow up expected Shown after sign out when no follow up has been recorded yet. Afterwards the bar reads "Follow up expected · due (date)". Print Assist, after finalizing. Orchest

text: Synoptic Reporting { top} Overview Purpose. A synoptic report is a structured checklist: a protocol for the organ and diagnosis, made of questions with fixed answers (histologic type, grade, margins, stage and so on). This article explains how to add a protocol to a specimen, answer the fields, work through the AI's suggestions, apply codes, use the voice and keyboard commands that move around the checklist, and how the checklist relates to the narrative Report Draft in Orchestration mode. Intended users. Pathologists, fellows and residents who complete the diagnostic report. Pathology assistants see the same checklist when it is part of their grossing work. Where it fits. The synoptic panel sits on the Report screen (route , described in that article). Its answers feed the narrative draft and the sign out checks (see Sign Out and Release). Gross, microscopic and ancillary text is entered on the other tabs (see Microscopic and Material). note "Template library today" The protocol templates that ship with PathScribe are generic, PathScribe authored placeholders (organ system protocols for breast, prostate, kidney, lung, colon, skin and others, plus PathScribe's own Mohs, oral cavity and neck dissection checklists, cytology, grossing and one autopsy template). The licensed College of American Pathologists (CAP) and Royal College of Pathologists (RCPath) wording is not shipped: a site needs its own licence before those exact protocols can be loaded. The protocol list shows the source and version of each template, so check them against what your laboratory has approved. note "AI behaviour is simulated in demonstration builds" The AI suggestions described below are produced by PathScribe's demonstration AI unless your site has connected a validated model. Treat every suggestion as a draft that a pathologist must verify. Screen Tour The Report screen has up to three tabs above the work area: Report Draft (shown only in Orchestration mode), Synoptic Reporting and Material . The synoptic checklist can also appear in a panel at the right of the screen next to the narrative text. Field definitions Add Synoptic Report window (opens from Add Synoptic , or when a specimen has no protocol yet, from the template picker) Field What it means Select Specimens Tick the specimen(s) the protocol will cover. A badge shows how many are selected. A specimen that already has a report is marked Report exists . Search protocols by name, source, or organ… Narrows the list as you type. Filter chips All , Breast , Colon , Lung , Prostate . Protocol list Each template shows its source, version and category. Suggested · n% marks the protocol the AI recommends for the specimen; Applied marks one already on the case. Learn this pairing Tick it so the AI suggests this protocol for similar specimens in future cases. Don't see what you need? Request a template Sends a request for a new template. Add Report Adds the protocol to the selected specimens. The footer says "Select specimen(s) and a protocol to continue" until you have chosen both, then "Adding "name" to n specimen(s)". Template picker inside the panel (shown when the active specimen has no synoptic yet) Field What it means Synoptic Report Heading. The subtitle says no synoptic report is associated with the specimen yet and asks you to pick one. Suggested for this case Templates matching the case. All templates Every approved template. If none exist, the message is "No approved synoptic templates are available." The checklist (right synoptic panel and Synoptic Reporting tab) Field What it means Progress badge For example "3/5 req · 8/20 total": required fields answered of required total, then all fields answered of all fields. Assignment Shows who the synoptic is assigned to. When it is assigned to someone else the line reads "This synoptic is assigned to (name), they must finalise it"; when it is yours the header shows "Assigned to you". A countersign required note appears when the protocol needs a second signature. Required marker A red asterisk ( ) after the field name. Every required field must be answered before finalising. Field controls One of: single line text, long text (with spell check), number, drop down (— Select —), radio buttons, tick boxes (multiple answers), a per part grid, or the organ map for Mohs stages. Check notes A red note under a field when what you typed cannot be right, for example "Enter a whole number, 0 or more", "Enter a whole number, "cannot be determined" or "at least N"", or "(value) is more than the (limit) it can't exceed". Part grid A table with one row per part of the case and one column per measurement (for example positive nodes by part). Counts must be whole numbers; a total typed in the field must match the grid or you are asked to reconcile (see Exception handling). AI badges on a field Badge What it means AI Confirmed You (or Confirm) accepted the AI's value. Overridden You replaced the AI's value. Check source The AI offered a value that needs a closer look. Hovering says "Compare with the source text before confirming". Your laboratory's setup can instead show "AI: low confidence (n%)" with the score. Tinted field with a dashed edge in Windows high contrast mode The field holds an AI value you have not confirmed or overridden. See "AI values you have not confirmed" below. AI: not found The AI read the narrative and found no evidence for the field. Fill it in yourself. Manual, AI missed You answered a field the AI had no suggestion for. The wording says this helps train the AI. Source not found in report text The AI quoted a source that cannot be found in the Gross, Microscopic or Ancillary text. Verify the value by hand. Toolbar Button What it does Orchestrator (lightning icon) Regenerates the AI suggestions for this synoptic from the current Gross description. It never overwrites a field you have already answered.
