title: Case Search
text: Case Search { top} Overview Purpose. Case Search finds cases that are not in front of you on the Worklist: completed cases, cases from other pathologists, and cases from earlier months. You fill in as many or as few filters as you need, run the search, and open a case from the results. It can also export the results to a spreadsheet file and group them into a report. Intended users. Pathologists, pathology assistants, accessioners, laboratory managers and quality staff. You only find cases you are allowed to see; cases outside your organisation or pools you do not belong to do not appear. Where it fits. Search is opened from Home. It complements the Worklist, which shows your own pending work. A case opened from the results opens in the Report screen. Screen Tour note "Demonstration data" In this version search runs over demonstration cases. Many filters (holds, locations, intake, payer, autopsy details, result flags) match nothing in the demonstration data, so an empty result for those filters does not mean the filter is broken. The Quick Links window lists a few example links, not your laboratory's own. The screen has a filter panel on the left (it collapses to a narrow bar after you search, so the results have room) and the results on the right under a summary line. Field definitions Field What it means Which date (Accession date, Sign out date, Release date) and 7d / 30d / 90d / 1 yr / All, From, To The date range, and which date it applies to. The range starts at the last 30 days. All removes the limit; it may take longer when a laboratory has years of records. Identifier One box for an accession number, patient name, MRN or other number. A badge beside the text shows what PathScribe took it for: Accession , MRN, MPI ID, Patient Name, Requisition , Slide Barcode or All fields. A name, MRN or accession number you type searches all dates unless you chose a date range yourself. Case Type Surgical, Gyn cytology, Non gyn cytology, Autopsy. Patient Demographics Gender (Male, Female, Unknown), Age (years) minimum and maximum, and Date of Birth from and to. Status The case status, for example Awaiting Grossing, Gross Complete, In Progress, Awaiting Sign off, Awaiting Countersign, Pending Release, Needs Revision, Completed. Choose one or more. Priority Routine, Rush, STAT. Flags / Comp Flags Case flags, and flags set from laboratory system test results. Use Browse to pick from the list. Synoptic Protocol Cases that have a synoptic report from the chosen protocol. Synoptic answers Cases where a synoptic question has a given answer ("is", "is not", "contains", "is at least", "has been answered" and so on). Every answer filter must match. Use Add answer filter . Pathologist, Attending Physician The pathologist on the case (with a choice of role on the case), and the referring or attending physician. Specimen Specimen types, searched or picked from the specimen list. Diagnosis Words in the diagnosis, for example "Carcinoma". Press Enter or the add button to add each term. SNOMED CT, ICD Codes Search by clinical code. ICD systems that your laboratory has not switched on are not offered. Facility The submitting facility. A parent organisation includes the sites under it. More filters Subspecialty, Performing lab, Location, Intake, Billing type / payer, CPT codes, Revisions (amended, corrected, addended), Holds, Result flag (Abnormal, Critical, Malignant), Pending work (Stains, IHC, Molecular, Add on orders), Past TAT target, and the Autopsy filters. Summary line In words, what the results show, for example "Showing cases with status: Completed · priority: STAT". Result count For example "1 25 of 63 cases". Hints and messages inside the filters The summary line says "Set filters and press … to begin" before the first search (the button named is Search Cases ), and "Showing all cases" when a search has no filters. Hints in the empty boxes: Identifier shows "Accession , patient name, or MRN…"; Specimen shows "Search specimen dictionary…"; SNOMED CT shows "Search concept or description…"; ICD shows "Search ICD 10 code or description…". The save box shows "Name this search…". Browse windows. Each Browse button opens a window with a title, a one line subtitle and a search box. Facility: "Filter cases by submitting facility", with the box "Search by facility name…". Pathologist: "Filter by assigned pathologist". Flags: "… available flags" (the number of flags you can choose from), with the box "Search flags…". SNOMED CT: "Search across … axes: …" (the number of concept groups and their names). ICD: "Select codes across active ICD systems"; if your administrator has switched every system off it says "No ICD systems are enabled." and tells you where to turn them on. When a code search needs a system, its box reads "Search … codes or descriptions…" with the system name. A search with no answer shows "No results for …" and "Try a shorter or different search term". Computational Flags window. Subtitle "Filter by live LIS test result flags", with the box "Search by test name…". Each row is marked "Computational / LIS flag": these flags come from laboratory system test results rather than from a person. The hospital box in a user list reads "Search by hospital…". Toolbar Button What it does Search Cases Runs the search with the filters you set. It reads "Searching..." and is greyed out while a search runs. Clear Resets every filter to the start (last 30 days) and empties the results. Collapse filters / Expand filters The arrow at the edge of the panel hides or shows the filters. + Save Search Names the current filters and saves them. Saved searches appear as buttons at the top of the screen; selecting one loads its filters and runs it. The small x removes it. Cases / Report Switches between the list of cases and a report of the same search (see Alternative workflow). title: Session and Connection
text: Session and Connection { top} Overview Purpose. This page explains what happens when you stop working for a while, when you sign in on a second window, when you sign out with unsaved work, and when your connection drops. Intended users. Everyone who signs in. Where it fits. These behaviours apply on every screen. Screen Tour Field definitions Item Meaning Idle time allowed Set by your organisation (15 minutes if nothing is set). A facility can set a different time while you are on a case. Session Expiring Soon Opens 60 seconds before the end, with a countdown. Unsaved Data Opens when you sign out with unsaved case work. "Signed out — logged in elsewhere" Shown on the sign in page. Toolbar Control What it does Stay Logged In Keeps your session. Log Out Ends it now. Log Out & Discard Changes Signs out and throws away unsaved work. Return to Page Cancels the sign out. Icons and status indicators Indicator Meaning Strip: Offline (red) No connection. Strip: Reconnecting… (orange) Trying again. Strip: Reconnected, "Connection restored." (green) Back. Badge: Live, Local updates, Connecting…, Offline, Reconnecting… Whether a list updates by itself. Something went wrong on this screen. If a screen stops working because of an unexpected fault, PathScribe replaces it with this message and keeps the rest of the application running. A line says either that unsaved changes on the screen may have been lost or that they were lost; work you had already saved is safe. Try again reloads the screen; Back to the previous page takes you to the page you were on before (kept for this browser tab), and Back to Worklist shows instead when there is no earlier page. The message ends with "Reference for support: …" and a short code. Read that code to support. If a single section of a report fails, only that section shows This panel stopped working (with the same reference and Try again ) and the rest of the report stays usable. Hotkeys None are specific to this feature. Step by Step Procedures Standard workflow 1. Keep working; any click or key press restarts the idle clock. 2. If Session Expiring Soon appears, select Stay Logged In . 3. When finished, select Sign out. If Unsaved Data appears, choose Return to Page and save. Alternative workflow 1. Select Log Out in the warning if you have finished. 2. If the screen says you were logged in elsewhere, sign in again where you want to work. Exception handling 1. Offline strip. Keep the page open; PathScribe retries. Save when it shows Reconnected. 2. You were signed out while away. Sign in again; drafts kept by an idle sign out are restored. 3. Signed in on a second tab. The first tab is signed out. Error recovery 1. After an expiry, reopen the case and check the last edit. 2. After Log Out & Discard Changes , the work is gone; redo it. warning "Save before the window ends" The warning says "Please save any unsaved work now — changes are not automatically preserved." An idle sign out keeps drafts, but an explicit sign out discards them by default. warning "Do not sign out and discard a report you meant to keep" Log Out & Discard Changes cannot be undone. Tips and Best Practices Common mistakes Walking away mid report on a shared computer. Ignoring the Reconnecting strip and editing for a long time. Efficiency recommendations Save often with the save hotkey on the Report. Sign out when you leave; do not rely on the timer. Workflow recommendations Laboratory managers: ask your administrator for a time that fits your bench. Related Features Upstream workflow Sign In Downstream workflow Notifications: the other signals. Report: where unsaved work matters most. Troubleshooting Common user issues Problem Likely cause Logged out often Short idle time set by your organisation. Signed out suddenly Same account used in another tab. Badge says Local updates Live updates are not available; the list refreshes on a timer. Resolution steps 1. Check the strip under the top bar. 2. Reload the page. 3. Sign in again. When to contact support Contact your laboratory's PathScribe support when sessions end much sooner than your idle time or the connection strip stays red.

title: Sign In
text: Sign In { top} Overview Purpose. The sign in screen is where you start a PathScribe session. You sign in either with the email and password your administrator gave you, or with your organisation's single sign on (Microsoft, Google or your own organisation's sign in). This article also covers what happens during the session: the "Already signed in elsewhere" question, the inactivity warning, the question "Which bench is this?", choosing a language, and signing out. On a live installation you sign in with your organisation's single sign on only; email and password sign in is part of the demonstration version. Intended users. Everyone who works in PathScribe. Where it fits. Sign in comes first. After it you land on the page you were trying to open, or on Home if there was none. Every other screen needs you to be signed in. The few pages meant for outside people (a consult link, a critical alert reference) do not. Screen Tour The sign in card shows the PathScribe logo and the words "Clinical Pathology Reporting". Which parts below it appear depends on how your installation is set up. Field definitions Field What it means Environment badge Production, Validation, Training or Development. Shown only when your installation names its environment. Check it before you start: it tells you which system you are signing in to. Email Your work email address. The cursor starts here. Password Your password. The eye button beside it shows or hides what you typed ("Show password" / "Hide password"). Forgot password? Shows the message "Ask your administrator to reset your password from the Staff screen." You cannot reset your password yourself on this screen. or continue with A line above the single sign on buttons. Microsoft, Google, Organisation sign in Single sign on buttons. Only the ones set up for your installation appear. Soon On installations with password sign in but no single sign on, the Google and Microsoft buttons are greyed out with a Soon tag and the tooltip "Single sign on is not yet available". Notice "This system contains protected health information. Access is restricted to authorized users and activity is recorded." Version A small version number at the foot of the card, when known. Choose your own password (shown after a first sign in with a temporary password) Field What it means New password At least the stated number of characters, and different from the temporary password. Confirm new password Type it again. Hint "At least (n) characters, different from the temporary one. Common, patterned or breached passwords are refused." Second factor (when your organisation requires it on password sign in) Field What it means Set up your second factor First time: an account name and a secret key to add to an authenticator app, then the six digit code it shows. Save your recovery codes Shown once after set up. Each works once if you lose your authenticator. Second factor Later sign ins: enter the six digit code, or a recovery code. Simulated A tag on these screens: in the demonstration the authenticator is a stand in and protects nothing. With your hospital's identity provider, the provider asks for the second factor instead. Which bench is this? (a window after sign in) Field What it means Station list "— Select a station —" then the active stations. Set the real bench or scan station this computer is. Second factor step wording Six digit code or recovery code is the label of the box where you type the code from your authenticator, or one of your saved recovery codes. Show demo code (Simulated) appears only on installations that use the demonstration authenticator. Select it and the line "Demo code: …" shows the current code so you can type it. It is a stand in for training and protects nothing. When a password change fails for a reason the screen does not name, the message reads "That didn't work. Try again." Toolbar Button What it does Sign In Signs you in with the email and password. Reads "Signing in..." while it works. Microsoft / Google / Organisation sign in Sends you to that provider to sign in, then back to PathScribe. Save and sign in Saves your new password and signs you in. Verify / Turn on Checks your second factor code; Turn on finishes set up. I have saved them, continue Confirms you have kept your recovery codes. Back to sign in Leaves the second factor step. Sign In Here In the "Already signed in elsewhere" question: sign in on this tab and sign the other one out. Set station / Skip, I don't scan here In the station window. Stay Logged In / Log Out In the "Session Expiring Soon" window. Sign Out (icon at the top right) Ends your session. Language button (top right) Changes the language of PathScribe's screens. Icons and status indicators Indicator Meaning Red message under the form A sign in problem. See Error recovery. Eye icon Shows or hides the password. Finishing sign in... The page you see for a moment after single sign on, while PathScribe completes it. Hotkeys Key Action Alt+L Log Out, while signed in. F1 Opens the User Guide in a new tab, once signed in. The spoken commands "log out", "logout" and "log me out" also sign you out. On the sign in screen itself, press Enter to submit the form. Step by Step Procedures Standard workflow Sign in with email and password 1. Open PathScribe's address. If you are not signed in, the sign in screen appears. If you were trying to open a particular page, PathScribe remembers it. 2. Check the environment badge, if there is one. 3. Type your email and password. A password manager may fill them in; PathScribe reads what is in the boxes when you select Sign In. 4. Select Sign In (or press Enter). The button reads "Signing in...". 5. You go to the page you were trying to open, or to Home. 6. If the window "Which bench is this?" appears, choose your station and select Set station . Sign in with single sign on 1. Select Microsoft , Google or Organisation sign in . 2. Your browser goes to that provider. Sign in there as you normally do. 3. Y

title: Tumor Board / MDT
text: Tumor Board / MDT { top} Overview Purpose. The Tumor Board / MDT screen is the agenda for your multidisciplinary team meetings. It lists every case that has been flagged for a board, grouped by meeting, so that the team can see what is coming, who is presenting each case and which cases still need a presenter. Intended users. MDT coordinators and administrative staff who schedule the meetings, and pathologists, fellows and residents who present cases. What you can change depends on your role. Where it fits. A case is flagged for a board from the report screen (see Report). It then appears here. Before the meeting a presenter claims it, and after the meeting its status is set to Presented. Screen Tour note "Flagging happens on the report screen" You do not flag a case from this screen. Open the case, and on the report screen choose Tumor Board in the bottom action bar. This screen is for managing what has already been flagged. note "Demonstration data" In the demonstration version the agenda is held in the demonstration data set. Calendar invitations and messages described below are produced by the same demonstration set up. Field definitions The filter bar across the top has five drop down lists. Field What it means Board Limit the list to one board: Breast MDT, GI MDT, Gyn Onc or Thoracic MDM. The default is All boards . Case status Limit the list to one status: Pending Presentation, Presented, Deferred, Cancelled or Dismissed. The default is Pending Presentation . Choose All statuses to see everything. Presenter Limit the list to one presenter. The list offers active pathologists, fellows and residents. Meeting window All , Today , Next 7 days or Next 30 days . The default is All . Sort by Meeting date (soonest first; cases with no date last) or Recently updated . Each meeting is a group with a heading such as "Breast MDT" followed by the date and time. Cases with no meeting date yet are grouped under Unscheduled . Each case is a row: Row item What it means Patient name and accession number The case. If no name is available, the case identifier is shown. Board badge The board the case is listed for. Source badge Manual if a person flagged the case, or Auto flagged if a rule listed it when the report was signed out. Point at the badge to see the reason. Claimed by name Shown when a presenter has been set. Point at it to see when. Status drop down Pending Presentation, Presented, Deferred or Cancelled. Claim this case Shown only when the case has no presenter and you are allowed to present. Presenter drop down The presenter. No presenter assigned when empty. Meeting date and Meeting time When the case will be discussed. The time stays greyed out until a date is set ("Set a meeting date first"). The Presenter filter starts at "All presenters"; choose a presenter to list only the cases they present. Toolbar Button What it does Print Prints the agenda as a checklist. The filter bar and the row controls are left off the printout. Dismiss On a row. Removes a case from the agenda with a reason (see Exception handling). Open case On a row. Opens the case on its report screen. Icons and status indicators Indicator Meaning Open The meeting's case list can still have cases added or moved. Locked The meeting's case list is frozen because the meeting is close. Your laboratory sets how many hours before the meeting this happens. n cases unassigned How many cases in that meeting have no presenter yet. Unscheduled Cases flagged without a meeting date. Hotkeys None are specific to this screen. F1 (View Help) opens this page. Step by Step Procedures Standard workflow 1. Open Tumor Board / MDT from the Home Dashboard. The screen opens showing cases that are Pending Presentation, grouped by meeting. 2. Choose a Board or a Meeting window to narrow the list to the meeting you are preparing. The groups update. 3. To schedule an unscheduled case, set its Meeting date on the row, then its Meeting time . The case moves into the meeting's group. Your role must allow scheduling; if the control is greyed out, ask your manager. 4. To present a case yourself, select Claim this case . The row then shows "Claimed by" and your name. 5. To assign a colleague, choose their name in the Presenter drop down on the row. If the date is in the future and the person has an email address on file, they receive an in app message and a calendar invitation. Neither contains patient details, only the board name and the accession number. 6. Select Print if you want a paper checklist for the meeting. 7. After the meeting, change each row's status to Presented (or Deferred if it was not discussed). Your role must allow status changes. Alternative workflow 1. To flag a case yourself, open it from Search or the worklist, go to the report screen and select Tumor Board in the bottom action bar. 2. In the window Flag for Tumor Board / MDT , choose the Board . Optionally set Meeting date and Meeting time ; leave them blank if the date is not known yet. 3. Select Flag for MDT . A message confirms the case was flagged, and the case appears here as Pending Presentation with no presenter. Exception handling 1. To remove a case that should not be discussed, select Dismiss on its row. A window titled Dismiss Tumor Board flag opens. 2. Type the Reason (required) and select Dismiss flag . The case's status becomes Dismissed. Dismissing needs a clinical permission that is narrower than scheduling; if the button is greyed out, ask your manager. 3. To stop a meeting going ahead for a case without dismissing it, set its status to Cancelled or Deferred . 4. If a meeting is Locked , you cannot move cases into it or change its board, date or time. You can still claim or assign a presenter, and change a status. Error recovery 1. If a case already has an active listing, a second flag is refused with "This case is already flagged for a Tumor Board." Find the existing row here instead. 2. If you see "This board's case list is locked for its upcoming meeting — c

title: Voice and Keyboard
headings: The rules that decide which command runs
Voice button and prompts: more detail
text: Voice and Keyboard { top} Overview Purpose. Every command PathScribe can run can be run three ways: by clicking, by a keyboard shortcut, or by saying it. This article lists them all, explains the rules that decide which command runs, and shows how to cancel or confirm by voice. Intended users. Everyone. Pathologists use voice and keys most on the Report screen; accessioners and histotechnologists on their own screens. Where it fits. The same command does the same thing however you start it. A command does nothing you could not do with the mouse: if a button is greyed out because you lack the permission, the key and the phrase are refused too. note "The list below is today's list" There are 286 commands. Your laboratory's administrator can change a shortcut or a spoken phrase for the whole laboratory (Configuration Action Registry), and you can teach the system your own spoken corrections. If a key or phrase here does not work for you, look at the Action Registry screen or ask your administrator. Screen Tour Field definitions Term What it means Command One thing PathScribe can do, such as Next Case or Sign Out Case. Shortcut The key combination that runs it. Written as Alt+W (hold Alt and press W). A shortcut shown as "Alt+J, then W" means press Alt+J, release, then press W. Phrase What you say. Phrases are lower case here. You can say them in English, French, German, Dutch, Korean or Spanish; the phrases in the other five languages are in the Action Registry screen. Your screen language chooses which set is listened for. Always on A command that works on every screen (the System and Go to groups). Screen command A command that only works on one screen (for example the Report screen). Toolbar Control What it does Microphone button / voice bar Turns listening on and off. While it is on, the bar shows what it heard and what it will do. Alt+J Opens the "Go to" panel: a small list of the always on commands by their keys. Press the key shown to run one. Icons and status indicators Indicator Meaning Microphone active The system is listening. "Say it again to confirm" The command is hard to undo, so it asks you to say the same phrase again within 8 seconds. Greyed button You do not hold the permission; the key and phrase are refused as well. Confirmation timed out. A command that is hard to undo waits for you to say it again. If you do not repeat it within 8 seconds the overlay briefly shows "Not confirmed in time: …" with the command's name, and nothing runs. Say the command once more and then confirm it in time. Hotkeys Key What it does Alt+J, then a key Runs the always on command with that key, even when a screen command has taken the key. Esc, a click elsewhere, Ctrl or an unknown key cancels it; it closes by itself after 3 seconds. F1 View Help: opens the article for the screen you are on. Ctrl+Alt+J Cancel: closes the open window, stops dictation or drops a command that is waiting to be confirmed (see "Cancel by voice"). Step by Step Procedures Standard workflow 1. Turn the microphone on (button on the voice bar, or the voice bar shortcut shown in the Action Registry). 2. Say a command phrase exactly as listed below, for example "next case". The bar shows what it heard. 3. The command runs. If it is one of the hard to undo commands, nothing runs yet and the bar asks you to say it again; say the same phrase within 8 seconds and it runs. 4. To dictate, say "enter gross", "enter micro" or "enter diagnosis" on the Report screen. What you say next goes into that section until you say "cancel dictation" or move to another section. Alternative workflow 1. Use the key instead: hold the keys shown in the Shortcut column. 2. If a key does nothing on your screen, a screen command may be using it. Press Alt+J and then the key to reach the always on command. 3. Or click the button. Every command presses the same button you would click. Exception handling 1. If the system hears a phrase that matches two commands, the command for the screen you are on wins. The always on command is reached with Alt+J, then its key. 2. Two phrases are special on the Report screen: "back" and "forward" move between sections there (not between screens). Say "go back to report" to close a window. 3. If a command is refused, the voice bar says why (not available on this screen, you did not repeat the phrase, or you did not repeat it in time). Refusals are recorded in the Audit Log, without what you said. Error recovery 1. If the system heard something wrong and a command ran, use the screen's own undo or the Cancel command; nothing runs that you could not do with the mouse, and every protected action still asks its own confirmation. 2. If you started dictating by mistake, say "cancel dictation". The system asks you to say it again to discard what was dictated in this session; if you say something else, the dictation simply stops and keeps the text. 3. If the wrong phrase keeps being heard, add a learned correction in your personal settings (see Personal Settings). The rules that decide which command runs The screen in focus wins. If a screen command and an always on command use the same key or phrase, the screen command runs. The always on command is reached with Alt+J, then its key. No two commands on one screen share a key or a phrase. The product's own tests enforce this. Hard to undo voice commands ask twice. These are: Delete Row (Worklist), Delete Message, Delete All Selected, Recall a released report, Release Case From Hold and Release Autopsy Body. A key press is already a deliberate act, so keys do not ask. Commands that open their own confirmation window (Sign Out Case, Confirm Finalise, Discard Unsaved Changes, delegation) do not ask a second time by voice. Cancel by voice. Saying "cancel" closes the open window, or drops a command that is waiting to be confirmed. While you are dictating, "cancel dictation" asks you to repeat it before discarding what you dictated in this session. Everything is audited. Every voic

title: Worklist
text: Worklist { top} Overview Purpose. The Worklist lists the cases you have to work on: cases assigned to you, cases waiting in a pool for someone to claim them, and the queues that need your attention (countersign, release, revision, review, holds, follow up). Tiles across the top count each kind of work and filter the list when you select them. Selecting a case opens it. Intended users. Pathologists, pathology assistants and laboratory managers. What you see depends on your role: the peer review queues, for example, appear only to people who may open them. Where it fits. The Worklist is the usual start of the working day. Cases arrive here after accessioning and grossing. From a row you go on to the case report. To find a case that is not in your list (for example a completed case from last month), use Search. Screen Tour note "Demonstration data" In this version the cases, pools and counts come from demonstration data. Screens, buttons and rules behave as described here, but the cases you see are not real patients. The screen has four bands, from the top: 1. LIS Cases and Outreach tiles (and, for people who may use them, the two peer review queue tiles). These switch the whole screen between your laboratory's own cases and Outreach cases. 2. Branch tabs : All Cases, Surg Path, Cytology and Autopsy, each with a count. 3. Filter tiles : one per kind of work, each with a count. 4. The case table , under the page title (the title changes to name the filter you chose, for example "Urgent" or "Awaiting Countersign"). Field definitions Field What it means LIS Cases / Outreach Switches between the cases reported through your laboratory system and the cases reported through Outreach. The number is every case in that group, assigned to you plus waiting in a pool. Your choice is remembered for the rest of your session. Urgent and Pool badges On the tile you are not currently viewing, small badges tell you that the other group has urgent cases or pool cases waiting. Cytology QC Peer Review Queue, Surgical Post Sign Out QA Two peer review queues that open inside the Worklist, with the number of items waiting. They are shown only if your role may open them. All Cases, Surg Path, Cytology, Autopsy Branch tabs. They narrow the list and the tile counts to one discipline. All Cases is the default. Your choice is remembered for the rest of your session. Case The accession number of the case. Patient, DOB (Age), Sex, MRN Who the case belongs to. Cases you may not see yet show a lock and a message instead (see Exception handling). Physician The requesting physician. Specimen(s) The specimens on the case. Point at a chip to read the full description. Flag(s) Flags on the case or on its specimens. Point at a chip to see whether it is a case flag or a specimen flag and what it means. Staff The people on the case. A small RES tag marks a resident or fellow. Selecting a name starts a message to that person. Status Where the case is, for example Draft, Accessioned, Gross Complete, In Progress, Finalizing, Pending Countersign, Pending Release, Returned, Pool. A finalized case with a revision reads, for example, "Final (Amended)". When a case has several reports that are not all in the same state, the status shows how many are final, for example "1/2 Final". Digital Readiness, DP AI Triage & Biomarkers Shown for cases that have digital slides or an AI screening result. Select the badge to open the slide or triage details. Sorted by A ribbon above the table that appears when you sort. Clear All removes the sort. Slide Detail panel. It slides out from the right when you select a digital slide badge. The heading is Slide Detail , with the accession, patient and MRN under it. Case Readiness Summary shows the case's digital readiness status and, when an AI screen exists, "AI Triage:" with its result and any biomarker note. With neither it says "No digital slide data available for this case." title: Embedding Station
text: Embedding Station { top} Overview Purpose. The Embedding Station is the bench screen for the person embedding tissue in wax. You scan a cassette, check that the number of pieces in it matches the number counted at grossing, record the mold size and how the tissue is oriented, and mark the block as embedded. If something is wrong with the cassette (broken, empty, unprocessed, extra tissue) you report it with one touch. You can also reprint a cassette label that has become damaged or covered in wax, and you can link cassettes that hold one specimen's tissue split across several blocks. Intended users. Histotechnologists and pathology assistants at the embedding bench, and laboratory managers. The screen opens only for roles that have the Embedding screen switched on; by default these are the Histotechnologist and Pathology Assistant roles. Where it fits. Embedding follows grossing and tissue processing and comes before cutting. The block you confirm here is the block you cut at the Microtomy Workstation. The piece count you compare against was recorded in Grossing. A mismatch or a reported discrepancy raises a Tissue Discrepancy item in Quality for the supervisor. The embedding step is also part of the chain of custody tracked in Batch Management. Open the screen from the Pathology Workspace (the Embedding Workspace tile) or with the Go to Bench button when your station is an embedding station. Screen Tour The page is titled Embedding Station . The Back button at the top left returns to the Worklist. Before a scan the screen shows only "Scan a cassette barcode to begin" and a scan box. After a scan a grey identity bar appears, with three columns below it. note "Cassettes only" This station takes block cassettes. A cassette shared by several specimens (a matrix block), a cell block cassette, a decant or a bare specimen barcode is refused with "The Embedding station takes block cassettes only. Matrix or cell block cassettes, decants and specimen barcodes aren’t supported yet." A slide barcode opens the block it belongs to. title: Microtomy Workstation
text: Microtomy Workstation { top} Overview Purpose. The Microtomy Workstation is the bench screen for the person cutting blocks. You scan a block (or a cytology decant or fluid container), see every slide that has been ordered from it, add stains and levels, and print or etch the slide labels, either one slide at a time as you cut or as a batch. It also lets you write comments for the block or a slide, flag a block that has run out of tissue, and read what each slide will be billed. Intended users. Histotechnologists at the microtome, and laboratory managers who oversee the bench. The screen opens only for roles that have the Microtomy screen switched on; by default that is the Histotechnologist role. If the tile is missing from the Pathology Workspace, ask your laboratory manager. Where it fits. Embedding comes first: the block was embedded at the Embedding Station. Slides are ordered from the report screen, from Add On Orders, or here. After cutting and staining, finished slides move on to the Slide Distribution Station. The microtomy bench is also one of the processing steps tracked in Batch Management. You reach this screen from the Pathology Workspace (the Microtomy Workspace tile) or with the Go to Bench button in the top bar when your station is a microtomy station. note "Printers and labels today" Slide labels go to the label printer set up for your scan station. In a demonstration setup the printing is simulated, and the Label Preview is always a drawing of the label (a pattern standing in for the barcode), not the barcode itself. Check the first real labels on your laboratory's own printer. Screen Tour The page is titled Microtomy Workstation . A Back button at the top left returns to the Worklist (not to the Pathology Workspace). Before anything is scanned, the screen shows only the prompt "Scan a block or decant/fluid container barcode to begin" and a scan box. Once a block or decant is open, a grey bar shows its identity and the screen splits into three columns. note "Your station" The top bar carries a small station indicator (a pin and a station name). The label printer used here is the one linked to that station. If it says "No station", click it and choose your bench. Station setup is an administrator task; see the Administrator Guide. Field definitions Identity bar (after a scan) Field What it means Accession The case number. Patient Patient name, as recorded on the case. DOB Date of birth, in your language's date format. Specimen/Block The specimen letter and block (or decant) label, for example A1. Type The specimen description. Scan next block/decant → Closes this work item and returns to the scan box. Nothing is lost: each change is saved as you make it. Left column Field What it means Tiny Tissue, Fragile, Decal Required Three alert badges on the block. A bright badge is on, a dim one is off. Select one to switch it. They show on the embedding screen too. Blocks only, not decants. Block exhausted Opens a window to tell the ordering pathologist the block has no tissue left. Greyed out unless your role has the permission to flag a block exception (Histotechnologists have it by default). After you flag, a line beside the button says where the notice went. See Exception handling. Cores in this matrix block For a matrix block (several specimens in one block): each position and the specimen in it. Status, Piece count, Tissue The block's current status, the piece count recorded at grossing, and its tissue description. Block comments Opens the comment window for the block. The number in brackets is how many comments exist. Prior Slide History Each slide already printed on this block, newest first, with its print time. Reads "No slides printed yet for this block." when there are none. Billing Read only. One row per slide with its billing codes and state (Applied, Declined, No billing code, Pending review) and, where a charge exists, its progress (Awaiting billing approval, Approved, Charged, Exported, On hold, Rejected by billing). Warnings appear above the rows, for example that charges are waiting for billing approval, or that a matrix block slide is billed once the pathologist confirms which cores were evaluated. $ Full billing review Opens the full billing panel for the case. It is greyed out unless you have the billing review permission. Center column: Slide Grid Column or control What it means Level The slide's level on this block, shown as L1, L2 and so on, with the cut depth in micrometres when one was given, for example "L2 (4µm)". A level number is never reused, even when a slide is removed. Stain The stain name. A Control badge marks a control slide paired with a patient slide. An On Label badge means a comment on that slide will print on the label. Print Status Pending, Printing…, Printed, Failed or Canceled. A failed slide shows the printer's message under the badge. "Reprinted 2×" shows how often a slide has been reprinted. Actions Print, Reprint, + Level, the comment button (speech bubble with a count), Remove. See the Toolbar table. Checkbox column Appears only in Batch print mode. Used to choose slides to print together. Printed and canceled slides cannot be ticked. Add a stain (under the grid) Field What it means Category tabs Special Stains, IHC, Cytology, Molecular, Other. They filter the list. Search stains… Narrows the list by name. title: Slide Distribution Station
text: Slide Distribution Station { top} Overview Purpose. The Slide Distribution Station is where finished, stained slides leave the laboratory bench. You scan slides one after another and send each either to a pathologist (a physical checkout, with the folder, tray or courier bag recorded) or to a digital slide scanner (with the scanner, rack and slot recorded). The screen keeps a running queue of what you have scanned, warns when slides from one block are going to different places, lets you flag a slide that has a problem, and keeps a chain of custody history for every slide. Intended users. Histotechnologists who distribute slides, and laboratory managers. The screen opens only for roles that have the Slide Distribution screen switched on; by default that is the Histotechnologist role. Where it fits. Slides arrive here after cutting at the Microtomy Workstation and staining. A checked out slide goes to the pathologist's desk; a slide routed to a scanner appears in the scanning queue in Batch Management (see WSI Scan), where it is loaded onto the scanner and scanned. Slides ordered through Add On Orders show their progress as "Checked Out / Scanned" once they are checked out or loaded on a scanner here. Open the screen from the Pathology Workspace (the Slide Distribution Workspace tile) or with the Go to Bench button when your station is a distribution station. note "What the queue is" The queue lives on the screen while you work. Each routing you confirm is saved on the slide at once, but the list of scanned slides itself is not kept: if you leave the page or reload it, the queue starts empty again. The slides keep their routing and their history. Screen Tour The page is titled Slide Distribution Station . Back at the top left returns to the Worklist. Unlike the other two stations, the scan box is always on screen, with the prompt "Scan a slide or block/cassette barcode — the queue grows continuously". Field definitions Top bar Field What it means Slides in Queue How many slides are in the queue now. Destination Mode Physical Checkout or Digital Scanner: the side of the destination panel you are on. Carrier / Scanner For the slide you are working on: its courier bag, tray, folder or scanner, whichever is recorded. A dash if none. Tech Your name. It is written on every chain of custody line you create. Left: Work Queue Field What it means Row heading The accession, specimen and block, and a priority badge (STAT, Rush or Routine) from the case. ✕ Takes the slide out of the queue. It does not undo any routing already saved. Second line The stain and the routing status, or "Not yet routed". Third line Where it is going: the pathologist's name, "Subspecialty pool", the scanner, or "Unassigned". Center Field What it means Batch Progress One small square for each queued slide, labelled with its block. Colours show physical, digital or exception. Hold the pointer over a square to read the slide and stain. Select a square to make that slide the active one. Unresolved Scans The last five scans that did not match anything, with the reason and time. Active Slide The slide you are working on: its name, stain and routing status. Split destination warning Appears when slides from the same block are going to different places (see below). Scan Exception Log A Note box and three reason buttons (Unreadable Barcode, Unassigned Accession, Missing Glass). Trigger Replacement Label Prints a new label for the active slide. Chain of Custody Every step recorded for the slide, newest first, with the time. Right: Destination & Assignment Field What it means Physical Checkout / Digital Scanner Chooses the kind of routing. Pathologist or pool A search box and buttons for pathologists ("Dr. Name") and subspecialty pools. Choosing one clears the other. Selecting the same button again clears it. Slide Folder ID, Tray Number, Courier Transit Bag Where the physical slide is going. Scanner Instrument A slide scanner from the laboratory's equipment list. Rack ID, Slot Position Where the slide sits in the scanner (examples shown: Rack 102, Slot 14). When you select a slide that has not been routed, the physical side is filled in with the case's assigned pathologist and subspecialty pool, if the case has them. Your laboratory can require some of these fields, shown by a red star; a line beginning "Still required" names anything missing, and the confirm button stays grey. By default the folder, tray, courier bag, rack and slot are optional, but a checkout always needs at least one of a pathologist, a pool or a location ("a pathologist, pool or location"). Routing status shown for a slide Status Meaning Assigned A pathologist or pool is set but no physical location has been recorded. Checked out A folder, tray or courier bag has been recorded. In scanning queue A scanner is chosen, but no rack and slot yet. Loaded on scanner Scanner, rack and slot are all recorded. Scanned The slide's scan batch was unloaded after a good scan. Shown in the Work Queue until the first scan. The queue is not kept when you leave the page. Search pathologists or pools… Hint in the recipient search for a physical checkout. Type part of a name to narrow the buttons. e.g. Rack 102 Hint in Rack ID for a scanner routing. e.g. Slot 14 Hint in Slot Position for a scanner routing. Confirm Physical Routing Saves the checkout for the active slide. Confirm Scanner Routing Saves the scanner routing for the active slide. title: WSI Viewer
text: WSI Viewer { top} Overview Purpose. The WSI Viewer page is a stand in for the window in which a laboratory's whole slide image viewer would show a digital slide. It reads the case it is given and shows the accession, the patient and the specimen, and a grey box where the slide image would be. It is a demonstration page . It does not show a slide image, and it cannot zoom or pan. Intended users. People demonstrating, testing or training on PathScribe. A pathologist or cytotechnologist who wants to open a real digital slide does not use this page; they use the Launch in Viewer button, which opens the laboratory's own viewer (see Alternative workflow). Where it fits. Digital slides start at the Slide Distribution Station, pass through WSI Scan in Batch Management, and are then read in a viewer. The viewer is a separate product that the laboratory connects through the Administrator Guide's vendor settings. PathScribe does not store or draw slide images itself. warning "A demonstration page, not a viewer" The page carries its own notice at the top: "Mock WSI viewer — no real image server exists in this environment. This is a real, honest placeholder for where a real digital pathology viewer would render this specimen's own real slide." Never use it to review a slide for a diagnosis. In a production installation the page is not present at all. Screen Tour The page has no menu, toolbar or buttons. From the top it shows: 1. A notice bar, with the text quoted above. 2. A case line: the accession number in bold, then "— Specimen A" (the label of the case's first specimen), then the patient name. 3. A large box reading "[ Real WSI slide surface — pan/zoom would render here ]". This is a placeholder. Nothing can be done in it. The page learns which case to show from the web address it is opened with (a case identifier added to the end). Nothing in the application's menus opens it that way today, so you reach it only by being given the address. Without a case it shows "No case specified."; with a case that cannot be found it shows "No case found for '…'." Field definitions Field What it means Notice bar States that this is a demonstration. Always shown. Accession The case's accession number. Specimen The first specimen on the case. Other specimens are not shown, even when the case has several. Patient name Shown last name first, then first name, as recorded on the case. Slide surface A placeholder box. No image is loaded. Toolbar None. The page has no buttons. Icons and status indicators Indicator Meaning Notice bar at the top The page is a demonstration. "No case specified." The address has no case. "No case found for '…'." The case named in the address does not exist. Loading indicator The case is being looked up. Hotkeys None. This page has no keys or spoken commands of its own. F1 opens this help article. Step by Step Procedures Standard workflow This is how to see the demonstration page, for trainers and testers only. 1. Sign in on an installation that includes the demonstration tools. If your installation is a production one, the address opens the sign in page or nothing at all; stop here. 2. Open the address that was given to you for the viewer window, with the case named in it. The notice bar appears at once. 3. Wait for the loading indicator to clear. The case line shows the accession, the first specimen and the patient name. 4. Read the placeholder box. Close the window when you are done. Alternative workflow This is how a pathologist or cytotechnologist opens a real digital slide. 1. Open the case in the report screen and select Edit in the block row. The block and stain window lists the slides on each block. 2. Look for the Launch in Viewer button beside a slide. It appears only when the slide is Coverslipped or Ready for Review, and the laboratory has at least one active viewer set up. In cytology screening, the same button appears on a case worked in whole slide image mode (see Cytology Screening Case). 3. If the laboratory set up more than one viewer, choose the viewer in the small list beside the button. 4. Select Launch in Viewer . The viewer opens in a separate window, on the slide named by the slide's identifier. PathScribe remembers where you put that window. 5. If a small warning mark appears beside the button, hold the pointer over it to read the reason. If the browser says "Popup blocked — please allow popups for this site and try again", allow pop ups for PathScribe and select the button again. Exception handling 1. The Launch in Viewer button is missing. The slide is not yet Coverslipped or Ready for Review, it has no identifier, or no viewer is active in the settings. 2. The warning mark says no launch address is configured. The viewer you chose has no address set. Ask your administrator to complete the vendor settings, or choose another viewer. 3. The address is missing its slide placeholder. The vendor's address was entered without the place where the slide identifier goes. The slide would not open on the right image, so PathScribe refuses to open it. Ask your administrator. 4. The demonstration viewer opens a sample page. One entry in the viewer list is marked as a demonstration. It opens a sample address, not your slide. Error recovery 1. If the page shows "No case specified.", the address is incomplete. Open it again from the instructions you were given. 2. If it shows "No case found for '…'.", check the accession or case identifier in the address. 3. If the window opens blank, check that pop ups are allowed and close and reopen it. 4. If the viewer opens at the wrong slide, close it, check the slide identifier on the slide list against the glass, and tell your administrator the vendor, the slide and the time.
